## Corpus measured, and one defect it exposed in merged M6a code

Landed in fork PR #131 (`docs/codex-claude-transport-anchors`, head `906a68f8`):
the verified error corpus for **Codex 0.147.0** and **Claude Code 2.1.233**, plus
a detector fix this work uncovered.

### The defect: M6a was blind on the installed build

`provider_recovery_evidence.py` anchored its only Claude terminal pattern on
`API Error: Connection closed mid-response`. That literal counts **0** in the
2.1.233 bundle — the wording is now `Connection lost mid-response`. M6a is dark,
so nothing regressed in production, but **M8 would have been built on a detector
that never fires on a current install**, and the failure mode is silence rather
than an error.

Both wordings are now recognised as the same condition under distinct pattern
ids, so the durable occurrence fingerprint stays stable across an upgrade and the
evidence records which build's text was seen. Two tests pin it; both fail when
either half of the pair is reverted.

### What M8 should take from the corpus

- **`exceeded retry limit, last status: ` (CX 1 / CL 0)** is Codex's explicit
  retries-exhausted marker, interpolating the final status. It is the single
  highest-value anchor for this issue: it states that the CLI already tried and
  gave up, which is exactly the condition a nudge is for and the one the operator
  named ("including if they might have been recoverable but they exhausted all
  retries").
- **`attempt n/max` gives a free lookahead.** `n == max` is the last banner before
  the terminal line. It does not license nudging — the turn is still live — but it
  is the one point where layer 0 can anticipate a halt rather than observe it.
- **A halt can exit 0.** Claude Code has printed `API Error: Rate limit reached`
  to stdout with exit code 0 and `"subtype":"success","is_error":true` in JSON
  mode. Any headless supervision keyed to exit status reads that run as a
  completed task. Read `is_error`, not the exit code.
- **`context_window_exceeded` is not provider-exclusive** (CX 8 / CL 13). The
  standing advice to prefer Codex's wire-code enum over prose holds for the other
  four codes but needs this one carved out, or the JSON path inherits the same
  cross-provider collision the prose path was avoiding.
- Also non-exclusive and unsafe bare: `You've hit your ` (7/13), `Not logged in`
  (3/10), `Usage limit reached` (2/1), `API error` (1/50), `ECONNRESET` (2/76).

### Drift is now measured, not asserted

Nine Claude Code patch releases (2.1.224 → 2.1.233) retired four of sixteen rows.
Nearly all of the drift was **suffix growth** rather than head rewording, so
anchoring on the distinctive head of a literal — never on end-of-string — would
have preserved every retired row but one. That is the cheapest durable habit
available to M8 and it is now stated in the doc.

Codex counts must be taken against the native vendor binary
(`@openai/codex-darwin-arm64/vendor/aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/codex`). The
Homebrew `codex` entrypoint is a Node wrapper: `strings | grep -cF` against it
returns **0 for every string**, which reads as a corpus-wide refutation rather
than a tooling error. The reproduction command is recorded in the doc.

Binary-tier, with `binary + observed` where a public paste corroborates. **None
is admitted to execute.** M6a's contract still gates execution on a targeted
local evidence gate, and no CLI was driven to force these paths, so presence in a
bundle remains unproven reachability. Challenge them when M8 is scheduled.

comments.body: Design decision recorded, to implement rather than relitigate: the acknowledgment is kept, the ceremony removed. It has real value the first time a given parked v1 track appears - informed consent that a deploy may strand that worker - and near-zero value on the twentieth redeploy of the same unchanged set. So each track is acknowledged once, ever, keyed on its own identity and the digest that makes an acknowledgment stale; a later deploy asks only about tracks that are genuinely new or genuinely changed. comments.author: human
comments.body:
Decision on the acknowledgment ledger having no revoke verb: filed, not built.

An acknowledgment row is entered by --acknowledge-retained-v1 and left when the track digest changes or the track leaves the parked set. An operator who simply changes their mind about an unchanged track has no verb, and AGENTS.md is normally unambiguous that a state with no outbound edge is half-built.

It does not apply here, because the disposition value drives nothing. Checked: the only consumers of the value anywhere in conduct/ are validation checks inside deploy_inventory.py itself - membership in DISPOSITIONS at :529, :698 and :772, and the fresh-succession-accepted/complete-five-value pairing rule. collect.py:63 PR_DISPOSITIONS is an unrelated vocabulary for pull-request dispositions. No code branches on whether a track was marked collect, abandon, or fresh-succession-accepted.

So changing your mind has no mechanical consequence to undo. The record is attestation that a human looked, and its value is evidence for a later reader rather than an instruction to the system. Building a verb to withdraw a record that performs nothing would add exactly the ceremony this issue exists to remove, and nothing currently refuses for want of it.

The one genuine case - withdrawing consent entirely so deploys hold again - is served by deleting the ledger, which the unreadable-ledger refusal already names as a supported action. If a disposition value ever becomes something the system acts on, this decision inverts and a revoke verb ships with that change.

comments.body:
## Severity correction: PR #132 closes the provenance half, not the P1 half

PR #132 (`fix/cond0478-transfer-resolves-from-row`, head `c8839048`) is open and reviewed clean. **It must not close this issue.**

When I filed this, I graded it P1 on the strength of the audit's Face A — the CAS at `task_handoff.py:1175` forcing a stale `incarnation_id`, which flips `admit_fresh_successor` from `launch` to `adopt-incarnation` and skips the `DISPOSITION_LOST` finalize and the `retire_incarnation`. That measurement stands. But the flip is driven by **`incarnation_id`**, and PR #132 does not change how `incarnation_id` is resolved — the CAS already pinned it to the row's value.

Independent review traced the consumer chain and established what the two repaired fields actually feed:

- `supervisor_worker_ops.py:427` compares only `predecessor["incarnation_id"]`.
- `retire_incarnation` at `:470-484` reads the roster's `current_incarnation`, not the occurrence stamp.
- A grep of `src/` finds **no programmatic consumer** of an occurrence's stamped `terminal_id`/`generation`. They are durable provenance exposed on read-only API and CLI surfaces, and they participate in `_open_once`'s immutable-content identity comparison.

So PR #132 closes **Faces B and C**: a permanently false durable record on the two fields cond-0441's own refusal text (`task_handoff.py:901-908`) names as roster-established. That is a genuine record-integrity defect and worth the fix, but on this repository's AGENTS.md bar it is not P1 — there is no reachable illegal control-flow transition behind it.

### What remains open, and its real severity

**Face A is untouched and is the part that carries P1 weight.** Its sequence: the recipient is rebound between delivery and transfer by ordinary lost-pane recovery; passing live evidence is *refused* by `:1175`, so the pre-rebind `incarnation_id` is the only completable value; the successor is stamped with an incarnation the roster reports `retired`; `admit_fresh_successor` then reads it and takes the adopt branch. No caller error is required — the refusal forces the stale value.

That is not fixable by resolving the stamp from the row, because the row holds the same stale id the CAS demands. Fixing it requires deciding **what the transfer should do when the roster has moved under it**, which is the design question `docs/session-lifecycle.md` already has an opinion about: "a replaced recipient is a rollback and a new handoff, never a transfer."

**Reserved to the M3-E owner.** The audit established that *loosening* `:1175` to accept live evidence is wrong — a refutation pass confirmed that path opens the successor on a pane the roster binds elsewhere. It did **not** establish that tightening it is right. The candidate shapes are: refuse the transfer and require rollback plus a fresh handoff; or admit it and finalize the retired incarnation as part of the transfer.

### Disposition

- Keep this issue **open at P1** after PR #132 merges, scoped to Face A.
- Alternatively split Face A into its own issue and close this one at P3 once #132 lands. I have not done that, because the choice affects which milestone the P1 hangs off and that is the M3-E owner's call.

### Reviewer findings, for the record

- The comment in the repair originally asserted the `admit_fresh_successor` flip as the harm. Corrected in `c8839048` to state what is measured.
- The `lineage_id` residual is **not** a follow-up: nothing reads `TaskOccurrenceModel.lineage_id`. Wiring a roster read for a field with no consumer would be the ritual guard AGENTS.md warns against. Recording this so it is not re-filed later as an obvious gap.
- `CompleteHandoffBody.terminal_id` is now a required field the complete path ignores. Left as-is; removing it is an API break.

Fix opened as PR #184 (branch fix/cond-0483-successor-args). Full suite 4991 OK.

The read now resolves and emits the locating arguments, so the `policy-snapshot-missing` refusal is answerable from supported output alone. Succession still validates every value exactly as before; emitting a value never implies accepting it.

Three defects were caught in adversarial review, and two of them made the first draft worse than not shipping:

1. The emitted `"--successor-artifact": ""` was itself an ACCEPTED value. `_successor_request` filters on `is not None`, so an empty string counted as supplied and `capture_artifact_identity` bound `artifact: null` - a successor admitted with no artifact, silently, with real provider I/O and a launch, so not free to undo. The human-facing `successor_command` was safe (its literal PATH refuses); only the machine-facing arguments block was not. Now emitted as null, and spawn refuses an empty `--successor-artifact` with a typed error naming the caller's unmade choice.

2. `successor_plan.resolve` copied only half of `derive_source`'s predicate, dropping the standing-fence clause, so a finalized source under a standing claim was told `source-finalized: exact values not derivable` - a claim the admission path does not make. A read-only sweep of all 35 parked retained tracks found 2 false-withholds, both plan=source-finalized / derive=ACCEPT. That reproduced this issue's own defect shape inside its fix: a supported read telling the operator the lawful remedy is unavailable.

3. `_artifact_candidates` offered paths succession is guaranteed to refuse. It derived candidates from git's commit view, while succession additionally requires the file to match its tracked blob on disk - so a parked worktree with uncommitted work, the normal state of an orphaned run, yielded candidates that refuse artifact-identity-mismatch with nothing marked. The read now takes succession's own verdict and offers only bindable paths.

The artifact remains the caller's choice, deliberately. It is a decision rather than a derivable fact, and the read declines to make it when several candidates are plausible.

Practical effect for the campaign: the 17 orphaned parked runs are reachable through the lawful path without reading run-directory internals per run. Whether any of them is worth resurrecting stays a campaign decision.

comments.body:
ACCEPTED REPAIR from the operator, and it is better than the one I proposed.

Rather than demoting `conduct retire`'s parked gate as the primary fix, the supervisor gets authority to investigate the stuck worker and file the round report ON ITS BEHALF, coupled to collecting it. Filed as its own issue covering the whole capability set.

Why it is better: it produces a real report from real evidence — every harness logs its conversation, so the worker's session log is investigable — rather than merely permitting a track to move without a report. The supervisor may dispatch a subagent for the log-reading so its own context is not spent on transcript summarisation.

THE FALSEHOOD PROBLEM I RAISED DOES NOT APPLY, and I was wrong to imply it would. `goal_store.py:772-773` already defines `authored_by_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (authored_by_type IN ('worker','supervisor','operator','system'))`. `'supervisor'` is already legal. `conduct/commands/report.py:148-149` merely hardcodes `authored_by_type="worker"`. So an on-behalf report is honest with zero schema change — set the author to the supervisor, and let the report's content describe the worker's state. Nothing has to be fabricated.

The safety property is that filing the report COLLECTS the worker (stops the session, closes the pane). That is what prevents doing this to a still-active worker, and what prevents the double-report pitfall where a worker whose report was filed for it later files its own. The coupling must be atomic or fail in the safe direction: a report that lands while the collect fails leaves a reported-and-live worker, which is the exact pitfall.

Spawn ownership has a durable field already: `terminals.caller_id` (fork `clients/database.py:57`, "terminal that created this one"). So "a supervisor may only collect and report-on-behalf for workers it spawned" is enforceable without new bookkeeping.

Demoting the parked gate may still be worth doing as a SECOND exit, since it costs little and a track with two exits is more robust than one with a single path. It is no longer the primary answer.

comments.author: human
comments.body:
A second defect on the same surface, found while closing a row today.

`conduct issue close --as duplicate` cannot succeed from the CLI. The parser offers it:

    --as {closed,wontfix,duplicate,resolved}

and the server refuses it:

    conduct issue close --id cond-0488 --as duplicate --resolution "..."
    -> {"detail":"duplicate status requires duplicate_of canonical key"}

`conduct issue close --help` exposes only `--id`, `--resolution` and `--as`. There is no flag that supplies `duplicate_of`, so no invocation of this CLI can satisfy the requirement. Every `--as duplicate` attempt refuses.

This is the half-built shape AGENTS.md names first: an enum member the surface offers that no caller can write. The workaround is to close as `closed` and name the canonical id in the resolution prose, which is what I did - but that loses the machine-readable duplicate link the status exists to record, so duplicates cannot be counted or followed programmatically.

Both halves are cheap:

1. Add a `--duplicate-of ISSUE_ID` flag and pass it through, refusing with a typed error when `--as duplicate` is given without it. That is the releasing half for the member already in the enum.
2. If the link is not worth carrying, delete `duplicate` from the `--as` choices so the surface stops advertising an outcome it cannot produce. AGENTS.md prefers shipping the releasing half over deleting the surface, because deletion hides the gap - so option 1 unless the duplicate link is genuinely unwanted.

Filed here rather than as its own row because it is the same command and the same class as the untyped-400 defect above, and a third near-duplicate row is exactly what this tracker does not need.

Test: assert `--as duplicate` without a canonical id refuses with a typed reason naming the missing flag, and that with the flag it succeeds and the stored record carries the link. Mutation-test by dropping the pass-through and confirming the link assertion goes red.

Root cause found and repaired on the mini. This is not a conductor adapter defect - conduct/lib/quota.py correctly passes route.quota_provider through to check-ai-quota, and the installed skill genuinely did not know the provider id.

The mini skillshare SOURCE tree had check-ai-quota overwritten by a stale copy, uncommitted:

    cd ~/.config/skillshare && git diff --stat skills/check-ai-quota/
    6 files changed, 27 insertions(+), 1200 deletions(-)
    scripts/quota.py  | 656 +------------------
    tests/test_quota.py | 362 ------------  (deleted entirely)

36 removed lines mentioned meta/muse and zero were added, so the working copy was an older revision, not new work. quota.py was 60903 bytes locally against 88925 at HEAD. HEAD equals origin/main and is correct; only the mini working tree had regressed. The live skill at ~/.claude/skills/check-ai-quota is a symlink to that source, so every consumer on the mini - including the conduct spawn quota preflight - resolved the stale file.

Repair: the overwrite is preserved in a labelled git stash on the mini (message names this issue) rather than discarded, and the tree restored to HEAD. Verified after:

    check-ai-quota --provider meta --format json          -> pressure green, no unknown-provider error
    check-ai-quota --provider meta --model muse-spark-1.2-contributor --preflight  -> exit 0

So the Muse Contributor route is selectable again from the mini. Your routing decision was correct and the refusal was environmental.

Worth noting for the campaign: this class of failure is invisible until someone routes to the affected provider, and it silently pushes work onto more expensive pools - here it forced a fallback to Opus while Claude was YELLOW/conserve. A periodic check that every provider id named by a route resolves in the installed adapter would catch it. Filing that separately.

comments.author: human
comments.body:
Diagnosed; fix in flight on branch fix/cond0495-fix-role-pr-lease.

Root cause is a contradiction spawn accepts and collect punishes.

`prlease.py` `_ROLE_GRANTS["fix"]` carries `open_pr=False` with `update_pr=True` - a fixer amends an existing PR. `spawn.py` `_PR_ACTION_BY_ROLE` defaults `fix` to `update-existing`, which agrees. But the value is taken as `args.pr_action or _PR_ACTION_BY_ROLE[route.lease_role]`, so an explicit `--pr-action create-draft` overrides the default, and NOTHING validates the override against the role grants. The lease is self-contradictory the moment it is written, and the contradiction first surfaces at collect - after the PR existed, merged and deployed.

The escape named in the refusal does not clear this gate. `ghstate.py` names `conduct collect --no-github`, and for its own refusal that is correct. `collect.py` sets `skipped_gates` including `pr-lease` only inside `if unsuccessful:`; on the successful path the else branch runs `_validate_lease`, and `--no-github` reaches only `_github_validation`. So `--no-github` cannot clear a pr-lease refusal, which is why both attempts failed.

That leaves one mechanical exit for this lane: collect it as unsuccessful - recording a run whose PR merged and deployed as a failure. AGENTS.md: never clear one by recording an outcome that did not happen; a repair path requiring a falsehood is not a repair path. That is the defect, and it is why the correct action was to preserve the lane rather than force it. Preserving it was right.

The fix is scoped to three properties: a lane whose PR merged is collectable as successful through a supported command with no field recording something untrue; a genuinely illegal publishing operation is still refused, and refused where the caller can act on it rather than after the effect; and if a contradictory lease can still be created, spawn refuses it naming both the role and the pr_action. The publishing lease itself is not being loosened - wrong base, wrong head, unassigned branch and force-push stay refused.

Open question the fix must answer explicitly rather than assume: whether `fix` + `create-draft` is legitimate at all. A fix round with no existing PR to update has to open one, and this PR merged and deployed correctly, which is evidence that it is. If no concrete bad transition can be named for `open_pr=False` on that role, the grant is over-strict and granting it is the honest repair rather than adding a special case.

Do not retire or force this lane meanwhile. Keep the task, generation, lease and PR identity preserved as they are; the supported sequence will be stated here when the fix lands.

comments.body:
THE LAUNCH TRIGGER DISSOLVES THIS ISSUE RATHER THAN REQUIRING A SECOND PRODUCER.

This issue is scoped to a cond-0485 implementation that publishes the restore
contract AT TEARDOWN. Verified that implementation never landed: on origin/main
(f0dc62ee) the only publish_contract( hit under src/ is the definition at
restore_contract.py:804, there is no production caller, and no open fork PR
carries one.

The accepted cond-0485 design publishes at BIND, not at teardown, and the
reasoning that chose it is the same reasoning that makes this issue moot.

Teardown was rejected because a dead pane, crashed harness, or host reboot never
reaches a clean park handler, so a teardown-only writer leaves precisely the
agents that need resurrection with no contract at all. The executable-fact
problem recorded here is the second consequence of that same choice: at teardown
the pane is dead and the launch facts are gone, so the contract can only record
'executable: unavailable' and _fact_refusal then refuses on the missing fact.

At the bind seam those facts are not merely still available - they were resolved
moments earlier in the same call. unmanaged_native_identity.resolve_pre_task_identity
produces native_session_id, working_directory, model, effort, executable_path,
executable_hash and executable_version, and terminal_service.py:1604-1612 writes
the identity to the roster immediately before the chosen seam at :1613. Seam B
publishes inside the caller's open transaction alongside bind_generation, where
the same facts are in hand from expected_record/reserved_request.

So there is no second producer to build and nothing to persist for later
recovery. The facts go into the contract at the moment they are known.

Two things from this issue survive and are being carried into the cond-0485
implementation rather than dropped:

1. The contract must actually CARRY the executable identity plus model, effort,
   and profile/provider-home material. Publishing at the right seam only makes
   them available; the implementation still has to record them. I will verify
   the landed contract carries a present executable fact rather than assume the
   seam guarantees it.
2. The unmanaged working_directory limitation should be stated rather than
   silent. If unmanaged launches cannot carry a durable working_directory they
   remain unresurrectable, and that belongs in the record as a named limitation.

The ordering note here is also correct and outlives this issue: once the
executable fact is present, _fact_refusal compares a digest taken at launch
against the binary on disk at resume, and these CLIs auto-update in place. That
is the cond-0481/0482 unpinning concern arriving at a new surface, and it should
be an override recording what was proven, never a precondition that refuses a
resume because the binary updated underneath a live agent.

Proposing this be closed as superseded once the cond-0485 launch-seam
implementation lands and the executable fact is verified present. Not closing it
now: the verification has not been done.

**Correction to the filing — two claims in the original body are wrong, and the scope is bigger than stated.**

Measured directly against merged main (`1f1ef9fc`) rather than the working tree I read when filing.

**1. The cited internals do not exist.** The body names `_SHORT_NAME_FOR_WIRE` and `_build_supports_operator_message` in `provider_controls`. Neither is in merged main — that file was reshaped by #135 (capability allowlists converted to overrides). I read an older checkout of the main repo. The real entry points are `controls_for(provider, version)` / `controls_block_for(...)`, backed by `_REGISTRY` at `provider_controls.py:263`. Anyone acting on this issue should ignore those two symbol names.

**2. agy is NOT the odd one out — Muse is in the same position.** The body says agy should get "the same first-class control surface the other four have". Only **three** of five have it:

```
provider          controls_for   blocks advertised
claude_code       True           compact, image, interactive_streaming, operator_message, steer_chords, stop
codex             True           compact, interactive_streaming, operator_message, steer_chords, stop
kimi_cli          True           compact, dispatch_grace_ms, image, interactive_streaming, operator_message, steer_chords, stop
muse_cli          False          None
antigravity_cli   False          None
```

`_REGISTRY` holds only `PROVIDER_CODEX`, `PROVIDER_KIMI_CLI`, `PROVIDER_CLAUDE_CODE`. Notably `muse_native_control.py` **does** exist as a module while `muse_cli` still has no registry row, so the adapter module and the registry row are separable — an antigravity adapter alone will not advertise anything.

**Scope revision:** this is "two providers lack a control-plane row", not "agy lacks one". Whoever takes it should decide whether to wire Muse and agy together, since the seam work is shared and doing one will otherwise strand the other.

**3. The argv-binder half-built finding stands, and is now sharper.** Verified on merged main:

```
SUPPORTED_NATIVE_PROVIDERS : antigravity_cli, claude_code, codex, kimi_cli, muse_cli
NATIVE_TUI_PROVIDERS       : claude_code, codex, kimi_cli, muse_cli
```

agy is the **only** provider with an argv binder that `NATIVE_TUI_PROVIDERS` cannot dispatch to. That asymmetry is exactly the AGENTS.md half-built shape and is unique to agy — unlike the control-plane gap it shares with Muse.

Also verified, unchanged from the filing: `UNMANAGED_PRE_TASK_PROVIDERS` is `antigravity_cli, claude_code, codex` — Kimi and Muse are deliberately absent, so agy's pre-task identity path is real and shared with the two that have it.

Parse cost is superlinear in MARKER DENSITY, not in bytes: 80 KiB of maximally dense emphasis measured 925 ms of raw parse against 98 ms for a 14.6 KiB fixture - 9.4x the time for 5.5x the bytes. Earlier full-scale figures from the same feature: 512 KiB of dense emphasis 62,065 ms, 512 KiB of list markers 40,056 ms, 160 KiB of dense emphasis 4,407 ms. So option 2 in this issue, lowering the byte constant, is not a fix at all - no byte number bounds parse time, and a smaller budget still has a pathological input. Only 'keep 512 KiB' and 'bound the parse rather than the size' remain live. The issue also stopped being theoretical: a test fixture sized by hand at 80 KiB consumed 73% of a 5 s budget locally and failed CI deterministically on a 2.5-3x slower runner. The repair there was to DERIVE the fixture from MAX_MARKDOWN_NODES, which is worth noting as a pattern - a test that must exercise a budget should be sized from the constant, never from a hand-picked number that silently drifts toward the limit.

**Root cause found, and the issue as filed named the symptom.** Found by the PR
9C lane, verified directly by the coordinator.

The defect is not the commits. It is that
`/Users/colin/Projects/cli-agent-orchestrator/.git/config` — the **primary
checkout's** local config — carries:

    user.name  = test
    user.email = t@example.test

Every worktree created from that checkout inherits it, which is why this recurs
across unrelated lanes and why nothing an individual lane does prevents the next
occurrence. `cao-conductor`'s local config is correct
(`REDACTED_PERSONAL_EMAIL`), which is exactly why only the fork is affected.

**Correction to the count: three merged commits, not two.**

- `2c00cc06` — "fix(cond-0386): isolate pre-push hook from Git local env vars"
- `fb113bcd` — "PR 9B: bounded communications catalog HTTP API"
- `860a4ba6` — "fix(communications-catalog): repair round 1 reviewer findings"

`2c00cc06` predates the 9B pair, so the pattern is older than this campaign and
my original framing of it as "both from this campaign's Kimi lane" was wrong.

**The fix is one line in that config**, and it is deliberately not applied here:
the primary checkout is shared with active sessions and is outside this
campaign's bounds. It needs the operator, or explicit authorization. Until it is
changed, every new worktree cut from that checkout keeps producing commits
attributed to a placeholder address, and each new instance makes the next lane
more likely to read the placeholder as an established convention — which has
already happened once.

Per-lane mitigation in the meantime, which works but does not scale: resolve the
identity in a freshly-sourced login shell pinned to the worktree
(`git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` should report `Colin Murray
<REDACTED_PERSONAL_EMAIL>`) and verify with `git log --format='%an <%ae>'`
before handing a branch back. The PR 9C lane did this and reauthored its 11
commits, proving the tree did not move (`git diff` empty against the
pre-rewrite HEAD) so its existing gate evidence still applied.

Note for whoever fixes the config: `REDACTED_PERSONAL_EMAIL` is the dominant
author on that history (37 of the last 60). The 21 commits authored
`murray.colin@utexas.edu` are GitHub web-merge commits and are not evidence of a

comments.body:
**Attempted fix, disproven by execution. Reverted; the launchers are unchanged.**

The suggested repair in this issue — add the host OAuth-refresh selectors to the
launcher's existing `unset` line — **does not work.** Recorded here so the next
reader does not spend the same effort.

## What was tried

The host session does export exactly the selectors this issue named:

    CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_HAS_HOST_AUTH_REFRESH
    CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_HAS_OAUTH_REFRESH
    CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES

All three were added to the child `unset` line in
`deepseek-claude-headless.sh` and `zai-claude-headless.sh` — the two launchers
that point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a third-party endpoint and set
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` themselves. (`claude-headless.sh` deliberately keeps the
host OAuth path, being Claude-to-Claude and subscription-billed; it was left
alone, correctly.)

Result: **identical failure.** `--effort low --posture review` with a one-line
prompt still returned exit 1 and
`401 Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****_wAA is invalid`.

Both files have been reverted to their original contents; `git status` in
`~/.config/skillshare` is clean.

## What this rules out, and what it does not

Ruled out: that the child prefers the host refresh path *because of those
environment hints*. Removing them changes nothing, so the credential is being
resolved by some route the child environment does not control — most likely a
stored credential (keychain or credentials file) taking precedence over
`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. That is a code-path question inside Claude Code, not an
environment question, and it is not fixable from the launcher by unsetting
variables.

Still holds: the token being presented is **not** the configured DeepSeek key.
That key is `sk-` plus 32 **hex** characters, and hex cannot produce `_wAA` —
uppercase and underscore are outside the alphabet. So the child is genuinely
sending a different credential to DeepSeek.

## One earlier claim is now weaker and should not be relied on

The original diagnosis rested partly on the masked value **rotating between
runs** (`****WAAA`, then `****3QAA`), which is strong evidence for a refreshed
OAuth token rather than a static key. Against that: two runs hours apart in this
session both reported `****_wAA`. The rotation observation may have been two
different tokens, or the maskings may not be comparable across runs. **Treat
rotation as unconfirmed** rather than as established, and re-observe before
building on it.

## Practical status

The route is unusable from inside a Claude Code host session and the workaround
is not known. `env -u` on the three selectors was reported as a fix earlier in
this campaign; that report should be treated as unverified, since the equivalent
change inside the launcher does not reproduce it.

Impact is bounded: Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor is green, is cheaper than DeepSeek
V4 Flash on every axis, and typically benchmarks ahead of it, so throughput is
unaffected. What is lost is **provider diversity** — a reviewer that does not
share Muse's failure domain — which matters for independent review passes and is
worth restoring when someone can look at the credential-resolution path
properly.

comments.body:
CORRECTION to the filing, and a sharper version of the hazard.

The filing said the overlay's ref copy held the correct tip. It did not, and I
acted on that before checking. Restoring the real ref from the overlay set the
branch to 691cd3a0; the true tip is d8117eef, an AMEND of that commit made about
15 minutes later. The overlay captured the pre-amend value and never saw the
amend.

That restore silently rewound fix/cond0500-donor-revision past 37 lines of
committed work in task_handoff.py and test_task_handoff_migration.py, and it
left a ref that resolves cleanly, so nothing would have reported it. Corrected
to d8117eef; both objects verified present; worktree clean and consistent.

The authoritative witness is the per-worktree HEAD reflog at
.git/worktrees/<name>/logs/HEAD, which records the ordered sequence:
  11c58f94 -> 691cd3a0  commit
  691cd3a0 -> d8117eef  commit (amend)

This makes the defect worse than filed, in a way worth recording. The overlay is
not merely a wrong destination for writes - it is a stale SHADOW of refs that
keeps being consulted as though authoritative. Recovery from this corruption has
two witnesses that DISAGREE, and the wrong one is the one sitting next to the
damage and looking purpose-built for the job. A recovery that trusts it produces
a valid-looking ref pointing at superseded work: no error, no broken object, no
signal.

So the suggested guard stands and gains a second half. Refuse the launch when a
worker would treat the operator's shared .git as its private overlay; and when
an overlay already exists, treat its refs as evidence of what the worker saw,
never as a recovery source. Reconstruct from the per-worktree reflog.

Evidence file updated with the correction:
/Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor/scratchpad/recovered/GIT-COMMON-OVERLAY-INCIDENT.md

comments.body: A worse variant of the ref-lock workaround, observed in the fork by the cond-0500 lane and worth knowing before anyone debugs a confusing worktree. **Muse's sandbox silently rewrote a worktree's git plumbing.** Unable to take a ref lock in the primary repo, it created a `.git-common/` directory and REPOINTED THE WORKTREE'S `commondir` at it, writing branch refs there while objects still went to the primary store through a symlink. The symptom is the detached-HEAD trap in a more confusing form: the primary ref sat at the previous commit while the worktree showed the new one, so a caller reading either one gets a consistent-looking but wrong answer. The lane removed `.git-common` before understanding it and broke the worktree; commit objects and refs were intact and it repaired the plumbing properly (`update-ref` with an expected-old-value, `commondir` restored to `../..`, three leftover symlinks pointing into `.git/refs` removed). Muse disclosed the whole thing when asked directly. Two lessons: verify `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` points where you expect before trusting any ref state from a sandboxed worker, and `--posture yolo` prevents the cause. Same lane also found its worker could not run the full suite (timed out around 28%) and initially classified a `$HOME` write block as 'pre-existing environmental' - which was wrong, since the lane's own baseline was green. That is the same misclassification shape as the loopback-bind case: a sandbox limitation reported as an environment fact about the repository.

THE FIX. The launcher now runs the agent in its own process, records that pid to
RUN_DIR/agent_pid, and waits on it. meta.json gains agent_pid_file. Status
decides liveness from the AGENT pid and distinguishes four cases instead of two:

  DONE      exit sentinel present
  RUNNING   agent pid alive
  STOPPED   agent pid was recorded and is now gone (a real observation)
  UNKNOWN   no agent pid was ever recorded - an agent may still be running

plus STARTING when the wrapper is up but has not recorded an agent pid yet,
which is startup and not a claim about the run.

UNKNOWN is the point of the change. The incident shape - no agent pid, wrapper
gone, no exit sentinel - previously reported 'STOPPED (process gone, no exit
code)', which reads to a caller as finished and therefore as 'this workspace is
free'. It now reports UNKNOWN and names the command that would settle it. Absent
and established-absent are different answers.

comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is a production defect, not a test defect.

conduct/commands/gc.py:_has_open_files (G6) runs 'lsof +D <worktree>' and treats ANY stderr as an error, failing closed to protect the workspace. On this machine lsof always writes to stderr, because of a mount that has nothing to do with any workspace:

    lsof: WARNING: can't stat() smbfs file system
          /Volumes/.timemachine/NAS_of_holding.local/.../home
          Output information may be incomplete.

So G6 protected EVERY workspace on this host, unconditionally. conduct gc has never been able to reap anything here. The failing test was reporting that correctly; the exemption everyone carried was a real bug being logged as noise, for the entire life of the campaign.

The lane ruled out the obvious alternative by testing it: /var versus /private/var produced identical results, so this is not the macOS symlink hazard it looks like.

Observed failure line:

    AssertionError: '/private/var/folders/.../tmpduge8v0d/wt-done' not found in []

with the workspace under protected_detail carrying guards: ['G6'] while lsof stdout was empty. Empty stdout and a protecting guard together are the signature: the guard fired on stderr alone.

SEVERITY RAISED to P2. The title of this issue is about a missing tracker record; the substance turned out to be that conduct gc is inert on this host. Left on this issue rather than filed separately because this IS the record the issue was filed to create, and a second issue would split the evidence.

FIRST FIX ATTEMPT WAS TOO BROAD AND IS BEING REWORKED. Adding -w suppresses the unrelated mount warning, but measured on this machine it also suppresses a warning that names a path INSIDE the workspace:

    lsof: WARNING: can't opendir(/private/var/folders/.../tmp.XXXX/sub): Permission denied

With -w that line disappears, stdout is empty, and G6 reports the workspace reapable - so a workspace containing a subtree lsof could not descend into would be deleted. That trades a guard that never releases for a guard that releases on an incomplete measurement, on an operation that destroys a workspace. AGENTS.md: a mechanism records only what it established, and a measurement that failed partway is not a verdict.

The rework keeps warnings on and scopes the fail-closed decision to the measurement's subject: a warning naming a path under the worktree means the subtree was not fully covered, so fail closed; a warning naming a path outside it says nothing about this workspace. The discriminator is the path the warning names, which is data, not the wording - this is scoping a refusal to its blast radius, not classifying on prose.

/Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor/scratchpad/recovered/DESIGN-cond0517.md

THE TRAP IS ANSWERED BY RE-KEYING, NOT BY DELETING EITHER GUARD.

The replacement comparison: the round is about a task occurrence, and the
reporter must be that occurrence's CURRENT EXECUTION AUTHORITY. At report time
the conductor resolves reporter terminal -> roster incarnation -> stable agent
-> that agent's open occurrence (the existing _resolve_catalog_occurrence chain,
report.py:192-296), then checks two legs: the resolved occurrence equals the
track's bound occurrence, and the fork dispatches that occurrence to THIS
terminal.

  case                    bound occ   dispatched to   reporter   verdict
  legitimate successor    occ-X       T2              T2         ACCEPT
  stale predecessor       occ-X       T2              T1         REFUSE
  unrelated terminal      occ-X       occ-Y / none    T3         REFUSE
  first report            -/occ-X     T1              T1         ACCEPT

Row 2 is why the refusal survives. The same fork that mints the occurrence moves
its current-execution-authority to the new incarnation on reincarnation - the
plan's M3-B text says the generation bind that closes the restore falsifies the
prior current-incarnation (remaining-work.md:823-831). So a stale predecessor is
PROVABLY not the authority while a successor provably is: exactly the pair the
physical comparison could not distinguish. Both occurrence-equality and
current-authority legs are needed; a dispatch-only check would pass an unrelated
terminal whose own occurrence is dispatched to itself.

THE CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY THAT MUST LAND FIRST (design section 7). The v2 admit
response must surface the minted task_occurrence_id, and the occurrence's
current-execution-authority must move on exact reincarnation. Without the
occurrence id at admit the conductor cannot bind the track at round creation,
and the only other source is a read-back keyed on an agent_id the conductor does
not know at spawn time, because the roster binding appears at launch. The
admit-response carry is the clean seam. Fork work, and it precedes conductor
step 2.

BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN report.py, and two items were not on my list:

- continue_round._prove_terminal (:134-204) and _identity_matches (:123-131) are
  the SAME physical-identity comparison on the resume/continue path. Resume needs
  the occurrence-aware proof too.
- finalization._v2_seal_report (:185-226) is a SEPARATE report identity chain
  that binds terminal_generation/obligation_generation and bypasses the W10
  record entirely. It must also learn the occurrence.
- callback_encoding's v2 field set is FIXED ('every field always present',
  :10-20, :37-54), so adding the occurrence and incarnation requires

DESIGN CORRECTION - THE ACCEPTED DESIGN'S SECOND LEG IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE
BUILT AS WRITTEN. Measured on fork main; full report at
/Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor/scratchpad/recovered/DESIGN-cond0518.md

The design (and my comment recording it) said the second leg is 'the fork
dispatches this occurrence to THIS terminal', reading dispatch from the open
occurrence. That premise is contradicted by the code.

MEASURED:
- task_occurrences.terminal_id, .generation and .incarnation_id are IMMUTABLE
  PROVENANCE, written once when the occurrence is first opened
  (services/task_handoff.py:1267-1270).
- NOTHING updates the task_occurrences row on exact reincarnation.
- So GET /sessions/{session}/agents/{agent_id}/task-occurrences keeps returning
  the open occurrence naming the PREDECESSOR terminal T1 after the successor T2
  is live.

CONSEQUENCE IF BUILT AS DESIGNED - it inverts the guard:

  legitimate successor T2   T1 != T2  ->  REFUSED   (false negative)
  stale predecessor    T1   T1 == T1  ->  ACCEPTED  (false positive)

The false positive is the corruption the two current checks exist to prevent: a
stale incarnation writing into a round it no longer owns. So the design would
have unblocked resume by admitting exactly the case it promised to keep
refusing, while presenting a truth table that says otherwise. It would have
looked like it worked.

This is why the trap in the brief demanded the stale case be shown to still
refuse, and why cond-0518 was ordered measurement-first. The measurement is what
caught it; the argument did not.

THE CORRECTION, and it is available. Execution authority DOES move on
reincarnation - on the ROSTER (stable_agents and stable_agent_incarnations), and
never on the task_occurrences record. So the second leg must read live roster
authority for the reporting terminal, not the occurrence's recorded terminal_id.

Corrected two-leg proof:
  1. occurrence equality:  track.task_occurrence_id == open occurrence id
  2. roster authority:     the reporting terminal is the stable agent's CURRENT
                           incarnation, read live from the roster

Leg 1 keeps rejecting the unrelated terminal. Leg 2 now genuinely discriminates
successor from predecessor, because the roster is the surface that actually
moves. The stale-predecessor refusal is preserved, which was the requirement.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR SCOPE:
- The occurrence's terminal_id is provenance and should be treated as such. Do
  not 'fix' it by making it mutable: it records who opened the occurrence, which
  is a real fact worth keeping, and mutating it would destroy the handoff

comments.author: codex:worker-identity-lane-a
comments.body:
Hard acceptance cases carried forward from cond-0619 strong review round 1, reproduced on exact base `132deb343969100916e98cf8ac9feef1ebb3f4a1` and unchanged at candidate `a1b559befbdb572c605f1ffd8639b0561320985c`:

1. `conduct up` currently calls `shims.cleanup_route` on `CaoResponseLost`, although that exception means the POST was fully sent and the supervisor session may have launched. A later exact-binding reconciliation can attach the live session without restoring the route, allowing ambient/wrong provider auth. Lawful flow: preserve the route while creation outcome is ambiguous; clear only after absence is proven. Illegal transition: a live gateway supervisor must not lose its declared route because its response was lost.
2. A crash after gateway registration but before durable create receipt/POST leaves the worktree-keyed route armed. A later new-create attempt with an unregistered Claude/Anthropic profile does not register or clear it, so its wrapper can consume stale DeepSeek identity. Lawful flow: retry/restart/provider change after proven no session. Illegal transition: non-gateway creation must not inherit a stale gateway route.
3. `register_route` writes its one-shot token before reading/updating `routes.json`; if the map is corrupt, rollback calls `cleanup_route`, which re-reads the corrupt map and raises before removing the token directory. Existing fake tests prove only cleanup was called, and the real-shim test fails before token creation when credentials are absent. Mutation/injected-failure proof must reach the partial-write call-site and establish no credential artifact remains.

These are pre-existing cond-0540 gateway lifecycle defects, not cond-0619 identity repairs. They must be resolved and mutation-tested in cond-0540 without inferring provider identity from filenames and without colliding with Lane D quota-provider persistence/service writes.

comments.body:
codex:worker-identity-lane-a — re-vet and contract freeze on exact merged main `03178226c03411a701bb4f193748e48ba01944d3`; existing claim is still owned by this lane. No edits started.

Vet: **REAL, with narrowed reachability after cond-0539/0541.** The 55 generated static task routes are already safe because `_typed_routes_map()` reads `providers[binding.provider].quota_key` directly. The stale public helper still takes `(harness, shim_route)` and unconditionally returns `openai` for `codex`. When Lane G declares codex@deepseek or codex@zai, a profile/attestation/override caller that reaches this helper can preflight OpenAI while the selected provider spends DeepSeek or Z.ai. The illegal transition is a trusted green quota receipt for a pool the launch does not debit; it can admit work onto a constrained/billed pool and corrupt the sealed route evidence. Current codex@openai remains lawful.

Frozen generic seam:

1. The declared operation is `(harness, ai_provider) -> quota_provider`, backed only by `registry/providers.json`: the AI-provider row must exist, must declare the harness, and its `quota_key` is returned. Unknown provider or undeclared pair refuses `configuration-schema`; there is no codex/openai default and no shim/profile-name inference.
2. Actual registry-to-Route projection must consume this operation, not a parallel direct lookup, so call-site mutation is observable.
3. Tests dynamically extend the existing registries with codex@deepseek and codex@zai compatibility and prove both projected task routes preflight the provider row's pool; codex@openai stays openai. Unknown provider, wrong harness/provider pair, and any fallback-to-openai mutation are red. The test derives the extension from registry rows rather than maintaining a known-good provider allowlist.
4. Lawful current inventory remains lazy/typed as accepted: pure task-name inventory does not force cross-registry validation; actual `resolve` performs it.
5. Lane A does not add the real Codex provider rows, bindings, gateway shim, credentials, launch flags, or tier-2 proof; those remain Lane G cond-0567/0568/0570. It does not touch `successor_policy.py`, lifecycle/state files, fork ProviderManager/database, or Lane D cond-0617 persistence/projection.

Compatibility seam to adjudicate before implementation: the old helper has live legacy profile-based callers (`apply_override`, `spawn._run_attest`, and a model-registry test). I recommend replacing its public contract with the generic pair lookup and giving those legacy callers an explicitly named compatibility adapter, rather than leaving two meanings under one function name. The adapter may only preserve currently reachable declared profile flows and must refuse—not default—when it cannot establish an AI provider. This keeps Lane G on the generic API without silently treating a future Codex provider as OpenAI.

goal-lifecycle-coordinator: DIAGNOSED. Two different root causes, not one, and my original hypothesis on this issue was WRONG — correcting it below.

main is still red three merges later (9b6987b, 0317822 both failing; last green 55d16d9) and this issue had no comments and no owner, so here is everything needed to fix it.

=== CAUSE 1 — three wheel tests: `uv` is not installed on the self-hosted runner ===

    File ".../tests/test_profile_identity.py", line 46, in _build_wheel
        raise AssertionError("uv is required for the offline wheel test")
    AssertionError: uv is required for the offline wheel test

`_build_wheel` (test_profile_identity.py:43-46) does `shutil.which("uv")` and hard-fails when absent. The runner is `/Users/admin/actions-runner/` and `grep -n "uv\b\|astral" .github/workflows/*.yml` returns NOTHING — CI never installs it.

MY EARLIER HYPOTHESIS ON THIS ISSUE WAS WRONG. I wrote that these three "likely assert against a wheel CI produces and a checkout run does not, in which case the local pass is vacuous rather than contradictory". The opposite is true: `uv` is present locally, the wheel really is built, and the local pass is a REAL pass. CI is the environment missing the capability.

Vision Q2 classifies this exactly: "Is the refusal caused by the absence of an input rather than its content? A capability gap is Tier 3." The test is correct; the environment lacks the tool.

FIX: install `uv` on the runner, or add a setup step to the workflow. Do NOT convert this to `skipUnless(shutil.which("uv"))` without a loud skip reason — a test that passes by not running is the fixture-versus-expectation failure in a different costume, and these three tests are the only thing pinning that the installed wheel composes without checkout imports.

=== CAUSE 2 — test_wait_command asserts against a LIVE cao-server, and that is a defect in both environments ===

    File ".../tests/test_wait_command.py", line 192, in test_listing_no_sources_is_an_empty_answer_not_a_refusal
    File ".../tests/test_wait_command.py", line 59, in run_cli
    AssertionError: 1 != 0 : stderr='{"ok": false, "error": {"failure_class": "cao-server-session",
      "message": "CAO GET /wait/registrations unreachable: [Errno 61] Connection refused", ...}}'

The test issues a real request to 127.0.0.1:9889. In CI nothing is listening, so it fails. It passes on the Mac mini ONLY BECAUSE COLIN'S LIVE cao-server IS RUNNING THERE.

That is the more serious of the two findings, and it is not a CI problem. This test currently certifies against whatever happens to be listening on 9889 — it would pass on this host even if the code under test were broken, provided a server answered. A local green is not evidence about this test's subject.

This campaign has hit that exact hazard twice before: a live cao-server on 9889 answering unstubbed routes made a lane's e2e evidence vacuous, and it is why every task/goal lane brief now requires port isolation and a statement of how it was achieved.

FIX: stub the server or isolate the port, so the test observes the empty-answer-not-a-refusal contract rather than the local machine's process table. If it genuinely needs a live server, it belongs in an integration tier that says so and skips with a precise reason when one is absent.

=== IMPACT AND OWNERSHIP ===

Blocks cao-conductor PRs #219, #220 and #221 from merging on a green check. Their own verification stands independently — each was differentialed against 9b6987b in an isolated worktree with a completion sentinel — but merging into a red base is refused.

Candidate commits remain d45a342, cbf059a, 46e19ac, 38d4abf (PRs #217/#218, worker-identity), though cause 1 is arguably not any commit's fault: the test was correct on a runner that had `uv`, and the runner does not.

The two causes are independently fixable and should be two changes: an infrastructure/workflow change for `uv`, and a test-isolation change for wait_command.

Writer path: conduct.commands.spawn builds the v1/v2 reserve request from the already-resolved Route.quota_provider. CaoApi sends that canonical key verbatim. Ordinary CreateTerminalBody accepts the same explicit key for non-managed callers.

Persistence path: managed_launch.launch and both v2 ACP/native launch branches forward the parsed value into terminal_service.create_terminal. terminal_service forwards assigned_quota_provider to database.create_terminal or create_terminal_v2. issues.body:
Messages delivered through CAO terminal paste paths can arrive visibly wrapped with the bracketed-paste control tokens ^[[200~ and ^[[201~. Reproduced during the self-heal campaign when the supervisor sent the cond-0021 scope amendment to persistent Fable terminal 5f0bd58f; the terminal log shows the control-token text at the delivered message boundaries. This was originally classified P4 because ordinary prose remained understandable.

Human-approved P1 promotion: the defect prevents CAO from reliably issuing interactive provider slash commands such as `/compact` plus explicit Enter. Persistent Claude/Kimi contexts therefore cannot be actively managed and may exhaust context or quota during long campaigns. The normal input endpoint force-wraps bracketed paste, while the key endpoint rejects `/`, so a client-only key loop is not credible unless literal slash delivery is actually supported. Require a separate identity-bound control-input surface that sends literal printable text/keystrokes plus explicit Enter without bracketed-paste bytes, targets the exact task-owning terminal/pane/generation, rejects wrong/stale identities, and guarantees no duplicate submission. Ordinary idle-gated `send_message` behavior must remain unchanged. Acceptance must execute `/compact` in retained Fable or a disposable Claude/Kimi fixture and prove provider recognition with no literal `^[[200~` or `^[[201~` in model input/composer, plus unit/integration coverage for printable text, slash, Enter, wrong/stale rejection, and exactly-once submission. Route this promoted P1 to persistent Fable for design review and implement it only in a small isolated worktree/PR separate from active PR-B.

Post-reboot installed reproduction on 2026-07-26 shows that bracket-free text
delivery alone does not close the interactive-command contract for retained
Codex. `conduct control-input` control id `871e85234295` targeted recovered
supervisor terminal `25c7d34e` with `/compact` plus explicit Enter and returned
HTTP success with both `text_sent=true` and `enter_sent=true`. Live pane
inspection showed `/compact` still present and unsubmitted in the Codex
composer, with context unchanged at 11%. A separately observed manual Enter
then executed compaction and reset the same native session to 100% context. The
control record was reconciled completed only after that manual recovery. This
keeps cond-0026 open for Codex: acceptance must prove provider completion, not
transport acceptance, and cover the text-versus-Enter timing/serialization
window without replaying the slash command. The recovered terminal predates
the latest generation-identity projection, so the regression test must include
both a newly admitted terminal and an exact retained/reincarnated terminal
before attributing the cause to the current server implementation.

The same failure reproduced twice on 2026-07-27 against newly admitted Codex
supervisor `c30013e7` after the merged final-gate deployment. Control ids
`cond0171-final-bounce-row1360-001` and
`cond0171-final-bounce-submit-003` each returned transport success with
`enter_sent=true`, but their text remained unsubmitted in the visible Codex
composer until a separately issued manual `tmux send-keys -t %0 Enter`.
The first manual Enter immediately began the intended guarded-bounce work.
This confirms that the outstanding defect is the Codex text/Enter submission
boundary rather than bracket-free printable-text transport, and that an HTTP
200 cannot be treated as provider completion.

The same boundary reproduced during the clean chess shakedown on retained
Codex supervisor `a2e2032f`. Root used `tmux send-keys -l` for one short
speed-first adjudication followed by one `Enter`; the full text remained
visible and unsubmitted in the Codex composer. A second standalone `Enter`
immediately started the turn. This direct operator reproduction removes the
HTTP/control journal from the causal path and further localizes the defect to
Codex's text-to-Enter timing or event boundary. The final fix still needs
provider-completion evidence rather than two blind Enter sends.

issues.body:
When conduct up runs from a pane already managed by another conductor project, prepare_session_env prefers ambient ZDOTDIR over the preserved CAO_CONDUCTOR_USER_ZDOTDIR. The child session therefore records the parent generated zdot directory as its user dotdir. Its generated .zshrc sources the parent generated .zshrc, which sees the same preserved value and can source itself recursively, hanging or destabilizing provider startup. Reproduced with two temporary project state dirs: the child user dotdir equals the parent's generated ZDOTDIR and that parent .zshrc exists. Fix must define true-user-dotdir precedence and add a nested-session integration test; current Fable spec review is the design-review path.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A / W3):** fixed per spec §4.2.
True-user-dotdir precedence: preserved `CAO_CONDUCTOR_USER_ZDOTDIR` >
non-generated ambient `ZDOTDIR` > `HOME`. Generated zdot dirs are
self-identifying (`.cao-conductor-zdot` marker installed with the assets);
resolution rejects any candidate carrying the marker or living under the
conductor state root, and the generated `.zshrc` refuses at runtime to source a
marked target (belt against pre-fix records). Regression proof: the exact
failing command above now resolves the true user dotdir, and the nested A-to-B
integration test starts a real zsh with session B's env reaching a prompt in
bounded time (the recursion reproduces as a hang without the fix).

issues.resolution: fixed (user-dotdir precedence + generated-dotdir marker; nested `conduct up` safe — proven by the mandatory nested A-to-B integration test, tests/test_session_env.py)

issues.body:
During self-heal-pr-a-implement, the supervisor sent an urgent cond-0029 P1 amendment and then the exact Fable revision-3 commit to the active Kimi K3 worker. CAO returned success for both inbox messages, but Kimi-Code left them queued in the composer (alongside the deadman nudge) while the current turn continued through commit, tests, push, and draft PR creation. The UI explicitly says Ctrl-S is required to steer immediately; without a human noticing, an urgent fix can miss the implementation/report boundary even though send_message says success. This is distinct from cond-0021 (missing event mirror) and cond-0026 (visible bracketed-paste sentinels). Fix direction: provide a conductor/supervisor urgent-steer path for active Kimi workers that deliberately sends Ctrl-S after the message, records/acknowledges the steering event, and has provider integration tests proving an in-flight amendment enters the current turn exactly once without spawning or interrupting the worker. Normal non-urgent inbox delivery should remain idle-gated.

Fresh recovery reproduction during Sol/max task `self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-post-final-fix`: after Codex emitted `task_complete` at `2026-07-21T23:54:16Z` on a hard-refusal prompt without a report/callback, the supervisor spent the task's single bounded cond-0069 continuation with unique id `prb-post-final-cond0069-refusal-recovery-1`. CAO accepted inbox message `406` at `2026-07-21T23:55:52Z`, but an exact-row read still showed `status=pending` after two minutes and the provider session remained unchanged. The terminal's empty active zsh pane made CAO classify the window non-ready even though sibling pane 2.0 still owned Codex session `019f8700-b267-7cb3-9fef-f5205d029ea7` at its prompt. Installed CAO has no terminal-identity-bound resume/reconcile endpoint: inbox delivery is gated on the cached terminal status and its tmux send path targets the window's active pane. Therefore the accepted continuation cannot wake the correct provider and must not be replayed, raw-pasted, or forced with a chord. The durable pending row proves transport was retained; this extends the P1 contract to require an identity-bound wake/reconcile path that delivers the existing message exactly once when the task-owning provider is ready, without creating a second message or targeting an unrelated active pane. Cross-reference the multi-pane status ownership evidence in cond-0071. Evidence: CAO inbox row `406`, terminal `79d5a2b8`, tmux window 2 panes 2.0/2.1, Codex session `019f8700-b267-7cb3-9fef-f5205d029ea7`, and source `services/inbox_service.py::deliver_pending`, `services/terminal_service.py::send_input`, and `clients/tmux.py::send_keys`.

Fresh installed reproduction on 2026-07-26 during task `pr07-spec-writer-k3-v1`: `conduct steer` against active native-v2 Kimi terminal `22fb591b` failed before input with CAO HTTP 422, `managed input requires a caller-retained operation_id; use managed-operations endpoint`. The task needed an urgent GitHub-auth recovery amendment, but the conductor steer client did not create or retain the managed operation required by the deployed server. No input was applied; the worker independently recovered through the configured `github-colin` SSH alias. This keeps cond-0031 open: the supported urgent-steer command and deployed managed-input API are presently incompatible for a live Kimi TUI. The fix must bind a durable operation ID and terminal/generation/native-session identity, preserve the existing at-most-once/ambiguous contract, and prove an active Kimi amendment enters exactly once. Artifact-free idle-gated `conduct control-input` remains a usable non-urgent queue path and is not a substitute for urgent steering.

Installed chess-shakedown acceptance on the paired merged build closed the
urgent path. `conduct steer` targeted active native-v2 Kimi reviewer
`a9a32f4f` with exact steer id
`root-pr09-v2-no-nested-route-probe-001`. The client retained the managed
operation, posted the text and provider-pinned `C-s` key, and returned
`path=managed-v2`, `input_posted=true`, and `key_posted=true`. The amendment
visibly entered the active turn once; the worker stopped the prohibited
diagnostic loop, finished the assigned review, and echoed the exact steer id in
its single `conduct report`. No second message, raw pane input, worker, or
replay was created.

issues.body:
Fable revision 4 (a720502, spec §15.2 step 3) specifies POST /key?key=C-s and only afterward persists key_posted=true, while claiming crash-safe exactly-once behavior. There is an unavoidable ambiguity window: if CAO accepts the key and the conductor process crashes before the journal update, the record remains input_posted=true/key_posted=false and the prescribed retry sends a second Ctrl-S. That can steer unrelated queued input or perturb the worker, violating the core no-duplicate promise. Tests that inject failure before or after the client call cannot prove away a crash between external side-effect acceptance and local persistence. Correct the design before implementation: either (a) add an idempotency key enforced durably at the CAO /key boundary, which expands into the fork lane, or (b) explicitly provide at-most-once/ambiguous-state semantics by durably recording key-attempt intent before I/O, never blindly retrying an ambiguous attempt, and using the worker ack/escalation path to resolve missing entry. Do not label option (b) exactly-once. Add the post-key/pre-journal crash case to the acceptance matrix.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A / W6, spec revision 5):**
option (b) implemented exactly as specified. `conduct steer` journals
`key_attempted_at` (atomic + fsync) BEFORE the key POST and sets
`key_posted` only on CAO's success response. A re-run with `key_attempted_at`
set and `key_posted: false` refuses to re-chord, marks
`resolution: "ambiguous"`, and prints the ack-resolution procedure; a
definitive HTTP rejection clears the attempt marker (a real retry stays
legitimate); the mandatory post-key/pre-journal crash-window test
(`tests/test_steer.py::CrashWindowTest`) proves zero further key POSTs after
a simulated crash-between-acceptance-and-journal. The "exactly-once" claim
is withdrawn in favor of honest at-most-once; fork option (a) stays a
documented revisit clause.
issues.failing_command: crash after successful POST /terminals/<id>/key?key=C-s but before setting key_posted=true
issues.resolution: fixed by design (steer journal records key-attempt intent before I/O; ambiguous crash-after-key states refuse re-chord and resolve per §15.2; exactly-once claim withdrawn)
issues.title: conduct steer journal cannot guarantee exactly-once Ctrl-S across crash-after-key

issues.body:
Fable revision-5 draft for cond-0032 correctly switches Ctrl-S to at-most-once intent-before-I/O semantics, but its ambiguity procedure treats a worker report without the steer-id acknowledgement as durable evidence that the amendment did not enter, then authorizes a fresh steer-id carrying the same amendment. Absence of an acknowledgement is not evidence of absence: the worker may have received and applied the amendment but omitted the required echo. Re-steering the same text can therefore duplicate or conflict with work while the spec claims amendment text is delivered at most once. Correct the design before revision 5 commits: an acknowledgement proves entry; a missing acknowledgement leaves the outcome ambiguous. The supervisor must validate the report/branch against the amendment and either accept it or dispatch a targeted fix for a demonstrated implementation gap. It must never blindly re-steer the original amendment based only on a missing ack. Add tests for received-but-ack-omitted and report-without-ack cases.

The installed `conduct steer` contract now states the required rule at the
operator boundary: an echoed steer id proves entry, a missing echo proves
nothing, and ambiguity must be resolved without blind re-steer. Live steer
`root-pr09-v2-no-nested-route-probe-001` exercised the positive branch: the
worker applied the amendment and echoed the exact id in its final report. The
supervisor received one callback and no replay was attempted.

issues.body:
The revision-5 W6 design and current implementation persist input_posted only after CaoClient.send_input returns. If CAO accepts the direct input and the process dies before that success write, the record still looks retryable; re-running the same steer-id injects the original amendment text a second time. This violates the stated guarantee that amendment text is delivered at most once and the mandatory test claim of at most one input in every interleaving. Fix the design and implementation with honest input-attempt intent-before-I/O semantics and ambiguity resolution analogous to the chord path, or a truly durable idempotency boundary. Add a post-input/pre-journal crash test proving that the same steer-id never repeats the input. This is P1 and should be sent to the retained Fable spec writer.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A / W6, spec rev 5 + cond-0034 amendment):** the steer record gained `input_attempted_at`, journaled and fsynced BEFORE the input POST; `input_posted` is set only on CAO's success response. An attempted-but-unconfirmed input is AMBIGUOUS: the same-steer rerun refuses to replay the amendment AND refuses to chord past unknown delivery, marks `resolution: "ambiguous"`, and enters the cond-0033 resolution procedure. Named proof: `tests/test_steer.py::CrashWindowTest::test_post_input_pre_journal_crash` — after a simulated crash between CAO's acceptance and the confirmation write, the rerun sends zero input and zero key POSTs.
issues.failing_command: crash after POST /terminals/<id>/input succeeds but before input_posted=true is durably written; then rerun conduct steer with the same steer-id
issues.resolution: fixed by design (input POST gets the same intent-before-I/O journal as the chord; input-attempted-but-unconfirmed is ambiguous — never replayed, never chorded past — and resolves via the cond-0033 procedure)
issues.title: cond-0034 — steer input acceptance has an unjournaled crash window

issues.body:
The current W6 implementation catches CaoApiError after /input and /key and clears input_attempted_at or key_attempted_at whenever status_code is non-null. That includes HTTP 500. In installed CAO, terminal_service.send_input and send_special_key perform the tmux side effect before later provider bookkeeping, last-active updates, and optional hooks; a failure after send_keys is mapped to HTTP 500. Clearing intent after such a response makes a same-steer retry duplicate the amendment text or chord. Preserve explicit ambiguity for transport failures and any response class that can occur after the side effect. Only errors proven by endpoint ordering to reject before I/O may clear the attempt marker, and tests must inject post-side-effect HTTP 500 for both input and key then prove reruns send zero additional POSTs. This is P1 and should be routed to retained Fable.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A / W6, spec cond-0035 amendment):** `steer._PRE_SIDE_EFFECT_STATUS` allows clearing only for code-cited pre-side-effect classes — /key 400 (TMUX_KEY_PATTERN validation precedes send_special_key, api/main.py) and 404 (metadata lookup precedes send_keys, terminal_service.py); /input 404 (same ordering) and 409 (TerminalInputBlockedError guards precede send_keys). Every other class — 5xx, unlisted statuses, transport/no-response — retains the attempted-but-unconfirmed marker and goes ambiguous. The allowlist carries a re-verify-on-fork-upgrade warning. Named proof: `tests/test_steer.py::Cond0035ErrorClassificationTest` — injected post-side-effect HTTP 500 on /input and /key retains the marker and same-steer reruns issue zero additional POSTs; the proven-404 clears and permits a clean retry; an unlisted 4xx retains.
issues.failing_command: make CAO apply tmux input/key side effect, then raise during post-send bookkeeping so endpoint returns HTTP 500; rerun conduct steer with same steer-id
issues.resolution: fixed by design (attempt intent cleared only for code-proven pre-side-effect rejection classes; 5xx/transport/no-response retain ambiguity; HTTP status presence is never pre-side-effect proof)
issues.title: steer clears attempt intent on ambiguous HTTP 5xx

issues.body:
Independent Sol/max validation at PR #1 head 70b4a9a reproduced a fail-open branch in the cond-0022 Codex MCP isolation. A temporary Codex config containing `[mcp_servers."dot.name"]` is classified as unexpressible by the generated override code. Spawn preflight emits only a warning and continues, while doctor returns `ok: true` even though that operator MCP server is not disabled. The worker can therefore inherit the personal server and recreate the first-turn wedge class. Fail closed whenever the skipped/unexpressible list is non-empty in provision and spawn, and make doctor non-green. Supporting probe: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-a-validator-sol/independent_core_probes.py`, test `W2McpAndUnstickProbe.test_reproduces_unexpressible_mcp_name_fail_open_and_false_green_doctor`.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A fix pass, spec cond-0036 amendment `e0bad58`):** a non-empty skipped/unexpressible set is now a fail-closed condition at all three surfaces. `provision._refresh_codex_mcp_pins` raises `configuration-schema` naming every offending server before any pin block is written (guidance: rename to a bare-key-safe name, remove, then re-provision); `spawn._codex_mcp_pin_preflight` raises before terminal creation with the same guidance; `doctor._check_codex_mcp_pin` returns non-green while the set is non-empty. Quoted-key support was NOT attempted — refusal remains the only proven-safe behavior until a name class is proven through the real CAO yolo command-construction path. Named proofs: `tests/test_codexmcp.py::ProvisionPinTest::test_provision_refuses_unexpressible_server_names_fail_closed` (dotted + quoted-with-space names error, no pin block written), `SpawnDriftGuardTest::test_unexpressible_server_refuses_spawn_fail_closed` and `::test_unexpressible_only_server_refuses_even_without_block`, `DoctorCodexMcpPinTest::test_unexpressible_server_names_are_non_green`, and the end-to-end `tests/test_spawn.py::SpawnTest::test_codex_unexpressible_mcp_name_refuses_before_terminal_creation` (refusal with zero `/terminals` requests).

Validator rerun amendment at PR #1 head `80dee5d06f8501f79ee787586ea0ab5a06725277`: dotted/space-name refusal at spawn and doctor now works, but `conduct provision` still installs profiles and performs other mutations before `_refresh_codex_mcp_pins` rejects an unsafe name. The same rerun also proved that `_SAFE_NAME_RE.match` with a `$` anchor accepts a TOML key decoded as `"line\n"`, classifying it as safe and reopening the original fail-open class. The correction must parse and validate the complete operator MCP-name set as the first read-only provision action, carry that validated snapshot through the pin phase, use `fullmatch` or a true end-of-string equivalent, and prove the full profile/skill/Codex trees remain byte-for-byte unchanged for every refused name while safe-name and supervisor-exemption cases still pass. Updated evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-a-validator-sol-rerun/report.md`; frozen probe tests `Cond0036Probe.test_reproduces_provision_mutation_before_unsafe_name_failure` and `Cond0036Probe.test_reproduces_control_character_mcp_name_regex_bypass`.

**Superseding adjudication (PR-A validator-rerun fix pass, spec cond-0036 amendment Fable `6fb873b`):** the earlier closure above was CONTRADICTED by the validator rerun (provision still mutated before refusal; a `$`-anchored `.match` accepted a TOML key decoding to `"line\n"`) and is superseded — the issue stayed open on authoritative main until this proof passed. Now: `provision._validate_operator_mcp_names` is provision's FIRST, read-only action — before profile copy, skill linking/addition, Codex-profile/config writes, and the repo record — and its one validated snapshot is carried through `_refresh_codex_mcp_pins` (no re-read mid-run). Classification uses `_SAFE_NAME_RE.fullmatch`, rejecting every control character and trailing garbage. Spawn (refusal before terminal creation) and doctor (non-green) behavior, safe-name provisioning, and the supervisor exemption are unchanged. Named proofs: `tests/test_codexmcp.py::Cond0036ValidateFirstTest::test_control_character_names_are_refused` (newline/BEL/trailing-space keys refused; bare-key name still safe), `::test_every_refused_name_class_mutates_nothing` (dotted, quoted, space, terminal-newline, control-char, trailing-garbage — each under a byte-for-byte full-tree before/after snapshot of agent store, Codex home, skill/worktree links, and state root), `::test_name_scan_is_first_action_and_snapshot_feeds_pins` (seam-recorded order: the single parse precedes the first mutation and its snapshot — not a re-read — feeds pin generation), the amended `::ProvisionPinTest::test_provision_refuses_unexpressible_server_names_fail_closed` (refusal installs NOTHING), the retained safe-name/supervisor-exemption provisioning tests, `SpawnDriftGuardTest`/`DoctorCodexMcpPinTest` non-green coverage, and `tests/test_spawn.py::SpawnTest::test_codex_unexpressible_mcp_name_refuses_before_terminal_creation` (zero `/terminals` requests).
issues.resolution: fixed (validate-first provision: complete operator MCP-name set parsed and validated as the first read-only action with fullmatch + control-character rejection; zero mutation on every refusal; fail-closed surfaces unchanged)
