issues.body:
Independent Sol/max validation at PR #1 head 70b4a9a found that caller-controlled `--steer-id` is concatenated into `<psd>/steers/<id>.json` without validation or containment. On a first steer, `--steer-id ../session-env` creates `steers/` and writes through `..`, overwriting `<psd>/session-env.json` before terminal I/O. Reject invalid IDs before any filesystem access or POST using a strict safe alphabet and defense-in-depth realpath/commonpath containment. Add first-steer tests for traversal, absolute paths, separators, empty/dot components, and zero terminal I/O on refusal. Supporting probe: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-a-validator-sol/independent_core_probes.py`, test `W6SteerProbe.test_reproduces_steer_id_path_escape_overwriting_session_record`. This terminal-delivery subsystem is already under the three-strikes design review and feature freeze; route the correction through retained Fable.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A fix pass, spec cond-0037 amendment `e0bad58`):** `steer.run` validates a caller-supplied `--steer-id` against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` as its FIRST act on both the steer and `--resolve` paths — before project-state resolution, any filesystem read/write, path construction, or POST — and rejects rather than normalizes. `_record_path` independently enforces canonical containment: `commonpath(realpath(record), realpath(steers_dir)) == realpath(steers_dir)` with a strict-beneath check, so an escape is refused even with the alphabet gate bypassed. Named proofs: `tests/test_steer.py::SteerIdValidationTest` — first-steer rejection of `../session-env`, an absolute path, `/` and `\` separators, `.`/`..`/`a..b` dot components, over-length (65) and empty values, and a non-alphanumeric first char, each with `steers/` never created, byte-identical `<psd>` snapshots, and zero requests/input/key I/O; `test_containment_seam_refuses_escape_with_alphabet_gate_bypassed` proves the containment seam independently; valid ids (`s1`, `A9_-z`, `a`, 64 chars) still steer. All cond-0032–0035 at-most-once and ambiguity tests (`CrashWindowTest`, `Cond0035ErrorClassificationTest`, `AtMostOnceMatrixTest`, `ResolutionTest`) remain green and unchanged in semantics.
issues.resolution: fixed (steer-id strict-alphabet validation before any path construction/IO/POST, reject-not-normalize, plus realpath/commonpath containment beneath steers/)
issues.title: conduct steer allows steer-id journal path escape

issues.body:
Independent Sol/max validation at PR #1 head 70b4a9a found that `conduct deploy --bounce` does not enforce its mandatory executable-identity interlock when neither expected CAO executable can be resolved. `_validate_bounce_target()` builds `allowed_exes`, then checks membership only under `if allowed_exes`; an empty set skips the executable condition entirely. A stable same-UID unrelated process whose argv contains `cao-server --port

` can pass the remaining checks and become a SIGTERM target. Fail closed when the expected executable set is empty, and require membership unconditionally otherwise. Add a seam-injected empty-resolver test plus positive CAO-venv and entry-script cases. **Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A fix pass, spec cond-0038 amendment `e0bad58`):** `_validate_bounce_target` now raises `deployment-failed` with the resolution evidence ("cannot establish the expected CAO executable identity", citing both `install.cao_venv_python()` and `shutil.which('cao-server')` results) when the expected-executable set resolves empty — before ps inspection and before any signal; when the set is non-empty the membership check is unconditional (`if allowed_exes and` guard deleted). Named proofs: `tests/test_deploy.py::SigtermValidationTest::test_empty_executable_resolution_fails_closed_no_signal` (seam-injected None/None resolvers; ps_fn never called; os.kill never called), `::test_cao_server_entry_script_exe_accepted` (entry-script membership), `::test_same_uid_foreign_exe_with_cao_like_argv_refused` (same-UID unrelated listener whose argv names `cao-server --port

` still refused), plus the pre-existing positive CAO-venv case `::test_valid_target_accepted_and_journaled`.
issues.failing_command: conduct deploy --repo <repo> --bounce (with cao_venv_python and cao-server resolution both unavailable)
issues.resolution: fixed (empty expected-executable set is a fail-closed bounce error before SIGTERM; membership unconditional when non-empty)
issues.title: conduct deploy bounce skips executable identity when unresolved

issues.body:
Fresh Sol/max validation at PR #1 head `80dee5d06f8501f79ee787586ea0ab5a06725277` proved that every real non-dry-run `conduct deploy` rejects its own doctor phase. Deploy first persists the current phase as `in_progress`; the real install-drift doctor check then treats that exact active journal as an abandoned critical deployment, causing the battery to fail and the attempt to end as failed. Existing deploy tests mask the composition by mocking the doctor battery.

Pass a narrowly scoped active deploy-attempt identity into the doctor battery and permit only that exact currently executing attempt/phase after all prerequisite phases are complete. Do not ignore arbitrary `in_progress` journals: stale or crashed attempts must remain critical. Add an unmocked real-battery deploy regression and a separate stale/crashed-journal test.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A validator-rerun fix pass, spec W4 §5.2 Fable `6fb873b`):** deploy passes its executing `{attempt_id, current_phase: "doctor"}` identity IN-PROCESS to the doctor battery (`deploy._run_doctor_battery` -> the doctor namespace's `active_deploy_attempt`; never an env var or file). `doctor._check_install_drift` (`_is_live_deploy_attempt`) accepts an `in_progress` journal only when the attempt id matches the identity AND the single in-progress phase is exactly the named doctor phase AND every other journaled phase is completed. Foreign/stale ids, a crashed pre-doctor in-progress phase, incomplete prerequisites, any `failed` journal, and standalone `conduct doctor` (no identity) remain critical exactly as before. Named proofs: `tests/test_deploy.py::Cond0044RealBatteryDeployTest::test_deploy_with_real_doctor_battery_completes` (unmocked deploy through the REAL doctor battery completes; journal finalized `completed`), and `::Cond0044ActiveAttemptTest` — `::test_exact_live_attempt_at_doctor_phase_is_accepted`, `::test_foreign_attempt_journal_stays_critical`, `::test_crashed_pre_doctor_phase_stays_critical`, `::test_incomplete_prerequisites_stay_critical`, `::test_standalone_doctor_passes_no_identity_and_stays_critical`, `::test_failed_journal_with_matching_identity_stays_critical`.
issues.resolution: fixed (in-process {attempt_id, current_phase} identity from deploy to its doctor battery; install-drift accepts only the exact live attempt at the doctor phase with all prerequisites complete; every other in_progress/failed journal stays critical)
issues.title: deploy doctor rejects its own active attempt

issues.body:
Fresh Sol/max validation at PR #1 head `80dee5d06f8501f79ee787586ea0ab5a06725277` proved that `conduct deploy --dry-run` violates its no-write contract. In isolated temporary state, agent-store, worktree-link, and Codex-config roots, the command returned success but copied/rewrote installed profiles and appended a deploy event to a pre-existing project's event log. The attempt journal and receipt stayed absent, localizing the writes to provision/event paths.

Make deploy dry-run provision planning-only, including profile copies, skill links/additions, and Codex configuration, and suppress deploy event emission. Add a complete before/after filesystem snapshot over state root, agent store, worktree links, and Codex configuration proving zero writes.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A validator-rerun fix pass, spec W4 §5.2 Fable `6fb873b`):** under `--dry-run` the provision phase now calls the read-only `provision.plan` (reports what it would copy/link/write — profiles, skill links/additions, Codex configuration, repo record — and performs none of it; the cond-0036 name validation still runs first, read-only), and `_log_deploy_event` emits nothing for a dry run. The attempt journal and receipt were already unwritten under dry-run. Named proofs: `tests/test_deploy.py::Cond0045DryRunZeroWritesTest::test_dry_run_success_writes_nothing` and `::test_dry_run_injected_failure_writes_nothing` — each under a byte-for-byte before/after filesystem snapshot spanning the state root, agent store, skill/worktree links, and Codex configuration, with an explicit assertion that no `deploy` event line exists in any project's events.ndjsonl, and the mutating provision entry point armed to fail the test if invoked.
issues.resolution: fixed (deploy dry-run is planning-only and zero-write end-to-end: provision plan, no attempt journal, no receipt, no deploy event — on success and on injected failure alike)
issues.title: deploy dry-run mutates profiles and event logs

issues.body:
Fresh Sol/max validation at PR #1 head `80dee5d06f8501f79ee787586ea0ab5a06725277` synchronized two `conduct steer` callers on the same previously unused steer ID. Both observed no record, both returned success, and the recording CAO client saw two amendment input POSTs and two `C-s` key POSTs. Atomic file replacement does not serialize the read/create/I/O transaction, so W6's at-most-once property fails under overlapping callers.

This terminal-delivery subsystem is already beyond three strikes, so require retained-Fable design review rather than another local peel. The smallest durable direction is an inter-process per-steer-ID lock or equivalent exclusive claim acquired before the first record read and held through final confirmation. The second caller must observe the durable attempted/completed state and follow existing no-replay rules. Require a multiprocessing race proving exactly one input and one chord plus crash/recovery coverage for the lock owner, without weakening the intent-before-I/O and ambiguous-state semantics from cond-0032 through cond-0035.

**Adjudication (self-heal readiness campaign, PR-A validator-rerun fix pass, spec §15.2 concurrency amendment Fable `6fb873b`):** after strict steer-id validation and BEFORE the first record read, `conduct steer` acquires a bounded-wait `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` on the contained per-ID lock path (`steer._steer_claim`, same validated-id containment-checked path family as the record) and holds it through every record read/write, both terminal POSTs, and the final confirmation write; `--resolve` takes the same claim. Timeout fails closed ("being executed by another process") with zero record reads and zero I/O. Owner crash needs no machinery: the kernel releases the flock and the next caller reads the durably persisted intent into the existing cond-0032/0034 ambiguity procedure. No stale-lock deletion; cond-0032–0035 semantics unchanged (their full matrices re-run with the claim active). Named proofs: `tests/test_steer.py::Cond0046ClaimTest::test_multiprocessing_race_exactly_one_input_and_one_chord` (two real processes on one fresh steer-id against a recording stub CAO: exactly one /input and exactly one /key in total; the loser observes the durable completed state and refuses), `::test_claim_timeout_fails_closed_zero_reads_zero_io` (held claim; refusal; zero record reads via a counting seam; zero POSTs; no record created), `::test_owner_crash_recovers_with_zero_repeat_io` (owner killed after intent persist, before confirmation; next caller goes ambiguous with zero repeat input/key POSTs), both under a `<psd>` containment snapshot, plus the pre-existing cond-0032/0033/0034/0035/0037 steer suites re-run with the claim active (33 tests).
issues.resolution: fixed by design review (exclusive per-steer flock claim serializing read->I/O->confirm across processes; bounded-wait timeout fails closed with zero record reads and zero I/O; owner crash recovers via kernel lock release into the existing ambiguity matrix)
issues.title: concurrent same-id steer duplicates input and chord

issues.body:
Fresh independent Sol/max validation of companion PR-C head `a81853fa547788b97775af9fa377bc25e6a1643e` proved that session-env deletion fails open. `set_session_env({})` delegates to `clear_session_env`, whose exhausted database delete is warned and swallowed before the cache is evicted. The valid stale row remains durable, is accepted on a cold read, and can be injected into a later window of a newly reused session name. A real SQLite exclusive lock reproduced the behavior; new-session creation proceeded, and reconciliation falsely reported the still-present row as removed.

Make public clear strict: durable deletion must complete before cache eviction, and retry exhaustion must raise `SessionEnvStoreError`. Empty-set and new-session pre-clear paths must fail before tmux creation. Reconciliation may report `removed` only after confirmed deletion. Cleanup that must preserve an earlier exception may catch/log the strict clear only at that explicit teardown call site. Add injected-delete-failure, real-lock, reused-session-window, and reconciliation regressions. This is a P1 amendment to the active C1 companion lane; PR-C must not merge or deploy until fixed and independently revalidated.

issues.body:
PR-B terminal 0747cca4 reached its 60-minute deadline while still finishing and the sentinel queued deadman inbox row 309 for the supervisor at 14:12:34 EDT. The worker then completed and emitted its truthful done report as row 311 at 14:15:21, closing the obligation. Because the supervisor was stale-processing, the pending-inbox watchdog later delivered the older deadman first at 14:17:34. The supervisor acted on that now-obsolete notification and sent row 313 to the already-completed Kimi worker at 14:18:02, reactivating it; Kimi performed read-only rechecks and emitted duplicate done report row 314 at 14:18:32. No state was damaged here, but this wastes provider quota and a less defensive worker could resume mutable completed work. When a report/emission closes an obligation, invalidate or supersede any still-pending deadman control notification for that obligation generation, or require event-state reconciliation before the supervisor acts. Add a race regression with a wedged supervisor inbox: queue a deadman, emit done before delivery, recover the inbox, and prove no actionable stale worker nudge and no duplicate callback.

The predicted mutable failure then occurred on PR-B task `self-heal-pr-b-fix-post-final-validator-p1`. Kimi emitted its done report at `2026-07-22T01:38:53Z`, claiming pushed exact head `cc2a3519dae50458b07a1cacbe59fa5c85b8326f` and a clean worktree. After that callback, two previously delivered urgent amendments and a deadman nudge remained queued in the Kimi composer. Kimi subsequently consumed the amendments, modified tracked files `install.sh`, `scripts/run_module.py`, and `scripts/_lib/test_vendored_runtime.py`, and started another test run. At `01:45` the remote branch and draft PR still pointed to `cc2a351`, while the leased worktree contained 170 uncommitted insertions/deletions beyond that reported boundary. The supervisor's independent pre-collection check caught the mismatch and correctly did not collect or launch the exact-head validator.

This makes cond-0054 P1: a done callback must seal the task generation against all older queued worker inputs, not merely queued deadman notifications. Otherwise a normal supervisor can validate a stale pushed head while the worker mutates the lease, or collect/delete a terminal with unreported changes after trusting the callback. On accepted report finalization, atomically supersede every not-yet-submitted input addressed to that task/run/generation; provider-queued text must be withdrawn if the provider supports it, and otherwise the terminal must enter a sealed state that prevents the queued text from starting mutable work. Any input intentionally sent after finalization requires a new explicit continuation generation and acknowledgement, not implicit composer drain. Add Kimi regressions for queued amendment + queued deadman + done callback, proving no post-report model submission, no tracked mutation, no duplicate report, and a stable exact commit/tree through collection. Cross-reference cond-0031 and cond-0072 for urgent steering and terminal-queued-versus-model-submitted lifecycle; this issue owns finalization invalidation and the immutable report boundary.

The same stale-deadman ordering defect later caused a false failed collection for Lane A task `self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-fix-functional-p1-d567be8-recovery-1`. The worker had already written a complete DONE report, pushed clean exact head `3ad661d4df178c4895cf9a75211aa6d45ae47d76`, and emitted its done callback at `2026-07-23T22:20:38Z`; a previously queued repeated-deadman notification was then acted on and the generation was collected failed at `22:21:00Z` before the callback was reconciled. The late delivered callback and durable report/Git identity prove product completion, so no implementation retry is warranted, but the run outcome is now falsely failed and the terminal was deleted. This recurrence requires pending deadman actions to revalidate the exact obligation generation against any already-emitted report/callback and durable finalization record immediately before failed collection. If completion raced with the deadman, collection must preserve and reconcile the DONE outcome rather than delete/mark failed; add the exact report-before-deadman-delivery and callback-pending-at-collection race. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-fix-functional-p1-d567be8-recovery-1/report.md`, report SHA-256 `d218f1b7d9a7c7239c6656329497cf6c80533939fdd4ec88359bbb16b6a75677`, and the clean local/remote/PR head above.

issues.body:
The persistent GPT-5.6-sol supervisor has reached the Codex "Additional safety checks" numbered interstitial on four distinct orchestration turns during this campaign (manual recoveries recorded at 14:03:02, 14:03:43, 14:20:29, and 14:25:25 EDT). Ordinary worker adjudication or spawn preparation stops indefinitely at choices Retry with a faster model / Keep waiting / Learn more. A fifth occurrence then wedged disposable Sol/max PR-B validator `350c2c19` during ordinary isolated probes; evidence is also in `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/350c2c19.log`. Worker deadmen do not cover the supervisor, and a worker deadman can notify the supervisor but cannot answer the worker's waiting-user-answer prompt; pending-inbox recovery resolves neither case. A nominally unattended long-running run therefore wedges or eventually discards healthy work until this external monitor sends key 2 plus Enter. Implement a narrow, auditable recovery boundary for every conduct-managed Codex terminal: detect this exact provider prompt, select only the non-bypass Keep waiting action with a bounded attempt count, journal/emit the recovery, and resume the same turn. Never choose a faster model or bypass a safety decision. If prompt text/choices differ, Keep waiting repeats beyond the bound, or recovery does not restore progress, fail closed and alert the human out of band. Add provider-adapter/integration tests for exact detection, single key sequence, changed-prompt refusal, bounded repeat escalation, preservation of queued supervisor work, and preservation of an in-flight disposable worker task.

**Implementation status (W8 fixer pass, `fix/long-run-readiness`):** the conductor side of spec §17 is implemented — the separate sentinel `interstitial_recovery` subsystem with the versioned one-entry prompt registry, durable eligibility (recorded supervisor / manifest-bound Codex workers with open obligation and write-role lease), generation binding with intent-before-I/O, at-most-one answer, 3/hour repetition bound, 10-minute progress window, pre-answer completion reconcile, redacted W1-mirrored events, and the full mandatory test matrix against a fake structured boundary (`plugin/tests/test_interstitial_recovery.py`). **Closure remains BLOCKED on the CAO fork companion:** installed CAO 2.3.0 exposes neither (ii) `GET /terminals/{id}/user-prompt` returning `{prompt_id, text, choices[]}` nor (iii) the idempotent stale-rejecting `POST /terminals/{id}/user-prompt/answer`, and its Codex adapter does not classify this interstitial as `waiting_user_answer` (see cond-0056). Until the companion lands and both supervisor and managed-worker coverages are proven against the real boundary, the subsystem runs fail-closed alert-only and this issue stays OPEN.

PR-A W8 head `74ba7fbae25eb94ef8ad4cf9780ee7e123fa505f` implemented the conductor-side alert-only seam but its pre-answer reconcile treats an existing `report.md` as `run-done`. The campaign's PR-C refusal timeline disproves that completion proxy: a report file can be fully written while the original `conduct report` callback/event is still undelivered, and recovery is required to let that callback occur. For W8 as for W9, durable completion is the delivered original callback/report event for the exact task/run/callback generation or finalized collection, never report-file existence, mtime, terminal idleness, or provider/dashboard status. Correct W8 before acceptance: written report + undelivered callback remains eligible for exactly one bounded option-2 recovery that preserves the report and yields only the original callback; delivered callback/event, finalized collection, or a callback race before answer produces zero answer I/O. Add the matching preservation/race/no-duplicate tests. This is an amendment to existing cond-0055, not a new issue.

**Authoritative user correction, superseding automatic option-2 and immediate-human-gate interpretations:** the OpenAI `Additional safety checks` choice screen is a transient validation display that normally self-resolves. On preserved Sol/max validator `self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-post-final-fix`, terminal `79d5a2b8`, the screen cleared with zero answer/input and the same turn continued. The attempted structured `answer_user_prompt(..., answer=2)` returned `success=false` before I/O, so it consumed neither an answer nor a recovery generation and is evidence only that no input was sent. Default handling is passive wait/monitor with no answer, no recovery-budget consumption, no deadman nudge, and no human-blocker alert. Escalation or any bounded recovery requires a separately specified timeout plus durable proof that the transient failed to resolve; prompt appearance alone is insufficient. Existing W8/spec language that treats appearance as immediately answerable must be corrected before implementation acceptance. Evidence: terminal `79d5a2b8`, provider pane `%158`, Codex session `019f8700-b267-7cb3-9fef-f5205d029ea7`, and the zero-I/O structured-answer response in `.conductor/JOURNAL.md`.

Fresh Sol/max validation of skillshare PR-B head `0de8da4429bc784fb040c5d357768f6e9d2ae58b` removed `orjson` from a temporary realized venv, then supplied a fake ambient `orjson.py` through `PYTHONPATH`. The health probe passed, skipped repair, and created a run, while the same venv failed `import orjson` under `env -i`. Ambient Python state can therefore mask a corrupt vendored runtime.

Make runtime health probes isolated from ambient Python configuration in preflight and installer, and retain the exact adverse-PYTHONPATH regression plus clean-environment verification. PR-B must not merge until fixed and independently revalidated.

Fresh exact-head revalidation at PR-B `e79d9e7525d166f6136b261462ae9b204fb7eca5` passed the hostile `PYTHONPATH`, user-site, `PYTHONHOME`, fake-module, sparse/empty-PATH, repair/fail-closed, and realized-venv import cases. This is sufficient current evidence for the cond-0058 behavior, but the entry remains OPEN until the revised shared C2 head passes full independent revalidation and merge/installed acceptance so a later fix cannot regress it. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-rerun/report.md`.

Fresh independent validation at exact staging head `642207ecc0f42c8a048764a89b920ad4dc4aee40` found cond-0058 still open. Isolation is limited to the runtime health probe (`-I`), while later preflight/install `$PY -B` invocations retain ambient Python startup configuration; a hostile `PYTHONPATH` containing `sitecustomize.py` can therefore execute foreign code after the health gate. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-final-staging/report.md` (F3). Use one sanitized/isolated launcher for every skill-owned Python process and add end-to-end `sitecustomize`, `PYTHONHOME`, fake-PATH-python, and fake-PATH-uv cases across preflight, persisted commands, renderers, and installer. Canonical port and Skillshare merge remain blocked pending a fresh exact-head proof.

Fresh independent exact-head validation at staging head `e8ab43b7449ab58e4349ad9e5c9841d1d4bf9ec8` retained two P1 cond-0058 failures. First, when fixed uv candidates are absent, both `resolve_uv` implementations execute a marker-writing PATH-only `uv`; sanitizing that executable's child environment does not make its selection trusted. Second, `env -i` plus `PYTHONPATH` and `python -B -m _lib...` remains ambient-CWD sensitive: a hostile or accidental CWD `_lib` wins module selection, caused production failure, and defeated two owned failure-injection tests in the exact-archive 594-test suite. Remove PATH uv fallback; accept only an explicit validated absolute uv or enumerated trusted absolute candidates. Run Python entrypoints under isolated startup without ambient `PYTHONPATH`, using an absolute trusted launcher/module root, and retain PATH-marker plus hostile-CWD package regressions. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-post-final-fix/report.md`, `first-pass/raw/uv-lock-and-versions.json`, `first-pass/raw/process-isolation-and-argv.json`, and the full-suite retry/diagnostic logs. cond-0058 remains OPEN and blocks canonical port.

Active fixer conformance evidence at `2026-07-22T00:49:18Z`: the first isolated-launcher attempt is itself nonfunctional. Exact safe command `skill/.venv/bin/python -I -B skill/scripts/run_module.py _lib.install_manifest --help` returns 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_lib'`; Python 3.13.5 reports `sys.flags.isolated=1`, `safe_path=True`, and a `sys.path` that omits `scripts/`. Under `-I`, executing a script does not establish the launcher's directory as `sys.path[0]`, contrary to the draft launcher's assumption. The launcher must explicitly seed only the canonical absolute trusted scripts directory before `runpy`, while retaining isolated startup and rejecting ambient CWD/PYTHONPATH. Add direct neutral- and hostile-CWD launcher regressions. Shipped comments/docs must explain the trusted-root invariant and shadowing failure self-containedly rather than relying on the historical `cond-0058` identifier. This is existing cond-0058, not a new issue.

Distinct active-fixer conformance evidence at `2026-07-22T01:00:22Z` proves the same `-I` breakage applies to direct script entrypoints, not only module dispatch. From a neutral CWD, `skill/.venv/bin/python -I -B <absolute-script> --help` returns 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_lib'` for `build_context_cost.py`, `render_personas.py`, `validate_context_cards.py`, and `snapshot_governing_context.py`; a static sweep found additional shipped scripts with the same implicit-root assumption. The single trusted launcher/root mechanism must support both trusted module dispatch and trusted absolute-script dispatch, and every preflight/install/persisted/fresh skill-owned entrypoint must route through it with `-I` retained. Add representative neutral/hostile-CWD module and direct-script regressions with zero marker execution. This is a second amendment to existing cond-0058, not a new issue or replay of the prior steer.

Fresh Sol/max validation of skillshare PR-B head `0de8da4429bc784fb040c5d357768f6e9d2ae58b` found installer sequencing and atomicity fail C2. A clean install reaches Python-dependent rendering before `ensure_skill_runtime`, so it fails before bootstrapping even when uv is available. In another isolated case, a broken runtime with uv unavailable allowed target/overlay/manifest mutation, then the late `ensure_skill_runtime || true` failure was swallowed and install exited success with an unusable target.

Hard-fail runtime bootstrap before every renderer or install mutation, remove the swallowed runtime failure, and stage/commit target and manifest changes so install cannot report partial success. Add clean-absent-runtime and broken/no-uv zero-mutation regressions.

Fresh exact-head revalidation at PR-B `e79d9e7525d166f6136b261462ae9b204fb7eca5` found two remaining P1 transaction failures. First, `install.sh --copy` removes the live target and copies directly into its place before target bootstrap, rendering, imports, and postconditions finish; injected target-sync and late-renderer failures returned nonzero but deleted the old-target sentinel and left a partial replacement (`029-0059-target-bootstrap-fail`, `031-0059-late-render-fail`). Second, `manifest_write_post_install ... || warn` deliberately suppresses an injected manifest-write failure, returns 0, and leaves inconsistent installation mutation (`035-0059-manifest-fail`). Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-rerun/report.md`. Build and fully validate a sibling staged target, include target/overlay/manifest publication in one fatal transaction, and atomically swap only after every postcondition succeeds with rollback preserving the old target. cond-0059 remains OPEN pending all failure-window proofs.

Fresh independent validation at exact staging head `642207ecc0f42c8a048764a89b920ad4dc4aee40` proved the attempted transaction still destroys the live target. The installer moves the existing target into `$TXN_DIR/old-target` before staging completes, never registers that path for rollback, removes the replacement on failure, then deletes the transaction directory and the only old-target copy. Target-sync, target-render, manifest-write, inode/postcondition, and TERM failures all lost the prior target; even success exposed a long missing-live-target interval. The committed rollback tests were false-green on macOS because their manifest used `/tmp/...` while production canonicalized the same inode to `/private/tmp/...`, taking a compensating stale-target branch absent in the canonical same-path case. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-final-staging/report.md` (F1/F2). Keep the old live target present while building/validating the sibling stage, register an actual rollback backup before publication, restore on every failure/signal, and canonicalize same-path fixtures with watcher assertions. cond-0059 remains OPEN and blocks canonical port/Skillshare merge.

Fresh independent failure injection at exact PR-B staging head `e8ab43b7449ab58e4349ad9e5c9841d1d4bf9ec8` confirms the remaining rollback branch is P1. The preserved probe forced manifest failure and then a second atomic-helper failure; the installer returned 1, but the canonical live-path watcher recorded 538 missing-target observations over approximately 139 ms, and neither the public-target snapshot nor the full-project snapshot was restored byte-equal. The validator's completed report confirms this as a must-fix implementation defect, not merely a missing proof. The smallest accepted correction is never to delete the public replacement as a rollback fallback: restore through a supported atomic exchange, or fail closed with the replacement still live and the registered old store retained for explicit recovery. A fresh exact-head validator must rerun the helper-failure watcher and byte-identical rollback matrix. Fresh Sol/max revalidation of companion PR-C head `8e46d8912c0033d7b8a6ce5097ec5773dc108587` proved the cond-0050 zero-side-effect boundary remains incomplete. New-session strict pre-clear is inside `create_terminal`'s broad resource-cleanup try. When pre-clear raises before this invocation acquires any resource, the generic handler still stops/unlinks the generated terminal ID's FIFO, clears status, cleans its provider, and deletes its terminal row.

A deterministic isolated probe forced the 32-bit generated terminal ID to collide with an unrelated seeded live terminal. Injected pre-clear exhaustion correctly retained the stale session-env row but deleted the unrelated terminal DB row, unlinked its FIFO, and removed/cleaned its provider state. Add a collision regression seeding unrelated FIFO/status/provider/row state and proving byte-for-byte preservation plus zero cleanup calls. cond-0050 remains open; PR-C must not merge until this P1 and the full strict-clear matrix pass fresh independent revalidation.

issues.body:
The exact provider refusal `This content cannot be shown` interrupted the benign PR-C validator twice and then interrupted the persistent campaign supervisor after ordinary test and issue-ledger work. In each occurrence the Codex terminal returned to an idle prompt without the active worker callback, a pending-inbox trigger, or a supervisor deadman. Manual structured inbox messages 334 and 335 resumed the same PR-C task and preserved its completed report; the report event was finally emitted at 2026-07-21T19:24:43Z. The supervisor required a separate human message to resume.

This is distinct from cond-0055. cond-0055 covers the structured `Additional safety checks` waiting-user-answer prompt and its non-bypass `Keep waiting` response. This refusal instead silently abandons an active conduct obligation/turn and presents no answer prompt. Three observed occurrences make it a P1 unattended-campaign blocker and require design review rather than another local recovery peel.

Add a structured, provider-bound refusal signal and recovery path for conduct-managed Codex terminals. Eligibility must be bound to the exact active project, terminal generation, task/run/report path, lease, and non-finalized obligation; the supervisor case needs an equally durable active campaign-action identity. Reconcile completion, callback, collection, supersession, and already-delivered continuation state before acting. Permit only a bounded benign continuation of the same task through a structured delivery surface, with durable attempt intent and ambiguity handling that never blindly replays. On changed refusal identity, ambiguous delivery, repeated refusal, exhausted bound, or no progress, fail closed and alert out of band.

Do not inspect pane text, scrape the TUI, or synthesize raw key sequences. Do not spawn a replacement, duplicate the task, lose an existing report, or emit a second callback. Tests must cover repeated worker refusal, supervisor refusal, completion racing recovery, ambiguous delivery/crash windows, preserved in-flight task/report state, bounded escalation, and exactly one callback.

Durable evidence: terminal logs for `ad48e90c` and `13e6fe47`; CAO inbox rows 334 and 335 in `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/db/cli-agent-orchestrator.db`; campaign report event at 2026-07-21T19:24:43Z in `events.ndjsonl`.

Fresh reproduction during exact-head PR-B validation broadened the recovery failure. Conduct task `self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-b65c222`, terminal `177067b6`, reached the same hard refusal after writing its supplemental atomic harness at reviewed head `b65c22237a17a93c47ee1905a072eadb126b720e`. It remained idle for about 25 minutes and did not resume automatically. At approximately `2026-07-22T03:44:49Z` the human directly entered `continue`; no CAO inbox row or structured recovery receipt exists for that input. The request immediately hit the refusal again, the visible provider session then changed from `gpt-5.6-sol max` to `gpt-5.6-terra xhigh`, and a second human `continue` resumed the original task. The preserved supplemental probes subsequently passed 3/3. This proves the current recovery contract must also preserve and attest model/provider identity across refusal recovery, distinguish direct human input from conductor delivery, and report any mid-obligation model change rather than attributing the continuation to automatic validation or the originally assigned route. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/177067b6.log` and `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-validator-sol-b65c222/evidence/03b-atomic-supplemental-results.json`.

**Human-authorized fallback amendment (`2026-07-22T03:55:46Z`):** treat the exact hard-refusal screen as distinct from the transient `Additional safety checks` screen and support an explicit lower-capability model handoff instead of waiting indefinitely. Preferred behavior is a structured provider refusal signal plus a structured model-selection/relaunch surface: seal the refused Sol generation, preserve its exact artifacts and unfinished obligation, create a new provider/profile/model/effort-attested fallback generation (currently `gpt-5.6-terra`/`xhigh`), transfer a bounded durable handoff, and disclose that the resulting review is mixed-route rather than the originally assigned all-Sol verdict. If the installed Codex surface exposes only the interactive `/model` menus, any supervisor automation must be version-bound and state-observing: exact task-owning pane/session/generation binding, bracket-free `/model` + Enter control input, captured menu identity before each deterministic arrow/Enter transition, post-switch provider-native route attestation, and fail-closed abort on any unexpected menu or ambiguous input. Never blindly replay a fixed key count. This fallback depends on the identity-bound bracket-free control-input capability tracked by cond-0026; until both seams exist, preserve the refused generation and require a disclosed human handoff.

**Fallback-return policy amendment:** make the downgrade route a configured, attested ladder rather than a Terra-only special case: prefer the originally assigned Sol route, fall back to Terra at the strongest available reasoning effort, and permit Luna only when the provider forces it or no stronger allowed route can progress. At the earliest safe checkpoint (no in-flight tool/process, artifacts durably flushed, obligation and handoff generation sealed), attempt a bounded return to the originally assigned Sol route when the task warrants the best available judgment. Re-attest the route before consuming the next handoff and record every segment; never present mixed-model work as a single-route verdict. For quality-critical validation/review, a fallback route may preserve progress and complete bounded evidence collection, but final adjudication/sign-off must return to a fresh assigned-Sol generation when available. Apply bounded retry/backoff and a no-oscillation limit; repeated refusal or ambiguous switching remains fail-closed with the current artifacts preserved.

Fresh route-integrity reproduction during exact-head gate `self-heal-postfix-review-terra-68e83a2`, terminal `2476fac1`: the assigned Sol/max generation reached the exact persistent hard-refusal screen after preserving artifacts under `/tmp/self-heal-postfix-review-terra-68e83a2.0SDiIW`. The human performed the authorized same-obligation fallback by binding sole task-owning pane `%178`, using literal bracket-free `/model`, capturing the menu states, selecting `gpt-5.6-terra` then `Extra high`, and verifying the visible route as Terra/xhigh before resuming. The durable terminal transcript subsequently recorded at least three automatic changes to `gpt-5.6-luna` at low effort before report completion. Therefore successful interactive selection and one post-switch UI check are not durable route attestation: the effective model can drift again inside the same obligation, making a nominal Terra/xhigh gate falsely claim stronger judgment. Treat the run's evidence as useful but the gate as BLOCKED and mixed-route; it cannot be final Terra or Sol sign-off. W9 must bind each route segment to provider-native model/effort identity at the model-input admission boundary, continuously or at every turn/handoff checkpoint, seal on any unrequested drift, and make the public report/callback derive its route provenance from those immutable receipts rather than launch arguments or a one-time UI observation. Automatic downgrade to Luna/low must never inherit Terra/xhigh authority; record the exact segment, preserve artifacts, fail closed, and require a fresh quality-critical final gate on the strongest available configured route after implementation fixes. Tests must reproduce Terra/xhigh selection followed by repeated automatic Luna/low drift, reject a falsely strong callback, prove exactly one truthful blocked callback with a complete segment ledger, and prohibit oscillation or silent route promotion. Evidence: terminal log `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/2476fac1.log`, preserved scratch directory above, and the eventual amended blocked report for this task.

Fresh Fable-route reproduction during retained spec task `self-heal-control-plane-recovery-fable5-route-gate`, terminal `d2dceff0`, pane `%208`, at `2026-07-23 08:44` local: the terminal had previously passed a route gate and completed Revision 9 entirely on `claude-fable-5`/high. The supervisor then delivered accepted P1 packet inbox row `679` at `2026-07-23 08:41:23.050040`, with an explicit stop-on-switch/no-fallback contract. The same retained generation verified the packet and starting head, read the packet, then visibly emitted the Fable safeguard notice and automatically switched to `opus-4-8`/high. A structured, identity-bound `POST /terminals/d2dceff0/key?key=C-c` returned `{"success":true}` exactly once; the pane recorded `Interrupted`, and the clean retry worktree remained at `b1f522ed59921295b0ce9e28c9ae4a737091cf52` with zero diff and no amendment commit. This proves a human-disabled automatic-switch setting and a prior same-generation route gate do not durably prevent later route drift at packet admission. The recovery contract must enforce the assigned route at the provider/model-input boundary for every turn or amendment, reject or seal the generation before non-assigned output can mutate the worktree, and preserve the accepted packet for a fresh identity-bound Fable-only retry without replaying it into the drifted generation. TUI/footer observation is evidence only, not the trust seam. Cross-reference cond-0026 because the pane also shows bracketed-paste sentinels around the delivered message, but no raw input or client-side paste workaround was used. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/d2dceff0.log`, tmux pane `%208` capture, CAO inbox row `679`, and the clean retry worktree proof above.

**2026-07-23 Lane B production capability recurrence at fork `388b535045052883c050db05c282cbf10977d855`:** fresh focused validation confirmed identity-only diagnostics remain disabled, but `validate_route_proof` accepts malformed caller dictionaries (`native_turn_id={}`, negative event sequence, non-digest model-input value) and accepts changed model or input values. Its claimed positive path is absent from the real `/managed/recovery-capabilities` endpoint, which supplies no route receipt at all. This is P1 functionality: operators cannot obtain trustworthy automated recovery authority from an actual provider route, while a caller-shaped dictionary can falsely advertise it. Add a provider-generated, authenticated, durable receipt source; load it in the endpoint; bind typed provider/session/turn/generation, positive sequence, resolved model/effort, and 64-hex model-input digest to the expected authority boundary. Until that source exists, expose no automated authority. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-b-focused-validator-sol-388b535/report.md`, SHA-256 `2e34192749070aa604556531566f4be5542e7fa1c4ef65955df85b55297c92e7`.

issues.body:
`conduct report` currently labels successful inbox enqueue as durable delivery. `conduct/commands/report.py::_deliver` calls `CaoClient.send_inbox`, ignores the returned inbox message id/status, returns only the receiver id, and immediately appends a campaign event with `detail=delivered_to=<receiver>`. CAO's inbox contract is idle-gated: POST creates a `PENDING` row and only a later idle cycle changes it to `DELIVERED`.

The live self-heal campaign reproduced the gap with PR-C report row 348. At `2026-07-21T19:56:52Z`, `events.ndjsonl` already contained `{"cmd":"report","detail":"delivered_to=13e6fe47",...}`, while SQLite inbox row 348 was still `pending` and the busy supervisor TUI showed the callback under “Messages to be submitted after next tool call.” Only later did the row become `delivered` and enter the supervisor turn. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/events.ndjsonl`, inbox DB `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/db/cli-agent-orchestrator.db` row 348, supervisor terminal log `/Users/colin/.aws/cli-agent-orchestrator/logs/terminal/13e6fe47.log`, and source `conduct/commands/report.py:107-113` plus `conduct/lib/caoapi.py:184-189`.

This is P1 because the newly approved W8/W9 recovery contracts use a “delivered callback/report event” as the durable completion boundary. Treating the current campaign report event as that proof can classify a merely queued callback as complete, refuse recovery, and strand the callback behind a wedged/busy supervisor—the exact failure the report/callback boundary corrections are meant to prevent.

Correct the contract and implementation before W8/W9 acceptance: durable callback completion must require the exact CAO inbox row for the original callback to have status `delivered` (or an equivalent authoritative delivery receipt), bound to sender/receiver/task/run/callback generation. The enqueue-time campaign event alone is not delivery proof. Rename/structure the enqueue event honestly (for example `queued_to` plus message id/status), and if useful emit a distinct delivery-confirmed event from the actual inbox-delivery transition. Add a busy-supervisor regression proving POST success + pending row + enqueue event remains an open obligation eligible for bounded recovery, then actual delivered status closes it; cover the transition/race and ensure exactly one original callback with no replay. Apply this boundary consistently to both existing P1 cond-0055/W8 and cond-0069/W9.

**Precision amendment (supersedes the response-status/example wording above):** verified CAO `POST /terminals/{receiver}/inbox/messages` first creates the row as `PENDING`, attempts immediate delivery, then returns only `success`, `message_id`, `sender_id`, `receiver_id`, and `created_at` — **no status**. The row may therefore be `DELIVERED` before the response or remain `PENDING` afterward. `conduct report` must retain the exact identity/creation fields and emit one status-neutral accepted event such as `accepted_by=<receiver> message_id=<id>`; it must not claim either `pending` or `delivered` at POST time. Authoritative completion requires a later identity- and generation-bound exact-message receipt read. The installed bounded list GET is not exact-message-addressable, and absence from it is ambiguous; no list-absence or direct-DB inference may become the trust boundary without explicit proof. Otherwise require the smallest exact-message CAO receipt companion and keep receipt-dependent W8/W9 behavior fail-closed alert-only. Mandatory tests include immediate delivery before response, pending after response, bounded-list miss, exact identity/stale-generation rejection, pending-to-delivered races, and no duplicate callback. Final approved design authority: Fable spec commit `1e8f8af57710f21ec5d7957457e46ff1b0541fc8`.

Exact-head hostile validation at conductor `9eb0b208c9560e13bff112b62f7aa0d81b2fbfed` found the W10 correction remains incomplete. A successful HTTP POST whose response object omits `message_id` raises ambiguity but does not persist `response_lost`; retry of the identical callback POSTs again and can create a duplicate row. The same gap applies to contradictory sender/receiver receipt fields. In addition, `_receipt_from_response` accepts a response containing only `message_id`, locally fills sender/receiver, accepts `created_at=None`, and persists that synthesized/incomplete identity as authoritative acceptance. The reproduced malformed-response sequence made two POST calls: attempt one raised, attempt two returned a receipt. Treat **every** failure after the POST begins and before the complete returned identity is durably committed as response-loss ambiguity and permanently suppress blind replay. Require exact nonempty returned `message_id`, sender, receiver, and creation time with no local substitution; journal sanitized malformed-response evidence before raising. Add cases for missing/empty/contradictory fields, validator exceptions after a successful POST, crash after response before receipt fsync, and retry proving one POST only.

issues.body:
Fresh Kimi terminal d95f499d visibly entered the assigned task and was actively reading the implementation worktree, but the full task text also remained queued in the Kimi composer with the Ctrl-S steering hint. The spawn readiness/retry path then concluded that input was not accepted, deleted the active terminal, and emitted inbox row 372 saying the worker never started. The terminal API now returns not found, the tmux window is gone, no report exists, and the implementation branch remains unchanged. This is a P1 unattended-campaign failure: a false-negative input-acceptance decision destroys live work and forces reassignment. It compounds cond-0026/0031/0071/0072 but is a distinct destructive spawn-lifecycle boundary. Spawn must bind acceptance to an authoritative provider/model-turn acknowledgement, never infer failure from a queued retry or cosmetic idle state, and must fail closed without deleting a terminal when processing may have started. Add a Kimi regression where the original task begins, a retry is left queued, status is stale/ambiguous, and cleanup preserves the live worker; cover unambiguously never-started cleanup separately, exactly-once task execution, and no duplicate queued task.

Fresh canonical-validator reproduction broadens the same P1 lifecycle boundary in the opposite direction. `conduct spawn` assigned Sol/max task `self-heal-pr-b-canonical-validator-sol` to terminal `51a6327c` after warning that the CAO server had restarted and session environment might be stale. Durable terminal evidence later proved that Codex did start, but stopped before model readiness at the interactive repository-trust preflight (`Do you trust the contents of this directory?`, choices `1. Yes, continue` / `2. No, quit`). Spawn misclassified that preflight UI as ready and pasted the full task before trust resolution; task text interacted with and escaped the prompt, Codex exited, and subsequent task fragments reached zsh, entered `bquote>` continuation parsing, and ended with `zsh: substitution failed`. CAO nevertheless kept the run `assigned`, emitted a first-deadman nudge at 45 minutes, and still showed the terminal `error` and run active roughly 3h40m later with no callback. This is not a completed or merely silent review. Provider process existence alone is insufficient: spawn readiness must detect and resolve-or-fail the exact trust preflight through a controlled, identity-bound path, then prove the same provider generation reached post-preflight model-input readiness before any task text. Shell/error states must fail the generation without task delivery, and the first-deadman path must escalate a provably never-started generation to failed collection plus one fresh exact-head replacement instead of leaving it assigned indefinitely. Evidence: terminal `51a6327c`, task run `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-canonical-validator-sol`, inbox/deadman message `487`, and the terminal log showing the trust prompt followed by shell parsing and `zsh: substitution failed`. cond-0073 remains OPEN.

Immediate retry reproduced the same failure and proves the recovery path lacks a retry breaker. After `51a6327c` was force-collected as failed, fresh task/generation `self-heal-pr-b-canonical-validator-sol-retry-1` was spawned on terminal `f69c1de9`; `conduct spawn` again warned that the CAO server had restarted and session environment might be stale. Codex again started only far enough to present the repository-trust preflight, and spawn again delivered Markdown before that UI was resolved or model readiness existed. Codex exited and the shell repeatedly executed task fragments, producing `command not found` and `permission denied`, so this failure is potentially side-effecting rather than a harmless missing callback. No review work or callback occurred, and the generation was force-collected failed. After one preflight-blocked/provider-unready failure, automatic/manual retry through the same unresolved launch boundary must be blocked: require an explicit project/session/provider environment refresh where applicable, controlled trust resolution or a pre-authorized known-trusted checkout, and an identity-bound post-preflight provider/model-input readiness receipt before any task text. Reset the retry budget only on that authoritative proof; otherwise preserve and alert without task delivery. Never blindly replay numeric choices or mutate protected Codex trust configuration as recovery. Tests must reproduce two consecutive trust-preflight task-delivery failures, prove the second launch is refused before text I/O until recovery succeeds, prove task fragments never reach a shell, reject stale/wrong terminal or provider generations, and prove exactly one later fresh generation only after trust and provider readiness are re-attested. Evidence: terminal `f69c1de9`, run `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-pr-b-canonical-validator-sol-retry-1`, repeated stale-session warning, the trust-prompt text, and subsequent shell error output. The stale server warning is corroborating context, not a sufficient root cause. cond-0073 remains OPEN; W11 already owns the design and no Fable recall is required.

Invocation-scoped trust-preflight investigation identifies an additional concrete W11 implementation boundary. Installed Codex CLI `0.144.6` documents `projects."/absolute/path".trust_level = "trusted"` for persistent TOML, but its CLI dotted override parser does not preserve a path segment containing `.worktrees`: `-c 'projects."/Users/colin/Projects/custom-skills/.worktrees/self-heal-pr-review-vendored-runtime".trust_level="trusted"'` resolves into a malformed nested session layer rather than the exact path. Codex's own `config/read` API proves that the byte-exact invocation-scoped form is instead `-c 'projects={"/Users/colin/Projects/custom-skills/.worktrees/self-heal-pr-review-vendored-runtime"={trust_level="trusted"}}'`, with the exact target key and sessionFlags origin and no user-config write. The installed CAO provider cannot emit that safe form through `codexConfig`: its key validator rejects slashes/quotes and its serializer rejects dict/list values, accepting only scalar values. Therefore a one-off CAO reviewer profile cannot currently supply the proven exact-path override without changing the provider/config contract; do not approximate it with the malformed dotted form or a quoted scalar. Add source/unit/integration coverage for exact absolute paths containing dots, invocation-only lifetime, unchanged protected user config, rendered argv equality, trust-prompt suppression, and post-preflight provider/model-input readiness before task delivery. This is further evidence for existing cond-0073/W11, not a new issue or Fable recall.

Fresh parallel exact-head implementation reviews at conductor `e6f723e54df79c89a29890a7297de79962fbb7ab`, CAO fork `274ffc6d987ffb863068783b6bad62c1e9869f38`, and operative spec `b78b8845a90b4eda108482e279c17886c99856d8` independently returned BLOCKED with no P0. Their accepted P1 evidence remains within this existing W11 lifecycle issue and does not allocate duplicate IDs: (1) readiness and submission receipts are locally composed from a separate probe process, pane/status state, or successful paste rather than provider-native proof from the exact reserved generation; (2) terminal cleanup receives only the reusable terminal id and can delete a replacement incarnation despite an old reservation generation check; (3) managed Kimi still sends `s` into its update reminder instead of remaining zero-input/fail-closed; (4) recovery dead-ends across absent reservation, `reserved`/`launching`/`ready`, and breaker-begin crash windows because conductor does not drive the fork's negative/cancel protocol or safely forfeit a stale domain admission; (5) launch-domain re-attestation trusts caller-controlled `CAO_TERMINAL_ID`, accepts a forged/unset worker identity, and does not bind the full attested route including model/effort; (6) a created delivery journal omits immutable canonical worktree/session/lease/full-route bindings, allowing same-task reruns with changed identities; (7) source proof and the prepared packet do not bind the absolute executable/package actually invoked and inherit ambient PATH; (8) `collect --outcome blocked|failed` rejects a successfully `submitted` managed run, while recover makes no terminal transition, leaving its lease and obligation wedged; and (9) the named sentinel deadman owner cannot recover ordinary journals without `source_proof`, cannot correlate pre-terminal blocked runs, and lacks the durable first-seen/containment-clock path required for crash/restart. Independent probes and source locations are preserved in the two reports at `runs/self-heal-root-exact-head-review-sol-cao/report.md` and `runs/self-heal-root-exact-head-review-k3-cao/report.md`. Keep cond-0073 OPEN; require one coherent, crash-safe implementation correction and fresh exact-head parallel validation before any install, bootstrap gate, or canonical-validator retry.

Root hostile validation at fork `43257c11942e3bc1b99e83bff112b60dc31cc552` reproduced a remaining generation-race in `terminal_service.delete_terminal`. A deterministic mock changed the DB identity from the expected old generation to a replacement immediately before the final conditional delete. The function eventually raised `TerminalGenerationMismatchError`, but only after it had already called Herdr unregister, FIFO stop, status clear, old-window kill, and `provider_manager.cleanup_provider` using the reusable terminal id. The final row compare therefore detects the replacement too late to preserve its provider/FIFO/status resources. Bind provider, Herdr, FIFO, status, memory, window, and row cleanup to one exact generation-owned teardown claim, or recheck the immutable generation immediately before each destructive subsystem call with rollback-safe ownership. Add a race at every boundary and prove zero replacement-generation side effects, not merely row preservation.

**2026-07-23 Lane A validator lifecycle recurrence:** fresh exact-head validator task `self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-validator-sol-rerun-d567be8`, terminal `7a26f2db`, froze its independent matrix at conductor head `d567be826120b0bd7e553a30a47ff617556f8df3` but never produced `report.md` or a worker callback. Its manifest remained `assigned` while durable root-monitor evidence reported the terminal structurally completed. Sentinel deadman inbox row `715` was authoritatively delivered, and supervisor non-steering nudge `718` was sent exactly once; the absence of sentinel traffic from `conduct status` events is a view limitation, not a sentinel failure. The implementation worktree remained clean at the frozen SHA. A matrix file or terminal completion state must never count as task completion: only the bound worker-authored report/callback/finality contract may do so. Failed recovery must preserve artifacts, finalize only the exact dead generation, and permit one new task/generation without reusing its callback identity. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-validator-sol-rerun-d567be8/lifecycle-failure-evidence.md`. Keep cond-0073 OPEN through fresh exact-head validation and installed lifecycle acceptance.

**2026-07-23 fresh Lane A functional validation at `d567be826120b0bd7e553a30a47ff617556f8df3`:** the documented `--human-dead-ack` recovery path accepted a malformed W11 proof against an ACTIVE submitted generation, returned success, issued the conditional DELETE, and closed the journal. The proof supplied `finding=no-survivor` and omitted project/run/delivery/examined-at; collection validated only schema plus current digest rather than the required `no-io-attempted` finding, complete identity, lawful pre-I/O state, and absence of any `io-attempted`-or-later transition under the same journal lock. This is a P1 functional destructive-boundary failure: ordinary operator recovery can tear down live work. Validate every proof field and transition against locked current bytes, then re-hash immediately before DELETE; refuse before attaching the acknowledgement or claiming ownership. The same validation found the Stage-1 resource-registry exact-source inventory gate vacuous: its sole invocation scans the test fixture itself, while production `conduct`/plugin sources have no concrete Registry construction or registered recovery operation. This is P1 operability, not merely coverage—operators have no executable proof that real recovery resources are journaled, discoverable, and represented in the old-binary rig. Declare the exact non-empty production inventory and bind its scan/runtime registrations to preflight/deploy. Full evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-validator-sol-rerun-d567be8-recovery-1/report.md`. Keep cond-0073 OPEN pending correction and fresh full-matrix validation.

**2026-07-23 Lane A fixer admission recurrence:** fresh task `self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-fix-functional-p1-d567be8`, terminal `694a26c0`, was assigned at exact clean head `d567be826120b0bd7e553a30a47ff617556f8df3` but never entered model processing; task input was not accepted after retries and the terminal was deleted. The run contains only manifest/quota/task files, with no report or callback, and the repository stayed unchanged. Failed collection released the stale publishing lease before the human-directed fresh reassignment. Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-control-plane-recovery-lane-a-fix-functional-p1-d567be8/task-delivery-failure.md`. This is the same provider/model-input admission boundary already owned by cond-0073; do not allocate another issue or infer worker execution from assignment.

**2026-07-23 fresh Lane B functional validation at fork `6eeeafd1d3cdfc8a82f4b63fd49114edf86a2848`:** six independent production-wiring probes remain P1 and amend existing lifecycle owners rather than allocating new IDs. (1) Actor assertions cannot issue through the claimed generation-private bridge: its broker requires a provider-child peer, but only the conductor/bridge client has a UDS path, so report provenance always refuses. (2) Response loss after `session.admit` crosses the provider boundary leaves the delivery journal `terminal_queued`; production never calls `mark_submit_ambiguous`, so recovery is told no submission occurred. (3) generic `DELETE /terminals/{id}` bypasses the conditional destructive endpoint and can tear down an active v2 generation without heartbeat/fence/dual-exit containment. (4) legacy retention unlinks a live registry-owned v2 log by name/mtime while the registry remains `created`; the runtime manifest also omits required call-site/API-verb/constructor coverage. (5) capability negotiation enables Codex and all automated paths when identity exists but provider route proof is unsupported. issues.body: Gate request and approval are stored as independent fixed files keyed only by gate id. Rewriting a request under the same gate id does not invalidate or bind the prior approval, and gate check reports the new request approved. A retry can therefore authorize a different dossier or bootstrap attempt without fresh human review. Bind approvals to an immutable request digest/nonce, reject stale approvals, and atomically consume single-use gates; add request-overwrite, replay, and concurrent-check regressions.

The existing _release_lease(force=True) catches any task-owner mismatch from release_worktree_lease and calls force_release_worktree_lease on the branch. After exact negative recovery releases the old run and a replacement task acquires that branch, collecting the old failed run can therefore delete the replacement task’s live publishing lease. This violates the shared lease safety boundary and can permit concurrent writers. Fix in the active P-3/P-4 lane: failed collect may treat an absent lease as already released, but must fail closed on a different live owner; never force-release another task. Add an old-run cleanup -> replacement acquire -> old-run collect regression proving the replacement lease remains byte-identical.

**2026-07-22T21:50Z P0 exact-head reproduction at `9eb0b208c9560e13bff112b62f7aa0d81b2fbfed`:** the force fallback is removed, but the replacement lease remains deletable through incomplete identity. `release_worktree_lease(..., expected=None)` and `release_worktree_lease(..., expected={reservation_id: None, launch_generation: None, worktree: None, publishing_repo: None})` both returned `True` and removed a concrete same-task replacement lease carrying a different reservation, generation, canonical worktree, and publishing repository. In `conduct/lib/state.py`, comparisons run only when both the lease and expected values are non-null, so unknown caller identity acts as a wildcard. Missing `expected`, a missing expected field, or expected `None` must fail closed whenever the lease carries a concrete value; only a `None` value on the lease itself may represent the pre-binding form, and then every other owner field must still match exactly. Add direct regressions for omitted/partial/all-None expected identity and a collect/recovery regression with an old or incomplete manifest.


### 2026-07-23 final-conformance gate amendments to existing issues

Fresh independent exact-head gates reviewed conductor `f550369cb53037eb55e9dec565c0b83b7bedde41` and fork `e473d3b50eb307d1a6e179ec209aeb2bd3e58dcb`. The OpenAI lane completed entirely on GPT-5.6-sol/max and reproduced nine P1 blockers; the independent Kimi K3 lane reproduced one additional P1. These amend the existing issue owners below and allocate no duplicate IDs. Full evidence is preserved in:

- `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/runs/self-heal-final-conformance-revalidation-sol-f550369/report.md`

**cond-0055 / W8:** when a terminal is structurally `waiting_user_answer` but its prompt companion is absent, empty, or unknown, W8 returns after alerting without installing a generation-bound input hold; the same sentinel tick can then emit a deadman or pending-inbox input. Fork startup output reattachment separately sends `Enter` after pipe attachment without consulting prompt lifecycle or the W8 arbiter, and the executed probe sent it into a live `Additional safety checks` prompt. Establish the fail-closed exact-generation hold before every input producer on unknown/unavailable waiting state, and gate startup reattachment on the same arbiter plus an authoritative no-prompt observation.

**cond-0069 / W9:** route receipts omit the assigned agent profile, so an observed different profile with matching provider/model/effort becomes requested and stronger-verdict eligible. The companion also served an unknown-schema route record with a transport producer and missing generation/session/turn/version binding; generic provider errors can become refusal records without an allowlisted refusal kind. Require a versioned capability handshake and typed provider-native schemas that bind provider/profile/model/effective effort, generation, provider session/turn, and allowlisted producer kind. Unknown versions or missing identity fail closed.

**cond-0070 / W10:** the immediate callback lock and response-loss correction passes, but no production path reconciles a provider turn acknowledgement that arrives after the callback POST. Accepted callback records remain without `submitted_receipt` unless a worker manually runs `conduct report` again. Add a bounded generation-aware reconciler under the callback-record lock, apply the same strict receipt validator, and persist the late acknowledgement without replaying the callback POST.

**cond-0072 / model-turn boundary:** bridge delivery can cross the provider model-input boundary, lose its response, then fall back to tmux paste, producing one provider submission plus one duplicate paste because there is no message-bound intent/idempotency record. An `ok` bridge response naming the wrong message was accepted. Separately, conductor accepted a weak/stale turn receipt lacking allowlisted kind, provider, sender, submission time, and expected receiver generation; W8 closed a live prompt using only matching message IDs. Add durable intent-before-provider-I/O keyed by message id/digest and receiver generation, exact ambiguity reconciliation with no paste fallback/replay, and one strict validator shared by the bridge response, companion API, W10, W8, and W9.

**cond-0073 / W11 lifecycle and source binding:** fork teardown still has adjacent destructive operations without an intervening claim check: replacement generation B installed during `_memory_injected_terminals.discard()` had its `_curator_locks` entry removed before the later row mismatch was detected. Recheck before every distinct mutation or generation-key every subsystem entry. The source chain also accepts ambient PATH-first provider and tmux identities—`/bin/echo` was accepted as the pinned provider/tmux in independent probes—rather than deriving them from the deploy receipt. Bind provider, tmux, bridge interpreter, and verifier to canonical absolute paths and digests in the trusted deploy receipt and use no bare/PATH-resolved execution after the gate.

**cond-0076 / collection and recovery ownership:** old collection releases its lease before deleting the worktree-keyed shim route. A same-task replacement can acquire the worktree and register a new route in that interval, after which old cleanup deletes the replacement route/token directory. Route cleanup needs complete reservation/task/generation/worktree/repository compare-delete ownership and must precede or atomically compose with release. Independently, a hard-killed spawn in the pre-reservation window owns an exact never-bound lease with `launch_generation=None`; `spawn --recover` reaches cleaned finalization but incorrectly calls the generation-bound release, which correctly refuses `None` and wedges. Operator force-release writes no exact receipt, so retry also refuses. Use receipt-writing `rollback_unbound_worktree_lease` only for the proven never-bound self-owned identity; keep strict six-component release for bound generations.

**2026-07-26 post-reboot exact recurrence:** both failed cond-0132 native GLM admissions had reservation-absent, never-bound leases with `launch_generation=None`. `conduct spawn --recover` reached cleaned finalization but invoked strict generation-bound release and refused both identities. All named P0/P1 issues remain OPEN pending correction, a fresh independent exact-head validation pair, merged artifacts, and installed/live acceptance.

**cond-0073 task-delivery reproduction during the bounded final-gate fixer launch:** task `self-heal-final-gate-fix-k3-abd24d3`, terminal `7543ea20`, was assigned through the installed `conduct spawn` path but never entered model processing; input was not accepted after retries, the terminal was deleted, and no report or product mutation exists. This is another occurrence of the existing W11 provider/model-input admission failure, not a new issue ID. Treat any detected violation as a gate failure requiring preservation verification before worker output is accepted.

**2026-07-23 workspace-identity recurrence at conductor `d567be826120b0bd7e553a30a47ff617556f8df3`:** fresh independent validation proved `workspace_fp` gives identical aggregate fingerprints to materially different workspaces. It emits a fully untracked/ignored directory once and stops recursion, so changing a nested untracked file from `first` to `second` left the aggregate unchanged. Its index-v3 parser consumes but discards the extended-flags word, so clearing `CE_SKIP_WORKTREE` while retaining the same primary flags and a valid index checksum also left the aggregate unchanged. This is P1 core usability: checkpoint/admission can accept a workspace that is not the frozen workspace the operator approved. A real `conduct checkpoint` followed by same-HEAD nested-untracked drift changed the aggregate from `d7e57b…` to `1bfa0b…`, yet production resume still classified it `current`. This leaves the core checkpoint feature unusable for its intended safety boundary. Under the existing lease/journal read locks, read the bound checkpoint, capture the current canonical fingerprint, compare both HEAD and `fingerprint_aggregate_sha256`, and feed mismatch into the existing write-role `ahead`/`ambiguous-preserved` refusal. An absent live publishing lease is synthesized from journal/worktree fallbacks into a matching identity and returns `current`/`resumed` despite no lease authority. Malformed checkpoint or lease JSON raises raw `JSONDecodeError` rather than a structured refusal. issues.body:
A successfully launched managed Kimi worker displays the raw ACP JSON-RPC stream
in its dashboard terminal pane instead of a readable, human-operable Kimi
worker interface.

Exact reproduction:

- terminal `44dda40b`, pane `%247`
- pane process:
  `python -I -m cli_agent_orchestrator.services.managed_provider_bridge`
- provider child:
  `@moonshot-ai/kimi-code ... acp`
- visible output consists of `session/update`, tool-call, thought, and content
  JSON records.

The worker is healthy and actively executing. CAO `send_message` delivery is
provider-native for this managed terminal: the inbox service asks the managed
bridge to submit a `session/prompt` to the same Kimi ACP session. That supports
supervisor follow-up turns, but it does not make the visible pane interactive.
A human cannot type or paste a follow-up, issue `/compact`, use the model or
reasoning menus, cancel a live turn, or otherwise operate the worker from the
terminal surface. The raw JSON stream also makes ordinary visual monitoring
impractical. This is incompatible with persistent, steerable CAO workers.

ACP is required internally for exact readiness, session, and delivery receipts,
so the fix must not replace the managed transport with an unverified ordinary
TUI launch. Managed launches must retain ACP as the underlying control channel
while providing a readable human-facing terminal or companion control surface
that accepts normal follow-up input and maps required lifecycle operations
(including cancel, compaction, model/effort changes, and resume/handoff where
the provider supports them) to provider-native ACP operations with durable
receipts. Unsupported operations must be surfaced explicitly rather than
silently accepted.

Severity: P1. Do not launch additional managed workers through a raw,
non-interactive ACP pane. The already-running bounded cond-0085 fixer may finish
without interruption, but this must be resolved before Lane C or the chess
shakedown launches more managed workers.

### Evidence amendment — 2026-07-24: structured nudge response loss

At the sentinel 45-minute deadman for the same active bounded worker
`44dda40b`, the supervisor sent exactly one CAO MCP `send_message` nudge to
the exact terminal. The request timed out at the loopback API after 30 seconds:
`HTTPConnectionPool(host='127.0.0.1', port=9889): Read timed out (read
timeout=30.0)`. Its enqueue/delivery/submission outcome is therefore ambiguous;
no retry, raw terminal/pane input, restart, collection, or replacement occurred.
Evidence: `/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/campaign-inputs/cond-0089-managed-uds-nudge-timeout-2026-07-24.md`.

This is same-P1 functional control-path evidence: the human-operable semantic
surface must give every generation/session-bound operation a bounded,
queryable receipt/outcome (`queued|submitted|accepted|completed|refused|ambiguous`)
and response-loss reconciliation that fails closed without duplicate provider
input. Raw ACP/tmux input cannot be a fallback.

### Evidence amendment — 2026-07-24: response loss killed the bridge

The one deadman `send_message` occurred while Kimi turn 0 was active. Kimi
returned `turn.agent_busy`; after the supervisor's API timeout, the bridge's
late response hit `BrokenPipe`. That exception escaped the per-connection
boundary, marked the bridge blocked, and terminated terminal `44dda40b`.
The nudge outcome is ambiguous; its worktree/session evidence is preserved and
no collection/delete/respawn/retry/raw fallback occurred. Evidence:
`/Users/colin/.local/state/cao-conductor/cao-conductor-self-heal/campaign-inputs/cond-0089-managed-bridge-operator-disconnect-termination-2026-07-24.md`.

The same P1 now explicitly requires per-connection exception containment:
busy/refusal, response loss, client disconnect, late response/BrokenPipe, and
serialization failures produce durable exact-operation ambiguous/refused or
terminal records with typed alerts, never a bridge crash/block/worker
termination or blind retry. Reconciliation must prove bridge liveness for a
later lawful operation under the same exact generation identity.
