issues.body:
The read-only inventory command refuses to emit the inventory whenever a disposition is required, and the disposition file cannot be written without the digests that inventory carries. When the gate is armed there is no supported way through it.

## Proven 2026-08-17

    conduct deploy --repo /Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor --inventory-retained-v1
    -> exit 1
    -> {"ok": false, "error": {"failure_class": "deployment-failed",
        "message": "15 parked v1 retained track(s) require exactly one operator disposition each",
        "safe_next_actions": ["write the disposition file from this exact inventory and pass --retained-v1-dispositions <absolute path>"],
        "details": ["aegix-mobile-phase0-renewal/p0-09b-rebase-refresh-spec-r1", ...]}}

    grep -c sha256 <that output>  ->  0

The action it names is "write the disposition file from this exact inventory". It does not print that inventory. `details` carries only `project/task_id` strings.

## The cycle

`conduct/lib/deploy_inventory.py:validate_dispositions` requires each row to carry `track_sha256` (:482) and `execution_mode_migration_sha256` (:485), and the file to carry `inventory_sha256` (:453). Those values exist only in the inventory document.

`conduct/commands/deploy.py:2720 _run_retained_v1_inventory` is the command that prints that document. It calls `_retained_v1_preflight` first (:2721), which raises at :2698 when `supplied is None`:

    supplied = _load_dispositions(getattr(args, "retained_v1_dispositions", None))
    if not parked:
        return result                 # <- :2696, prints only when nothing is parked
    if supplied is None:
        raise ConductorError(...)     # <- :2698, before :2722 can print anything

So the print at :2722 is reachable only when `parked` is empty - exactly when the operator does not need the inventory. Whenever a disposition IS required, the command raises before printing the values required to write one.

To supply dispositions you need the inventory. To see the inventory you must already have supplied dispositions.

## Impact, observed

The p1-closure supervisor merged PR #121 at exact head 509e0ef (merge commit 47b90150), advanced the deployment source to origin/main, and was held here. It correctly refused to reuse the stale approval file or fabricate one, and parked. It was right to: there was no supported path, so no amount of supervisor resourcefulness could have produced one. Deployment and final implementer retirement have been held since. The same gate blocks every campaign in the installation, because the inventory is installation-wide (15 tracks across aegix-mobile-phase0-renewal, dnd-scheduler and p1-closure).

The docstring at :2659 calls this "the read-only §10 inventory" and :2667 states "Every hold here is unconditional... an override would reintroduce exactly the silent stranding this gate exists to prevent." The hold is correct. What is missing is the releasing half: the operator-facing read that makes the hold satisfiable.

## Fix

Make `--inventory-retained-v1` do what its name and the safe_next_action promise: emit the full inventory including `inventory_sha256`, and per parked track its `sha256` and `execution_mode_migration_sha256`, with exit 0, regardless of whether a disposition file was supplied. It is a read; it performs no install, mutation, or approval, and it grants no authority - `validate_dispositions` still fences every decision on the deploy path.

Concretely: `_run_retained_v1_inventory` must not go through the `supplied is None` raise. Either give the inventory path its own build+print that skips the disposition requirement, or pass a flag so the requirement is enforced only on the install path (:2783), which is where it is actually load-bearing.

Emitting a disposition TEMPLATE - one row per parked track, digests filled in, `disposition` and `reason` left empty - would reduce the operator's step to filling in decisions. That is evidence-gathering, not approval.

## Guard that must NOT move

The disposition requirement on the deploy path itself, and the second preflight immediately before install (:2661-2665) which re-validates against the inventory taken at install time. Those are correct. This issue is only that the operator-facing READ is gated on the thing it exists to produce.

## Test

Assert `conduct deploy --inventory-retained-v1` exits 0 and its output carries `inventory_sha256` plus a per-track `sha256` for every parked track, in an installation that HAS parked v1 tracks and NO disposition file. Mutation-test: restore the raise and the assertion goes red. Add a second test asserting the install path still refuses with no dispositions, so the fix cannot be mistaken for removing the gate - and confirm that one goes red independently.

Related: cond-0468 (the whole-inventory digest voids every disposition on unrelated drift). Both must land for the gate to be satisfiable in practice: this one makes an approval writable, cond-0468 makes it survive long enough to spend.

Template rows (:2860-2869) carry track_sha256, execution_mode_migration_sha256 and execution_mode_classification with disposition/reason blank. `python -m unittest tests.test_retained_v1_inventory_command` -> Ran 13 tests, OK. | The chicken-and-egg is gone and both guards the issue said must not move are intact: the install path still refuses without dispositions, and the second preflight still re-validates against the inventory taken at install time. The comment-252 acceptance note ('the emitted output must be sufficient to write a valid file with NO other source of information') is met by the pre-populated disposition_template. Related cond-0468 landed in the same commit. | Vetted 2026-08-17 against origin/main 1f0b8a6 in an 8-agent sweep of all 64 open P0/P1 issues; every remove/soften recommendation was independently spot-checked against source.

issues.body:
Task/goal PR 9A shipped the communication catalog store, capture library, reader CLI, quarantine
verb, `conduct report` producer seam, and legacy backfill (merged `6271cd9`, `cond-0438`). It did
**not** ship the operator-safe publication projection, which the plan assigns to the same slice:

> **PR 9A — conductor communication ledger/capture.** ... publish a safe catalog projection, and
> backfill only provable legacy records.

And the design (§7, "Operator-safe publication and API"):

> The conductor publishes a versioned presentation index plus immutable content objects under its
> fixed state root. Publication does not expose canonical store internals.

This is a prerequisite for **PR 9B**, the fork's bounded catalog API, which by design *"never opens
the conductor database"* (§3, §7) and reads the published projection with the same confinement
posture as the existing annotation reader.

## Root cause

The projection was cut from the PR 9A implementation brief during coordination, under a YAGNI
assessment that read `export_projection()` as "a second authority with no consumer in this PR." Both
halves were wrong: it is the design's specified publication boundary rather than a parallel
authority, and its consumer is the immediately following slice. The simplicity mandate asks whether
a construct earns its place in this PR; a deliverable the plan assigns to this PR earns it by
assignment, and that check was not made against the plan text.

## Scope

Publish, under the conductor's fixed state root:

- a **versioned presentation index** and **immutable content objects**, exposing no canonical store
  internals (no raw table shapes, no internal row ids beyond the opaque identifiers the reader needs);
- content addressed by the opaque identifiers `conduct communication show` / `conduct attachment read`
  already use, so the CLI and the projection agree;
- digests carried alongside content so the fork can verify before serving;
- coverage typed as `complete | partial | truncated | unavailable`;
- correct handling of quarantined blobs — a quarantined document must publish its tombstone metadata
  and must never publish bytes; and
- republication that is idempotent and safe to run repeatedly.

## Out of scope

The fork API (9B), the dashboard viewer (9C), the project-wide view (9D), and any change to the
catalog store's schema or invariants. This adds a publisher; it does not alter what is stored.

*Surface:* gate journal / approval CLI.

*Surface:* communication catalog / operator repair verb.
The loop in `conduct/lib/communication_store.py:1043-1108` runs on an autocommit connection (`goal_store.py:1195`), so each cleared document commits before the next is attempted. If any document's blob was already quarantined (routine when two leaks are reported separately, given content-addressed dedup), `communication_blob_quarantine_once` (`goal_store.py:711-725`) aborts the whole command mid-loop: earlier documents are cleared, later ones still hold their secrets, no receipt is printed, and `cli.py:118-125` re-raises the bare `sqlite3.IntegrityError`. issues.body:
*Surface:* communication catalog / content lifecycle.
`_insert_blob` is content-addressed on sha256 with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (`conduct/lib/communication_store.py:106-135`), so two communications capturing identical bytes share one blob. Quarantining either clears `content` on the shared blob and writes only the blob row; the other communication's `communication_document` keeps `content_state='present'` with sha256 and byte_size, its own CHECK still passes, and the receipt reports `quarantined_count: 1 / untouched_count: 0`. `read_communication` then reports the body as present while `read_attachment` on the same document refuses with "blob is unavailable". The `content-quarantined` enum member the document schema declares is written only by the *re-capture* path (`communication_store.py:540-560`), never by quarantine; `communication_document_no_update` (`goal_store.py:754`) refuses the correction, `_no_delete` (`:756`) refuses removal, and re-running quarantine on the collateral communication refuses for every input forever because the once-guard requires `old.content IS NOT NULL`. issues.body:
Severity: P1. Repository: `cli-agent-orchestrator`. Found by a post-merge combined-state audit of fork `04adf876`, which was run specifically because cond-0433's hold change and cond-0439/0440/0441's state-machine change never coexisted until merge. Two findings survived independent refutation out of eight candidates.

## The defect

cond-0441 made two of the three recipient-pane columns roster-**established**. The transfer 250 lines away still checks only the one column it did not change.

- Gate: `services/task_handoff.py:1175` — `if incarnation.incarnation_id != row.to_incarnation_id:`
- Write: `task_handoff.py:1250-1257` — `occurrence.open_occurrence(OpenRequest(..., incarnation=incarnation, ...))`, where `incarnation` is the **caller's** object
- Persisted verbatim: `services/task_occurrence.py:670-672`
- The roster-verified copy that is ignored: `task_handoff.py:985-986` (`to_terminal_id`, `to_generation`), written from the roster-corrected incarnation in the same seam cond-0441 fixed (`:881-892`, `:909-918`)

The handoff row holds the authoritative triple. `_complete_once` reads one field of it and takes the other two from the caller's body, which `api/task_handoff.py:238-243` accepts as four independent fields and validates against nothing.

## Cooperative failure sequences

Reproduced by execution against `04adf876`.

**Face A — a retired pane is stamped, and the CAS makes stamping it mandatory.** Handoff pending, recipient roster-bound at `(inc-B, term-2, gen-2)`. Delivery runs; cond-0441 verifies against the roster and records `to_incarnation_id=inc-B`. Ordinary lost-pane recovery — the steady state this module's own docstrings describe — retires `(term-2, gen-2)` and rebinds the same agent at `(inc-C, term-2, gen-3)`. The supervisor calls `complete_handoff`. Passing live evidence (`inc-C`) is **refused** by `:1175`, so `inc-B` is the only completable value. The successor occurrence carries an incarnation the roster reports `retired`. No caller error is required — the refusal forces the stale value.

**Face B — a foreign live pane is accepted.** The body carries `incarnation_id=inc-B, terminal_id=term-9, generation=gen-9`, where `term-9` is another worker's live binding. `:1175` compares only `incarnation_id`, so the successor is stamped onto a pane the roster binds elsewhere.

**Face C (P3, separated deliberately) — the correction is discarded wholesale.** A caller that copies only `to_incarnation_id` out of the delivery response writes a handoff row saying `gen-new` and a successor occurrence saying `gen-old` **inside one transaction**. Two durable records contradicting each other about the physical pane. Graded P3 rather than P1 because `to_terminal_id`/`to_generation` have no reader today (`receipt_digest` at `:558-585` covers neither), so nothing consumes the divergence — a record-integrity defect, not currently a corruption path.

## State-integrity impact

Faces A and B are P1 because the wrong `incarnation_id` has a live consumer. `services/supervisor_worker_ops.py:363` `_predecessor_occurrence` — whose docstring says the recorded `incarnation_id` "is the durable name of the pane that was lost, which is what lets a retry tell 'this agent is still on the dead pane' from 'a previous attempt already launched its replacement'" — feeds the gate at `:427`.

Measured against a control: with a correct stamp `admit_fresh_successor` returns `launch`; with the Face-A stamp it returns `adopt-incarnation`, skipping the `DISPOSITION_LOST` finalize and the `retire_incarnation`. That is the orphaned-pane / duplicate-launch harm the branch's own comment names. No verb rewrites `TaskOccurrenceModel.incarnation_id` after `_open_once`, so the misstamp is permanent for that occurrence.

## Smallest coherent repair

In `_complete_once`, resolve the transfer against the row rather than the caller:

- keep the `incarnation_id` CAS at `:1175`;
- build the `EffectIncarnation` passed to `open_occurrence` from `row.to_incarnation_id / row.to_terminal_id / row.to_generation`.

That closes Faces B and C outright and makes Face A's stamp self-consistent rather than merely permitted.

**Do not loosen `:1175` to accept live evidence.** A refutation pass confirmed that path opens the successor on a pane the roster binds elsewhere.

## Acceptance criterion

Not "the row is now read". A test must fail if the successor occurrence's `terminal_id` or `generation` can diverge from the handoff row's roster-verified copies. Note that the two landing tests for cond-0441's roster ladder (`test/services/test_task_handoff.py:799` and neighbour) both call `complete_handoff` and assert **only** `successor_occurrence["incarnation_id"]` — never the two fields cond-0441 actually made roster-established. A test asserting the full triple would have failed on Face C the day cond-0441 landed.

## Deferred design question — file separately, do not decide inside this repair

Whether a transfer to a pane the roster has since retired should be refused at all, given `docs/session-lifecycle.md`'s rule that "a replaced recipient is a rollback and a new handoff, never a transfer". The audit verified that *loosening* `:1175` is wrong; it did not establish that *tightening* it is right. That is a call for the M3-E owner.

## Why no single-PR review could have seen it

Both `to_terminal_id`/`to_generation` and the one-field gate existed at `f8f60f64` (PR #126), in a world where all three columns were one caller assertion — comparing `incarnation_id` alone was sufficient *by construction*, with nothing to diverge from. cond-0439/0440/0441 (PR #129) made two of the three roster-established for the first time but did not touch `_complete_once`, so its reviewer saw the delivery write it changed and had no reason to re-derive whether a downstream consumer still held. Honest qualifier: the unchanged half predates today, so this is a cross-*change* composition rather than strictly a cross-*merge-pair* one. It is unreachable in either PR's world and is not covered by any of the 91 merged tests.

## Catalogued patterns this is an instance of

- **"A test that proves an ingredient without proving the wiring."** The correction is proven; its survival through the transfer is not.
- **"A precondition checked once is an assumption for the rest of its window."** The roster check fires on the delivery write and is never re-run, while the roster moving between delivery and transfer *is* the ordinary lost-pane recovery path. `_complete_once` re-reads nothing, despite the module importing `stable_agent_roster` 250 lines earlier.

## Verification caveat carried from the audit

Face A's forced-stale claim assumes a retrying supervisor client that does not exist yet — no conductor code calls `complete_handoff`, and the only non-test caller is the fork's own HTTP route at `api/task_handoff.py:200`. The sequence is reachable through the API and the CAS genuinely forces the stale value, but the retrying caller is projected from the design rather than observed in a shipped client. If the eventual client rebuilds the whole triple from `_row_dict`, Face C never fires; Faces A and B still do.
issues.title: complete_handoff admits the transfer on incarnation_id alone, discarding cond-0441's roster verification and stamping the successor from an unverified caller assertion

issues.body:
Severity: P4. Repository: `cao-conductor`. Found by the post-merge combined-state audit of conductor `b7472ecf`.

## The defect

`conduct/lib/marshal_probe.py` sets `report["run_dir"] = run_dir` only on the success path (`:827`). Nine bare returns precede it (`:762, :766, :775, :791, :799, :807, :815, :821, :823`). Three of them — `:815, :821, :823` — discard a run directory they **already know**.

The consumer at `:1353-1357` carries a comment at `:1350-1352` stating that `run_dirs` "matters most on a REFUSED paid run, which otherwise leaves them a refusal string and no way to reach the transcript they just paid for." For the one producer that spends a second paid turn, that stated purpose is unmet.

## Sequence

Reproduced with the real `harness_launcher` against `scripts/marshal-probe-fixture-harness.sh`, wrapped so only the RESUME leg sets `FIXTURE_NO_REPORT=1`.

The resume leg launches, the provider turn runs to completion **and bills**, `$RUN_DIR/exit_code` appears, the harness writes no report, control reaches `:815`. cond-0443's `resume-launcher-error` refusal fires (`:965-978`). Result:

```
run_dirs = {"launch": ".../20260817-154844-7802-27829", "resume": null}
```

Two run directories on disk; the second is named nowhere in the result. The refusal detail names only `report_path`, which both legs share.

## Impact — deliberately graded P4

There is **no** state-integrity impact. cond-0443 correctly preserves the prior receipt and nothing enters an illegal state.

It is also not "no way back": every real launcher places run dirs as timestamp-ordered siblings under one root (`claude-headless.sh:176`, `kimi-headless.sh:178`), and `run_dirs["launch"]` is populated, so `ls $(dirname <launch run_dir>)` reaches the paid transcript in one command.

Only three of the nine shapes discard a *known* run_dir; five never had one, and `:807` embeds it in prose. Under this repository's AGENTS.md bar this is a diagnosability nit, reported only because the mechanism's own stated purpose is unmet for the producer that costs money.

## Repair

Carry `run_dir` into the three late `launcher_error` dicts at `:815, :821, :823`. One line each.

## Why no single-PR review could have seen it

`run_dirs` landed in `b5677d0`; the resume-leg refusal in `f7211d9` (cond-0443). Before cond-0443 every refusal fired on the launch leg, whose run_dir *does* survive, so the docstring's promise was kept for every existing producer. Visible only by reading the launcher adapter's nine return shapes — untouched by PR #173 — against the new producer in the same file's scoring function.
issues.title: the resume-leg refusal cannot deliver its run_dir: three late launcher_error returns drop a run directory they already know

issues.body:
Severity: P1. Repository: `cli-agent-orchestrator`. Found while investigating cond-0432. Directly affects M8, whose only action is a single-line nudge.

## The asymmetry

`services/claude_native_control.py` refuses a **multi-line** composer write when no composer-newline pin is proven for the installed build, and silently degrades a **single-line** one.

- `:321-335` — `undeliverable` is set only `if len(lines) > 1 and pin is None`.
- `:356` — `"submit_settle_seconds": 0.0 if pin is None else float(pin["submit_settle_seconds"])`.
- `:359` — `"deliverable": undeliverable is None`.

So a single-line payload on an unpinned build is `deliverable: True` with a **zero** settle.

## Why zero is not a neutral default

The comment immediately above the pin table (`:130-136`) states the reason the value exists:

> `submit_settle_seconds` is not padding. The Ink renderer is already known in this codebase to swallow an Enter that arrives too soon, leaving the message sitting unsubmitted in the prompt box **with no error** — see `ClaudeCodeProvider.paste_submit_delay`, whose 2.0s was chosen from that observed behaviour.

The fallback therefore selects the one value the surrounding documentation says causes a silent non-delivery, on precisely the builds where nothing has been verified.

`codex_native_control.py:363` has the identical `0.0 if pin is None` shape and should be checked against the same reasoning.

## Cooperative failure sequence

A worker halts on a recognised provider error. M8's only initial action is one static submission — `Continue your current task.` — a **single line**. On a build with no composer pin, the plan is built `deliverable: True` with `settle=0.0`, the text is typed, Enter is sent too early, Ink swallows it, and the nudge sits unsubmitted in the composer with no error raised.

Layer 1 then observes no model turn, and the recovery ladder concludes the nudge was ineffective — when in fact it was never submitted. Every downstream signal is consistent with "the model ignored the nudge," which is the wrong diagnosis and drives the wrong escalation. The accepted design counts *ineffective* nudges against a budget; an unsubmitted nudge burns that budget without ever reaching the model.

This is the exact failure mode the pinned settle exists to prevent, reachable by default on any build not in the pin table.

## Why the multi-line half is right and worth copying

The multi-line refusal is well built and its comment is explicit about why it refuses rather than improvising: splitting across turns, pasting, and flattening newlines are each "a way of appearing to deliver something that was not delivered." A zero settle on a single line is the same class of thing — appearing to deliver — and it is the case the guard does not cover.

## Proposed repair

Treat a missing pin as undeliverable for **any** line count, or supply a conservative non-zero settle floor and record on the plan that the value is a floor rather than proven evidence. Do not leave a proven-evidence field carrying an unproven value; per this repository's rules a mechanism records only what it established, and `submit_settle_seconds: 0.0` alongside `composer_evidence: None` currently asserts a timing that nothing verified.

Prefer the refusal if either is contentious: a typed refusal is answerable by exact id, while a swallowed Enter is not observable at all.

## Open question, not resolved here

**Is the zero-settle path reachable after cond-0432 removes 2.1.233 from `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`?** If the upstream advanced-authority gate prevents an unsupported version from ever reaching the composer-plan builder, this is latent rather than live, and its severity drops accordingly. If any path reaches a composer write for a version outside the pin table, it is live. That reachability trace is the first thing to establish, and it decides whether this is P1 or a latent trap for the next version someone adds.

Either way the asymmetry is worth closing, because the next build added to the pin-less set reopens it silently.
issues.resolution: [ALREADY-FIXED] cli-agent-orchestrator commit d8f69ae7 'fix(native-control): floor an unproven build submit settle at the longest proven interval (#134)', confirmed an ancestor of origin/main via `git merge-base --is-ancestor d8f69ae7 origin/main`. In `git show origin/main:src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/claude_native_control.py`: :164 `_SUBMIT_SETTLE_FLOOR_SECONDS = max(float(entry["submit_settle_seconds"]) for entry in _PROVEN_COMPOSER_NEWLINE.values())`, :369-370 `"submit_settle_seconds": (_SUBMIT_SETTLE_FLOOR_SECONDS if pin is None else float(pin["submit_settle_seconds"]))`, :377 `"submit_settle_proven": pin is not None`. | The `0.0 if pin is None` shape the issue named is gone from all four adapters, replaced by a floor computed from each provider's own pin table so it rises as proofs land, and the plan now carries `submit_settle_proven` so a floor is recorded as a floor rather than as evidence — which the issue's own comment 257 confirms has a real reader at operator_message_service.py:1138. Comment 257 also corrected the severity to latent (the zero-settle plan was constructed but never executed, and the M8 nudge string does not exist in the repository), so nothing live was ever swallowed. The ordering argument that made it worth landing first — that the version-unpinning work removes exactly the gates keeping it latent — was satisfied: the floor landed at d8f69ae7 and the unpin policy at 43812413 immediately after. This is the correct shape under the version-allowlist rule: no build is excluded, an unproven build proceeds on the safe end of the observed range rather than on the null value. | Vetted 2026-08-17 against origin/main 1f0b8a6 in an 8-agent sweep of all 64 open P0/P1 issues; every remove/soften recommendation was independently spot-checked against source.

issues.body:
Severity: P2. Repositories: `cli-agent-orchestrator` (provider contracts and the per-feature tables), `cao-conductor` (M18 quarantine verb, filed separately). Operator direction, 2026-08-17.

Policy: `docs/provider-version-policy.md` (fork). Locked decisions and M18: the fire-marshal remaining-work plan. Agent-facing short form: `AGENTS.md` in both repos.

## The direction

Unpinned is the correct default state for every harness. A pin is a temporary incident artifact, not a normal update policy. New harness builds bring capability far more often than they break the narrow slice this system drives, so withholding a feature until a build is proven costs more than it protects.

The existing design already unpins **launch** (`VERSION_ENFORCEMENT_OPEN`) while keeping **capability** allowlist-gated and fail-closed until a build is proven. That split is what this issue removes.

## Scope: convert six surfaces from gate to override

Each currently withholds a capability when the installed build is absent from a table. Each must instead select a conservative default and proceed.

| surface | current | target |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` | gates native control, rendered-session proof, steer/composer, image, resume, route authority | not a capability gate; retained only as the strict-mode quarantine set |
| `_PROVEN_COMPOSER_NEWLINE` | absence withholds multi-line delivery, and yields `submit_settle_seconds: 0.0` for single-line | override with a **safe floor**, never zero — see cond-0480 |
| `_PROVEN_STEER_CHORDS` | absence withholds steer authority | override with a conservative default |
| `_RENDERED_SESSION_PROVEN_BUILDS` | absence withholds rendered-session proof | override; unproven records as unproven rather than withholding |
| `IMAGE_PROVEN_BUILDS` | absence withholds image authority | override with a conservative default |
| `PINNED_VERSIONS` | advisory head of each tuple | advisory only, everywhere |

**Not in scope, and they stay:** `NATIVE_BIND_CAPABLE_VERSIONS` and the Muse profile-carrier cell. Those are the case where no safe default exists — there is no way to pretend a session is resumable, and degrading silently would produce a launch that cannot resume itself. They fail closed on one operation while the rest of the provider stays open, which is what the policy permits.

## The rule that makes this safe, and the trap

**Conservative means the safe end of the range, never the null value.** Choosing zero, empty, or "no delay" because nothing was proven converts an absent measurement into a silent failure.

This repository already contains that defect, filed as **cond-0480**: a build with no composer pin receives `submit_settle_seconds: 0.0` against a renderer whose own in-tree comment says it "is already known in this codebase to swallow an Enter that arrives too soon, leaving the message sitting unsubmitted in the prompt box with no error." cond-0480 must land as part of or before this work — converting `_PROVEN_COMPOSER_NEWLINE` to an override while the fallback is still zero would generalise the defect from one build to every unpinned build.

For each of the six surfaces, the conservative default must be **chosen and justified individually**. This is not a bulk find-and-replace, and the null value is wrong for all of them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A build absent from every per-feature table still launches, binds where §6 permits, delivers assignments, receives steer and operator messages, and carries route authority.
- No per-feature table's absence yields a timing of zero or an empty required set.
- A test fails if any conservative default is the null value for its type.
- A test fails if a capability is withheld solely because a version is unlisted, for any surface outside the §6 exception.
- `strict` mode still refuses an unlisted build at the launch boundary, and the runtime lever `CAO_PROVIDER_VERSION_ENFORCEMENT_<PROVIDER>` still switches modes without a deploy.
- Unparseable version banners still raise `ProviderVersionDrift`. Unparseable is a failed observation, distinct from unlisted, which is merely nothing written down.

## Test-shape warning

The four assertions that keep fork main red today are the exact-set tests (`test_pinned_versions`, `test_the_advertised_versions_are_an_exact_set`, `test_capability_handshake_is_exact_and_versioned`, `test_a_drifted_claude_build_is_refused`). They were **correct** — they detected an unproven build receiving advanced authority.

Under this direction they are asking the wrong question, because exact-set membership stops being the authority. Do not simply update their expected values. Rewrite them to pin the new contract: that an unlisted build gets capability with a safe default, that strict mode still quarantines, and that no default is null. A hand-maintained set frozen beside a derived one is a gate that decays; assert the pairing in both directions or derive the baseline.

## Related

- **cond-0480** — the zero-settle defect; a prerequisite in practice.
- **cond-0432** — the four exact-set failures. Its committed repair on `fix/cond0432-claude-version-set` drops Claude 2.1.233 from the accepted set, which is the opposite of this direction and should be **superseded, not merged**. Its rewrite of `test_a_drifted_claude_build_is_refused` — open mode attests and records a drift, strict refuses, unparseable refused in every mode — is correct and worth keeping.
- **M18** — the marshal quarantine verb, which depends on this landing first: a quarantine and a capability allowlist disagree about what an unlisted build means.
issues.title: unpin harness versions across the board: convert six capability allowlists to overrides with conservative defaults

issues.body:
Severity: P2. Repository: `cli-agent-orchestrator`. Operator direction: strive to un-pin everything, because an un-pinned harness is what having a stable way to use it looks like. Policy: `docs/provider-version-policy.md` §6 (PR #133).

Replaces the last two capability allowlists with runtime self-proof. Research lane findings below; every claim is traceable to the cited code.

## The finding that decides it

**No build has ever failed the Codex bootstrap contract.** Git history, PR/issue records, docs, and tests were checked. Every recorded negative is a CAO-side refusal of an untested build, never a failed exchange:

- **0.147.0 succeeded** at bootstrap and was then refused at bind by the broad table (`25a823f2`, PR #117 — "completed the zero-turn bootstrap, exposed the exact provider session identity, reported `input_ready`, and was then refused at bind"). Same pattern at route attestation (`ecbe4266`, PR #118). The bootstrap worked on a build the table did not list.
- **0.146.1** was never bootstrap-tested — it appears only as a fail-closed fixture and as the error-corpus binary.
- **0.148.0** was never tried — a hypothetical fixture only.

So the enumeration has only ever refused builds nobody tested. That is the expiry-date failure mode §1 of the policy describes, not a guard.

**The gate also prevents its own evidence.** `_validate_binary` (`codex_native_bootstrap.py:93`) fires *before* the probe, so on an unlisted build the proof is never attempted. Removing the gate and letting the exchange stand or fail on its own results reduces the table to a cache at most.

**The table's only advantage over self-proof is that a human once ran it** — an audit-trail property, not a correctness property. The TUI-side `codex … resume <id>` rendering, which is the actual consumer of the guarantee, is caught by neither: the visual smoke was explicitly deferred (`codex_native_bootstrap.py:47-48`).

## A defect found on the way

The documented contract claims a "fresh `thread/resume` adopting the same UUID," but **no code path ever calls `thread/resume`.** It exists only as a comment claim; the stage transcripts are not in the repo. The guarantee the allowlist exists to protect is therefore unverified in code — prose asserting an invariant nothing enforces.

A second app-server process calling `thread/resume` on the minted id is zero-turn and costs nothing. Closing that gap is part of this work, not a follow-up.

## Codex: two-layer self-proof, then delete the gate

1. **Shape probe**, cheap, cached per binary SHA-256: `codex app-server generate-json-schema --out <tmp>`, then assert the required methods and fields exist (`config/read`, `thread/start` params/response, `thread/name/set`, `thread/resume`). Zero sessions, zero network. A missing element refuses with a typed reason naming it. The digest is already computed in `_validate_binary`.
2. **Behavioural proof**: drop `is_bootstrap_capable_build` from `_validate_binary`, keep every postcondition assertion, and add the second-process `thread/resume` leg asserting `result.thread.id == minted id`. Cache the digest-level verdict; the per-launch mint already runs.

The shape probe alone is insufficient and the behavioural leg is what covers the gap: a semantics change that keeps field names (say `ephemeral=false` silently treated as ephemeral) passes the schema and fails the rollout-materialization assertion.

Fail direction stays closed — any failed leg refuses with a typed reason naming the leg. TUI resume rendering stays an installed-E2E follow-up rather than a launch gate, which is its status today anyway.

## Muse: behavioural echo-probe, replace banner-plus-digest

The pin cannot survive a vendor update by construction, and the mechanism guarantees churn: `~/.local/bin/muse` is a self-updating bash wrapper that checks hourly (its `.muse-update-checked-at` was touched today), downloads `muse-bin-<revision>`, **prunes old inner binaries**, and selects via `.muse-version`.

What the carrier actually needs (`muse_native_launch.py:67-97`): the env-addressed file `TBH_EVAL_APPEND_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE` must be read and its exact bytes become the session's base instructions on the meta provider, including across an exact `muse resume <id>`.

The probe, already documented in the code comments:

1. Resolve the inner binary as today (`.muse-version` → `muse-bin-<revision>`, `MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`) — this is exactly the binary a probe exercises, which answers the standing objection that the update-capable launcher script is never evidence.
2. Write a sentinel profile file, launch `muse --provider echo` with `TBH_EVAL_APPEND_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE` set. **Pass = the refusal `provider does not support base instructions`.** Positive control: `--preset miniswe` produces the same refusal. Negative control: an echo launch with `--agents <JSON>` runs a clean turn.
3. Cache per inner SHA-256 and record the cell as *probed*, with the probe transcript digest, rather than pinned.

The echo provider is local and deterministic (`--provider echo`, `--echo-delay-ms`, both confirmed in the installed binary's help strings), so this is zero-network and zero-cost. The env-var family and the refusal string are all present in the installed `muse-bin-0.1.0-R708.1`, so the probe can be calibrated against the currently pinned build before the pin is dropped.

The probe proves the file is read and treated as base instructions; it does not positively observe composition into the meta request. **Neither did the pin** — a digest only proves byte-identity with a build where that inference was once drawn — so the probe loses nothing and gains survival across updates. The existing fresh→kill→exact-resume meta sentinel canary (PR #96) remains the optional stronger per-digest evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- An unlisted Codex build that passes both proof layers binds, with no table edit.
- A build that fails either layer refuses with a typed reason naming the failed leg, having launched no provider and sent no task bytes.
- `thread/resume` adoption is asserted by executing code, not by a comment.
- An unlisted Muse build that passes the echo probe carries the profile carrier; one that does not advertises `profile_carrier_unverified`.
- Verdicts are cached per binary digest so the cost is per-build, not per-launch.
- A test fails if a capability is withheld solely because a version is unlisted.

## Constraints

Probe design must stay zero-cost: no paid provider turns, no network calls to model APIs. Both designs above satisfy this — Codex's schema probe creates no session, and Muse's echo provider is local.

## Not determined by the research, carry as open

- No stage-verification transcripts exist in-repo for the 0.146.0/0.147.0 bootstrap (PR #8's bundle "is archived in the conductor run directory"). This argues for encoding the checks in code, where they become self-documenting.
- Whether app-server `thread/resume` exercises the same rollout-load path as the TUI's `codex resume <id>` is statically unverifiable.
- Whether `generate-json-schema` exists on builds older than 0.138. Moot going forward, but the shape probe must itself fail closed when the command is absent — a missing probe command is a typed refusal, never an admission.
issues.title: replace the last two capability allowlists with runtime self-proof: no build has ever failed the Codex bootstrap contract

issues.body:
`conduct continue` refuses a legacy parked run and names fresh succession as the remedy, but nothing emits the four values that remedy requires. The path exists and is lawful; taking it costs archaeology across three files per run.

## Reproduced 2026-08-17

    conduct continue --project p1-closure \
      --task-id cond-0296-checkpoint-callback-provenance-implement-terra-r1 \
      --instruction "..."

    {"ok": false, "outcome": "successor-policy-refused", "provider_io": false,
     "reason_code": "policy-snapshot-missing",
     "reason": "this retained track predates the campaign policy snapshot contract; a legacy parked run migrates only through an explicit fresh successor, never through `conduct continue`",
     "safe_next_action": "conduct spawn --successor-of <task> --expected-source-round 1 --successor-artifact PATH --expected-artifact-head SHA"}

The refusal is correct and well formed: typed, no provider I/O, no mutation, and it names a real verb. `conduct spawn --successor-of` requires four exact values - source task id, the source's exact parked round, the artifact path relative to the source worktree, and the exact source head the artifact is bound at.

`conduct successor show` does not emit them; for a run with no attempt yet it returns `successor-no-claim` and nothing else. No other command emits them either.

## Where the values actually live

For that run, spread across three files under the run directory:

- `retained-track.json` -> `current_round: 1`, and `worktree`
- `workspace-checkpoint.json` -> `head: dd0c615a6abb90c44e41b07769fb31aff7e660b2`, `branch`, `canonical_worktree_realpath`
- the artifact path is not recorded as such; the caller must decide which tracked file the successor continues

So the values are discoverable - this is not an absorbing state - but the supported surface stops one step short of the command it just told the operator to run. This is the same shape as cond-0469: a remedy is named and the arguments it needs are not provided by any read.

## Why it matters now

17 runs in p1-closure are parked with `ATTENTION=orphaned-run`, parked between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-10, terminals long gone. That is the largest block of stalled work in the campaign. The supervisor audited them and reported "no lawful duplicate or continuation dispatch is currently available", which is accurate for `continue` and incomplete for succession - the lawful path exists, and its cost is what makes it look absent.

## Fix

Have the refusal emit the successor invocation with every value it can resolve already filled in, leaving only the artifact choice to the caller - the same shape as the retained-v1 disposition template in cond-0469. Resolve `--expected-source-round` from `retained-track.json` and `--expected-artifact-head` from the checkpoint, and list the tracked files at that head as candidates for `--successor-artifact`.

Alternatively or additionally, teach `conduct successor show` to emit a `successor_command` for a parked source with no claim, so the read that exists for this question answers it.

Nothing here changes what succession validates. The values are still checked exactly as they are today; a stale round or a wrong head must still refuse.

## Test

For a legacy parked run with no successor attempt, assert the `continue` refusal carries a command string whose round and head equal the durable records, and that a successor spawned from exactly that command is accepted. Mutation-test: change the emitted head and assert succession refuses, so the emitted value is proven load-bearing rather than decorative.
issues.resolution: Triage 2026-08-21 vs vision + main 13bcdcc: Verified already-fixed on conductor main. Fix commit/proof cited in triage comment (see prior comment_id). Live file inspection (git log -S, grep) confirms defect absent. Vision: check now correctly scoped/closed; smallest check shipped. No further action. If re-observed, reopen with current file:line.
issues.title: the successor remedy is named but its four required arguments are emitted by no command

issues.body:
Severity: P1. Repository: `cao-conductor`. Found by the handoff/resurrection mapping pass, walking the operator's quota-driven model-migration scenario against current code.

This is the composition failure `AGENTS.md` names explicitly: *"Checks individually correct and individually fail-closed together leave a record with no legal transition out for any actor, the operator included — a correctness defect of the same severity as a corrupt write, which 'every check behaved as specified' describes rather than defends."*

## The sequence

A retained worker's track stays `active` until a round **parks**, and parking requires a durable round report carrying an acceptance-time digest from an accepted `conduct report` callback (`checkpoint.py:657-680`).

**A worker whose provider quota is exhausted cannot produce that report.** It cannot take another turn. Quota is a spawn-time preflight only; nothing observes exhaustion mid-track.

Every downstream verb then refuses on `state != "parked"`:

| verb | refusal |
|---|---|
| `conduct retire` | `retire.py:277` — "a live round is never retired (zero mutation)", and there is no `--force` in its argument list |
| `conduct collect` | `collect.py:579` |
| `conduct continue` | `continue_round.py:805` |
| `conduct track move-retained` | `track_move.py:472` |
| `conduct successor` / `spawn --successor-of` | `_successor.py:354` — "fresh succession requires a complete PARKED source occurrence" |

`conduct unstick` sends bytes through the pane, which a quota-exhausted provider will not answer.

Each refusal is individually defensible. Composed on one record they leave **no verb for any actor, including the operator.**

## The exit that exists costs a falsehood

`conduct report --terminal <worker>` accepts an arbitrary terminal id and never proves the caller is that terminal (`report.py:319`, `:349`), so a supervisor can author the worker's callback. The report's *content* can honestly say `--status blocked`, but the callback record will then assert that the worker reported when it did not.

`AGENTS.md`: *"Never clear one by recording an outcome that did not happen — a repair path requiring a falsehood is not a repair path."*

## Why this matters beyond the edge case

This is the operator's stated motivating scenario for the whole flexible-handoff direction: an Opus agent owns a long track, Anthropic quota runs out, and authority must move to a provider that still has capacity. Running out of subscription quota mid-track is ordinary operating reality on this installation, not a rare fault.

## Smallest coherent repair

**Demote `conduct retire`'s parked gate to a disposition requirement.** Allow retiring an `active` retained track when the caller names an explicit non-`reported` disposition, and record that no round report exists rather than requiring one to be manufactured.

Leave `collect`, `continue`, and `move-retained` parked-gated — those consume a report and genuinely need one. The distinction is that `retire` does not consume the report; it only currently insists one exist.

The evidence-loss concern the gate protects against is already handled correctly and independently in the fork: `retire_worker_pane` (`supervisor_worker_ops.py:177-187`) finalizes the occurrence first with an explicit typed disposition, then retires the incarnation. The conductor-side gate adds no protection that path lacks; it only forces a supervisor to author the worker's callback under the worker's name.

## Acceptance criterion

Not "a flag was added." A test must fail if a retained track whose worker cannot report has no verb that moves it out of `active` without fabricating a round report. Enumerate the states reachable on that record and name the verb and actor that leaves each — per `AGENTS.md`, that enumeration is the deliverable, not a by-product.
issues.resolution:
Conductor PR #200 merged (13bcdcc): retire gains a second exit for a retained round whose worker cannot report. Unit Tests (3.13) green, mergeStateStatus CLEAN at merge.

Two lanes contributed and both should be named. The first built the exit; the second found that the repair carried the defect it repairs, one level down, and fixed it. That recursion is the durable lesson here: round 1 committed the falsehood this issue exists to prevent, round 2's fix collapsed 'unreadable' into 'negative' (the same error inverted), and the absorbing-state fix itself introduced an absorbing state. The chain was broken not by reviewing the newest commit but by asking a class-closure question -- enumerate every failure mode of the read and name the verb and actor that leaves each -- which is what AGENTS.md asks for and what a diff review does not produce.
issues.title: a quota-exhausted retained round has no exit for any actor, and the one that exists requires fabricating the worker's report

issues.body:
Severity: P1. Repository: `cli-agent-orchestrator`. Found by the handoff/resurrection mapping pass.

## The defect

`publish_contract` and `transition_dormant` appear **only in `test/`** and `test/e2e/exact_canary/runner.py`. Verified by grep over the whole fork excluding `.venv`. Nothing in `src/` ever writes a restore contract.

Every resurrection gate hard-requires that row:

- `operation_journal.py:922-930` — "publish one before claiming an exact reincarnation"
- `exact_executor.py:1451-1458`
- `supervisor_worker_ops.py:229-237`, and `has_exact_resume_identity` returns `False` for every real agent
- `stable_agent_roster.transition_dormant`'s own contract requirement
- `cohort_resume._has_resume_identity` (`:276-289`) returns `unresumable`

Production teardown takes the contract-free path: `terminal_service.py:1370-1387` calls `roster.retire_incarnation` directly.

**So no real agent is resurrectable today.** Every refusal fires and no releasing half exists.

This is the half-built shape from `AGENTS.md`, inverted — not "a field an agent sets that nothing reads", but a record everything reads and nothing writes. Same consequence: a refusal with no counterpart that clears it.

## Blast radius is wider than handback

**Fleet Stop is a one-way door today for the same reason.** `cohort_resume` requires resume identity that no agent has, so a stopped cohort cannot be resumed. This is not a handback-only concern; it is the general durability of Stop.

## Smallest coherent repair

Publish the contract inside `terminal_service._roster_retire_incarnation_best_effort`, then retire through `transition_dormant` instead of `retire_incarnation`. Everything the contract needs is already resolved at that point in the call.

**Keep the best-effort posture.** A failed publish must not block Stop; it just means that agent is not resurrectable, which is the state of every agent today. That direction is important: the change can only improve resurrectability, never remove a teardown that works now.

## Verification note

Whether `restore_contracts` is empty on the live installation was not confirmed — no live database was inspected. Rows are possible only via tests or the e2e canary runner, so the expectation is empty, but that should be checked before the repair is graded.

Also undetermined: whether the absent writer is a deliberately parked slice or an oversight. `transition_dormant`'s docstring says "later slices deliberately adopt this transition when they retire an incarnation that must be resurrectable," which reads as intentional deferral, but no issue reference or design doc naming that slice was found. If a slice exists, this issue should be folded into it rather than duplicating it.

## Why it matters now

The operator has directed that A→B→A handback be a byproduct of two general capabilities composing: arbitrary agent-to-agent handoff, and resurrection of a retired agent on its preserved native session. The mapping pass established that **both capabilities are already general in shape** — the handoff has no direction column and no prior-relationship constraint, and the resurrection service is keyed on the stable agent id. The gap is producers, and this is the first of them.
issues.title: the restore contract has no production writer, so no agent is resurrectable and fleet Stop is a one-way door

issues.body:
Severity: P2. Repositories: `cao-conductor` plus global/custom skills. Operator direction, 2026-08-17.

Supervisors are capable agents with a large gap in diagnostic and recovery tooling. They should have wide freedom to check in on their workers, investigate them, find their chat history, judge whether a worker is on the right task or has hit an error it cannot solve, and clean up any mess. This issue covers that capability set and the one narrow guard it needs.

## The guard model, which is the important part

The operator drew the line deliberately, and it is the mechanism-vs-policy rule applied:

- **Mechanism, narrow:** a supervisor may collect only workers **it spawned**, and may file a report on behalf of only workers **it spawned**. `terminals.caller_id` (`clients/database.py:57` in the fork — "terminal that created this one (callback target)") already records this, so the guard has a durable field and needs no new bookkeeping.
- **Policy and skills, open:** everything read-only — inspecting tmux panes, reading session logs, tailing output, checking what a worker is doing. Other agents *could* do these if determined; the risk of them doing so is low, and they will not because it is not in their skills, policy files, or prompts. Do not build mechanism here. Granting a capability by installing a skill is the intended enforcement, and it is proportionate.

The distinction: reads stay open and guided, while acts that carry authority or destroy a pane are scoped to spawn ownership.

## Piece 1 — a session-log discovery skill (standalone, not tied to recovery)

Given a session id and a harness, locate that agent's chat/session logs. Every harness logs its conversation somewhere, and the mapping differs per harness.

**Deliberately independent of the recovery flow.** It is useful in many contexts — checking whether a worker understood its task, finding where it went wrong, reading what it actually did versus what it reported — and it should not be reachable only through a teardown path. Build it as its own skill.

Cover at minimum the harnesses this installation runs: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Muse, plus the headless launcher run directories (`run_dir`, `final.txt`, the stream-json transcript), and the provider-native session stores.

## Piece 2 — terminate-and-report-on-behalf

The recovery flow for a worker that cannot report for itself. This is the accepted repair for cond-0484, where a quota-exhausted worker cannot produce the round report every downstream verb requires, leaving the record with no exit for any actor.

Shape:

1. The supervisor may dispatch a **subagent** to investigate and summarise the worker's session logs. Not strictly required, but it protects the supervisor's context from the grunt work of reading a large transcript. Supervisors should be using subagents for this class of task.
2. The supervisor files the round report **on the worker's behalf**, from that investigation.
3. **Filing the report collects the worker**: it stops the session and closes the tmux pane, atomically with the report.

### Provenance is already honest, and must stay that way

`goal_store.py:772-773` defines `authored_by_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (authored_by_type IN ('worker','supervisor','operator','system'))`. The value `'supervisor'` is **already legal**.

`conduct/commands/report.py:148-149` currently hardcodes `authored_by_type="worker"` and `authored_by_id=terminal_id`. That hardcoding is the entire reason a supervisor-authored report would today assert the worker reported.

**So this needs no schema change.** Set `authored_by_type="supervisor"` and `authored_by_id=<supervisor terminal>` for an on-behalf report, and the record is truthful about who wrote it while the report's *content* honestly describes the worker's state. A repair path that requires a falsehood is not a repair path; this one does not require any.

Anything that consumes report provenance should be checked for an implicit assumption that reports are worker-authored.

### Why coupling the report to collection is the safety property

The operator named both failure modes it prevents, and both are real:

- It stops a supervisor doing this to a worker that is **still active** — you cannot report-and-collect a healthy worker without also ending it, so the act is self-limiting.
- It prevents the **double-report** pitfall: a worker whose report was filed by the supervisor cannot later file its own, because it no longer exists.

**Make the coupling atomic, or self-healing in the safe direction.** If the report lands and the collect fails, the result is a reported-but-live worker that can report again — exactly the pitfall the coupling exists to prevent. Either do both in one transaction, or order them so a partial failure leaves the worker un-reported rather than reported-and-live, and record which leg failed.

## Piece 3 — the broader diagnostic toolkit

Beyond the two pieces above, supervisors need enough to answer, without operator help:

- is this worker alive, and is its pane responsive?
- what task does it think it has, and is that the task I gave it?
- has it hit an error it cannot recover from?
- what has it actually produced?

Ship these as skills and policy rather than as new mechanism wherever the action is a read.

## Acceptance criteria

- A supervisor can bring a quota-exhausted worker's retained track out of `active` without fabricating a worker-authored record.
- The resulting report is attributable to the supervisor, and any consumer of report provenance handles that.
- A supervisor cannot collect, or report on behalf of, a worker it did not spawn — spawn ownership resolved through the supervisor succession chain (`successor_terminal_id` in `supervisor-retirements.json`, `conduct/commands/_common.py:587` / `is_supervisor_successor`); a live successor of the spawning supervisor is authorized for workers its predecessor spawned (cond-0620).
- A partial failure of the report/collect pair never leaves a worker both reported and live.
- The session-log discovery skill is invocable on its own, outside any recovery flow.

## Relationship to cond-0484

cond-0484 records the composition defect: a quota-exhausted retained round has no exit for any actor. My earlier suggestion there was to demote `conduct retire`'s parked gate. **This issue is the operator's preferred repair and it is better**, because it produces a real report from real evidence rather than merely permitting a track to move without one. Demoting the parked gate may still be worth doing as a second exit, but it is no longer the primary answer.
issues.title: give supervisors real diagnostic and recovery tooling: session-log discovery, terminate-and-report-on-behalf, spawn-scoped authority

issues.body:
`conduct issue close --resolution <text>` rejects some payloads with an untyped HTTP 400 that names no cause, so the caller cannot tell what to change.

## Observed 2026-08-17

Closing 39 vetted issues in one pass, 36 succeeded and 3 failed identically:

    conduct issue close --id cond-0320 --as closed --resolution "<1181 chars>"
    {"ok": false, "error": {"failure_class": "cao-server-session",
      "message": "CAO PATCH /tracker/issues/cond-0320 failed: HTTP 400",
      "evidence_path": null, "safe_next_actions": []}}

`safe_next_actions` is empty and nothing states what was wrong with the payload.

## What it is not

Ruled out by experiment on the same issue ids:

- **Not length.** The 36 accepted resolutions ran up to 1700 characters; the three rejected ones were 1181, 1494 and 1588.
- **Not non-ASCII.** `conduct issue close --id cond-0459 --resolution "em dash test — here"` succeeded.
- **Not the close itself.** `--resolution "test short"` on the same id succeeded immediately.

The three rejected payloads all embed a shell-quoted git invocation containing nested single quotes and doubled backticks, e.g.

    (`git log --reverse -S'Ordered after ``URLError`` on purpose' -- conduct/lib/caoapi.py`)

That is the remaining difference, and it is exactly the kind of text a good resolution carries: the command that proves the claim.

## Why it matters

Evidence is a path or a command, not a paraphrase - the tracker's own rules require it. A resolution field that rejects the commands worth quoting, without saying so, pushes callers toward vaguer resolutions or toward a placeholder. Both happened here before the payload was moved into a comment, which accepted the identical text.

Note the asymmetry: `conduct issue comment --body` accepted every one of these payloads unchanged. Whatever validation or encoding the resolution path applies, the comment path does not.

## Fix

Two parts, and the first matters more:

1. **State what was observed.** Whatever rejects the payload should return a typed reason naming the offending field and constraint, with a usable `safe_next_actions`. AGENTS.md: a refusal states what it observed, not what it assumed - an HTTP 400 with an empty action list asserts nothing and sends the caller guessing.
2. **Then decide whether to reject at all.** If the constraint is encoding or escaping rather than a real limit, fix the encoding so a resolution can carry the same text a comment can. A resolution is append-only audit evidence; refusing it loses the record, and recording a fact the tracker can place creates no illegal state.

## Test

Close an issue with a resolution containing nested single quotes and doubled backticks. Assert it either succeeds, or refuses with a typed reason naming the field and a non-empty safe_next_actions. Mutation-test by removing the typed reason and asserting the test goes red, so the refusal text is pinned rather than incidental.
issues.failing_command: conduct issue close --id cond-0320 --as closed --resolution <text with nested quotes and backticks>
issues.title: issue close rejects some resolution payloads with an untyped HTTP 400 naming no cause

issues.body:
Launch admission was opened to any semver-shaped build; capability was not. Two enumerated known-good sets remain, and each one goes dark for every future vendor release.

## Current state on fork origin/main

    src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/provider_contracts.py:657  NATIVE_BIND_CAPABLE_VERSIONS
    src/cli_agent_orchestrator/services/provider_contracts.py:713  ROUTE_ATTEST_CAPABLE_VERSIONS

Both are enumerated sets tested with `normalized in ...`, which is False for every build not written down in advance.

This is the exact pattern `docs/policy` and AGENTS.md already forbid:

> An allowlist of known-good versions is not a guard, it is an expiry date. It excludes every future build by default, so the system degrades by standing still and a vendor release silently removes a capability nobody chose to give up. Where a check must exist, name the build that is known broken, not the ones known good. Per-version knowledge is an override recording what was proven on a build, never a precondition: a missing record selects a conservative default and proceeds.

Commit 43812413 ("docs(policy): unpinned harness versions as the default, and forbid capability allowlists") settled the policy. `VERSION_ENFORCEMENT_MODE` was opened for launch admission. These two tables were not converted.

## Why this is filed against the tables and not against a build

Three separate issues were filed and closed for individual builds this pattern rejected:

- cond-0401 - GLM native route attestation rejected the installed Claude Code version
- cond-0412 - native launch-domain attestation rejected source-proven Codex 0.147
- cond-0480 - same family

Each was fixed by adding a build to a table, or by opening enforcement on a different axis. The rows are individually dead and the pattern that generates them is alive. Every vendor release regenerates this issue class, and each instance costs a file, a triage, a fix, and a deploy to add one string. Filing per-build is the defect reproducing itself through the tracker.

## Fix

Convert both tables from precondition to override, per the policy already adopted:

1. A build with **no** record selects a conservative default and proceeds. Conservative means the safe end of the range, never the null value - an empty capability set or a zero timing chosen because nothing was proven converts an absent measurement into a silent failure.
2. A build **known broken** is named in a quarantine entry, and only that build refuses.
3. A build **proven good** may carry an override recording what was proven, used to widen behaviour rather than to permit it at all.
4. Where no default can be made safe for a specific operation, refuse that one operation with a typed reason naming what was not established, and leave the rest of the provider working.

The properties whose failure is a wrong write rather than wasted effort - zero old-generation bytes, exclusive native attachment, no input replay - stay hard per-cell proof. Those are not what this issue asks to loosen.

## Test

Assert that a semver-shaped build absent from every table reaches the conservative default and is not refused for absence alone; that a quarantined build refuses with a typed reason naming the build; and that a proven build still gets its widened behaviour. Mutation-test by restoring the `in` check and confirming the absent-build case goes red - otherwise the test pins nothing about the direction of the fix.

issues.body:
`conduct gate check` now reports two delivery buckets — `undelivered` for the occurrence in force and
`undelivered_superseded` for unobserved attempts on superseded occurrences (PR #180, `cond-0475`).
Neither bucket has an operator verb that empties it.

A `pending` delivery row means nobody observed whether the announcement landed. The stated
reconciliation is "read the target by exact `delivery_id`" — but having read it, the operator has no
`conduct gate` subcommand that settles the row. `settle_delivery` exists in the library
(`conduct/lib/gate_journal.py`) and is reachable from no command. So a row enters the bucket and
stays there permanently, and the bucket grows monotonically for the life of the project.

Two independent reviewers of PR #180 found this without prompting and converged on the same wording:
the repair for a bucket that could never clear introduced a bucket that cannot be drained. It is the
half-built-mechanism shape this repository's `AGENTS.md` names — *"every refusal ships the
counterpart that clears it"* — at report level rather than state-machine level, which is why it is
medium and not blocking.

Related, from the same reviews: a `failed` attempt on a superseded occurrence is now reachable only
through the library's `deliveries()`, with no CLI surface at all. The commit's justification
("`deliveries` still lists it as the history it is") holds only for library callers. Whatever verb
drains the pending bucket should probably also give that history a CLI surface.

Suggested shape: an operator verb that settles a named `delivery_id` with an outcome and a reason,
reachable from `conduct gate`, that refuses a delivery on the occurrence in force (those are the
delivering command's to settle, not the operator's). Do not add a bulk drain — a per-row verb keeps
the reconciliation honest.

**Severity: medium.** Nothing is trapped and no state machine wedges; the cost is a report that
accumulates rows an operator has already reconciled and cannot mark as such.

issues.body:
`conduct resume` cannot return `resumed` for any input, has never been invoked on this installation, and emits a permanent RED doctor advisory. It is a verb refusing for every possible input - the first item AGENTS.md lists as half-built on sight.

## Proof it always refuses

`conduct/commands/resume.py:118-145` builds the admission context with four hardcoded literals:

    capability_receipt_valid=False,   # no capability receipts on this base
    observed_route_supported=False,   # PF-2 red for every enabled provider
    confinement_proven=False,         # PF-3 red: mechanism unproven
    prior_generation_proven=False,    # PF-1b not green

`conduct/lib/resume_admission.py:87-90` refuses on the first of those alone:

    if ctx.version_drift or not ctx.capability_receipt_valid:
        return _refuse("capability-unsupported",
                       "capability receipt absent/revoked or version drift")

`capability_receipt_valid` is never anything but the literal `False`, so no input can reach the `resumed` return. The next two rows would refuse independently anyway.

The module docstring states this deliberately: "While the red feasibility gates stand (PF-1a/PF-1b/PF-2/PF-3), confinement-dependent admission always refuses; identity/resume mechanics are still evaluated in full so every refusal row is truthful."

## Proof nothing has ever used it

`conduct doctor` reports `recovery-capability: PF-1a=RED PF-1b=RED PF-2=RED PF-3=RED (recovery execution lane blocked, alert-only); capability receipts on disk: 0`.

Across every campaign event log on this host, no `conduct resume` invocation appears. The only "resume" hits are unrelated payload text in `control-input`, `skill-record` and `unstick` rows. Recovery in practice happens through `spawn --recover`, `continue`, and fresh succession.

## Why this is worth a decision rather than a shrug

The verb is honest - it refuses rather than pretending - so it is not corrupting anything, and it blocks no work today because nobody depends on it. The cost is elsewhere:

`conduct doctor` reports the RED recovery-capability row on every single run, permanently, with no action that can clear it. An advisory that can never go green trains operators and supervisors to skim past advisories, which is exactly where a real recovery-path defect would appear. A permanently-red check is worse than no check, because it consumes the attention a real one would need.

## The decision

Pick one; both are legitimate and the current state is neither.

**(a) Wire it.** Feed `resume_admission.evaluate` live facts instead of literals - read the capability receipt, the observed-route authority, and the confinement/prior-generation proofs from wherever they are actually established - and let the refusal reflect what was observed. This is only worth doing alongside the M3 reincarnation work (cond-0132, cond-0382), which is what would produce those receipts.

**(b) Delete it, and the advisory with it.** Remove the subcommand and the `recovery-capability` doctor row until the receipts exist. AGENTS.md: for an always-refusing verb, ship the releasing half rather than the surface, whose deletion hides the gap - so if this is chosen, the gap must be recorded in the M3 plan rather than lost, and `resume` returns when it can succeed.

Do NOT leave it as is. A verb that cannot succeed plus an advisory that cannot clear is the combination that decays into ignored signal.

## Related

cond-0132 (reboot recovery cannot reattach persisted native sessions) has the same root: the fork's `exact_executor` for same-native-session reincarnation is merged and has no caller in `src/`. cond-0382 sequences activation. Whichever way this issue is decided, it should be decided together with those.

issues.body:
Nothing verifies that the provider ids the routing table names are resolvable by the installed quota adapter. When one is not, the failure is invisible until a supervisor routes to that provider, and the recovery is to fall back to a more expensive pool.

## The instance that motivated this

cond-0489: `conduct spawn` preflight for a Muse Contributor route failed with `unknown provider 'meta'`. The conductor was correct - `conduct/lib/quota.py` passes `route.quota_provider` straight through - and the installed skill genuinely did not know the id, because the mini's skillshare source tree had been overwritten by a stale copy of check-ai-quota (1200 deletions; the whole test module gone).

Cost of the gap, measured: the supervisor made the right call under quota pressure - route bounded work to the cheapest healthy provider - and was refused. It fell back to Claude Opus while Claude was YELLOW with a `conserve` posture at 4.8 points over weekly pace. Kimi and Z.ai were EXTREME and Codex RED at the time, so the cheap route was the only healthy one and it was silently unavailable.

## Why a check is proportionate here

This is not new ceremony on a working path. It is read-only observability over a drift that already happened, in a place where the failure mode is silent and the fallback spends scarce quota rather than failing loudly.

Absence is the whole signal: a route naming a provider id the adapter cannot resolve is a configuration fact establishable at rest, with no provider I/O, no credentials, and no network call. It does not gate anything and must not: a failing row is advisory and names the route and the id.

## Fix

Add a `conduct doctor` advisory row that, for every provider id appearing in the routing table, asks the installed adapter whether it resolves that id, and reports the ones that do not with the route names that reference them.

Constraints that keep it cheap and honest:

- **Resolution only, never a live quota probe.** Do not authenticate, do not call a provider, do not spend a request. The question is "does the installed adapter know this id", answerable from the adapter's own vocabulary.
- **Advisory, never critical.** An unresolvable id must not block a deploy or a campaign. It is a warning that a route is unselectable.
- **Name both sides.** The refusal text must carry the provider id and every route that names it, so the reader knows what became unselectable rather than only that something did.
- **Absent adapter is a distinct answer from unresolvable id.** If the adapter itself cannot be invoked, say that, and do not report every id as unresolvable - that is the "absent and unreadable are different answers" rule.

## Test

Build a routing table naming a provider id the adapter does not know; assert the doctor row reports exactly that id and the routes referencing it, that its severity is advisory, and that no provider request is issued. Mutation-test by making the check pass unconditionally and confirming the assertion goes red.

Related: cond-0489 (the instance). The skill-sync drift itself is an environment concern rather than a conductor defect; this issue is only about the conductor being able to see it.
issues.title: nothing detects a routing-table provider id the installed quota adapter cannot resolve

issues.body:
PR #182 made `deadline_at` something the coverage validator judges: a deadline anchors a hold only
when the caller supplies an `as_of` instant and the deadline is still ahead of it. Two reason codes
were added — `deadline-elapsed` and `deadline-unobserved`.

The write-side shape check did not move with it. `coverage.hold_reasons` still accepts a
`deadline_at` in any non-empty string shape, so a record the validator can now never credit remains
storable. The judging boundary and the storability boundary disagree.

Two independent reviewers of #182 found this without prompting and both graded it medium. Nothing is
trapped: a hold carrying an uncreditable deadline simply does not cover, and `hold resolve` and the
other exits all remain available. The cost is that an agent can write a bound the system will never
honour and gets no signal at write time — it discovers the problem later, as an unexplained
`deadline-elapsed` or `deadline-unobserved` on a hold it believed was anchored.

Suggested shape: make the pre-freeze check reject a `deadline_at` the validator could never credit —
at minimum a well-formed RFC3339 UTC instant, since `_rfc3339` already documents that it "cannot tell
a malformed deadline from a distant one" and now something downstream can. Whether the write boundary
should also refuse an already-elapsed deadline is a judgement call: refusing is friendlier, but it
requires a clock at the write path, which is exactly the dependency the validator was designed to
avoid. Recording it and letting the validator report `deadline-elapsed` may be the better answer.
Decide deliberately rather than by omission.

**Severity: medium.** Consistency between what may be stored and what may be credited, not a trap.
