issues.title: the standing test_gc_workspaces exemption has no tracker record and has been misattributed twice

issues.body:
conduct/lib/capability.PINNED_PROVIDERS is not in cond-0481's scope table, which
enumerates six FORK surfaces (SUPPORTED_VERSIONS, _PROVEN_COMPOSER_NEWLINE,
_PROVEN_STEER_CHORDS, _RENDERED_SESSION_PROVEN_BUILDS, IMAGE_PROVEN_BUILDS,
PINNED_VERSIONS). This is the conductor-side analogue and no issue covers it.

NOTHING IN IT IS PINNED. All four providers carry version_policy: 'open'. The
in-code comment states the intent plainly: 'launch/admission accepts any
non-empty semver-shaped observed version, so routine provider auto-updates do
not ground the route before task bytes.' The name asserts the opposite of the
behaviour, which is how a reader arrives believing this system pins harness
versions when the operator direction is that unpinned is correct.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOAD-BEARING is the per-provider launch contract, and it is
real knowledge that cannot be defaulted: resume_forms ('resume <id>' for codex,
'--session <id>' for muse, '--resume <uuid>' for claude), native_id_sources,
forbidden_flags (--last/--from-pr resolve a session indirectly and can open an
interactive picker that hangs a non-interactive launch), and
native_status_capture with measured cannot-capture rates (39% claude native TUI,
12% codex, 0% kimi).

THE VESTIGIAL VERSION DATA IS ALREADY STALE, measured 2026-08-19:

  muse_cli     contract 0.1.0,   accepted_versions ('0.1.0',)  vs installed 0.2.1-R1215.1
  codex        contract 0.145.0                                vs installed 0.148.0
  claude_code  contract 2.1.220                                vs installed 2.1.233
  kimi_cli     contract 0.34.0 with an 8-entry accepted_versions list

muse_cli's accepted_versions names a build that no longer exists on disk. That
is precisely the cond-0482 shape: an allowlist naming a muse-bin revision the
self-updating launcher pruned, which in the fork made the carrier capability
permanently unsatisfiable and took Muse out of CAO entirely.

Here it is inert ONLY because version_policy is open. The code then invites the
flip: 'to re-enable strict mode, set version_policy to strict and enumerate the
allowed versions in accepted_versions.' Following that instruction for muse_cli
today reproduces the outage immediately, because the enumerated version is not
installed. An allowlist is an expiry date, and this one has already expired
without anyone noticing, because nothing reads it.

THE MEMBERSHIP GATE IS CORRECT AND SHOULD STAY. spawn.py:1713 refuses a native
launch when the provider is not a key. Without resume_forms a native resume does
not fail loudly - it starts a FRESH session, exits 0, and answers fluently,
which is documented behaviour for these CLIs and is why continuity is scored by
codeword recall rather than a returned id. That is a silent corruption worth
refusing over, and it is explicitly the exception cond-0481 preserves: 'there is
no way to pretend a session is resumable, and degrading silently would produce a
launch that cannot resume itself.'

But the refusal text is 'no pinned provider contract', which describes a version
pin. What is actually missing is a resume form. A reader hitting it goes looking
for a version problem that does not exist.

SUGGESTED REPAIR, all of it text and data, no behaviour change:

1. Rename to something naming what it holds - provider launch contracts - so it
   cannot be read as a version allowlist.
2. Delete accepted_versions, or demote it to an explicitly advisory
   proven-on-this-build record. Per policy, per-version knowledge is an override
   recording what was proven, never a precondition; these currently read as
   preconditions and are wrong.
3. Remove the 'to re-enable strict mode, enumerate accepted_versions' comment,
   or correct it to say the enumeration must be re-measured first. As written it
   is a documented path to reproducing cond-0482.
4. Reword the spawn refusal to name the missing resume form rather than a pin.
5. If the 'version' field is genuinely advisory, say so beside it; three of four
   being stale with nothing broken is the evidence that it is.
issues.title: conductor PINNED_PROVIDERS names a version pin it does not implement, and its vestigial version data is stale on three of four providers

issues.body:
M3-F (cond-0382) gates all M3 activation. Its plan text requires binding
callbacks to task occurrence plus incarnation "rather than requiring permanent
terminal identity equality". That amendment is UNSTARTED, and it is the one
conductor-side gate that stops an M3-F resume cell from being ATTEMPTED at all
rather than merely from passing.

MEASURED, on cao-conductor main 95cca2d:

conduct/commands/report.py:854-857

    if track.get("terminal_id") != terminal_id:
        _refuse_occurrence(
            f"retained track binds terminal {track.get('terminal_id')!r}, not "
            f"the reporting terminal {terminal_id!r}")

and report.py:907-937, _check_occurrence_generation, refuses when the observed
control-identity generation differs from the bound one, on the stated reasoning
that "a replaced incarnation is reporting into the previous incarnation's round".

After an exact reincarnation the resurrected agent holds a NEW terminal id
and/or generation by construction. Both checks therefore fire on precisely the
case M3 exists to support. The fork can restore a pane today; the conductor then
refuses that pane's report on any retained-run cell.

Each check is individually defensible - they were written to stop a stale
incarnation reporting into a round it no longer owns. The defect is that the
identity they compare is the physical terminal rather than the occurrence and
incarnation the round is actually about, so a legitimate successor and a stale
predecessor are indistinguishable to them.

DEPENDENCY CHAIN, which is why this cannot be fixed alone:

  M3-D occurrence seam -> callback contract -> cond-0303 design amendment

The fork-minted task_occurrence_id is not carried into the flow that would need
it. It exists only as a late-bindable optional column (goal_store.py:24,
:490-495 "minting a task-occurrence id is M3-D authority", :798-799) and a
read-only client method (caoapi.py:485-509). It is ABSENT from spawn.py,
collect.py, continue_round.py, spawn_delivery.py and retained_track.py - the
files that define launch identity and the callback binding. So the callback has
no occurrence id to bind to yet.

Related conductor-side M3-F items, all PASS-blocking rather than
ATTEMPT-blocking, recorded here so the chain is visible:

- cond-0303 design amendment distinguishing exact reincarnation from fresh
  succession: unstarted; the design has no reincarnation section.
- Predicate scoping (exact reincarnation must consume only the same-harness
  capability receipt, not fresh-successor route-equality/Fable/human-gate):
  currently safe BY ABSENCE - no exact-reincarnation surface exists to
  mis-scope onto (spawn.py:854-866, :3287, :4201). It becomes a real
  requirement the moment the surface is built.
- Activation surface: dark and fail-closed, currently unflippable per cell
  (resume.py:124-126, :141-142, resume_admission.py:89-96, :122-130,
  execution_mode.py:127-130).
- Client verbs for the M3-B/C exact operations: absent from caoapi.py, pending
  a decision on whether the supervisor drives reincarnation through conduct or
  directly against the fork HTTP API.

SCOPE NOTE. Do not "fix" this by deleting the two checks. They prevent a real
stale-incarnation write. The repair is to compare the identity the round is
about - occurrence plus incarnation - which requires the occurrence seam first.
Deleting them would trade a blocked resume for a corrupt one.

Mapped by a read-only pass over the conductor; report.py:854-857 and
_check_occurrence_generation were re-verified directly against main before
filing.
issues.title: conduct refuses a reincarnated agent's report on terminal identity equality, so no M3-F resume cell can be attempted end to end

issues.body:
Fork-side prerequisite for cond-0517, which is itself the one conductor-side
gate stopping an M3-F resume cell from being ATTEMPTED. Filed separately because
it is a different repository and lands first.

MEASURED on fork main f0dc62ee:

  task_occurrence_id across src/cli_agent_orchestrator/  ->  170 references
  task_occurrence_id in services/managed_launch_v2.py    ->  0

It lives in the occurrence API, task_handoff, communications catalog, session
lifecycle, and the database layer. It is absent from the v2 launch/admit path
entirely.

WHY THAT BLOCKS cond-0517. The accepted cond-0517 design replaces the
conductor's physical terminal-identity check with two legs: the reporter's
resolved open occurrence must equal the round's BOUND occurrence, and the fork
must dispatch that occurrence to the reporting terminal. The second leg is what
preserves the stale-predecessor refusal. The first leg requires the retained
track to carry a bound task_occurrence_id, written once at round creation.

The conductor cannot obtain it at round creation today. The clean seam is the
admit response, because the only other source is a read-back over
agent_task_occurrences keyed on an agent_id the conductor does not know at spawn
time - the roster binding appears at launch, after the point where the track is
created. So without this, the occurrence-equality leg has nothing to compare and
a dispatch-only check would admit an unrelated terminal whose own occurrence
happens to be dispatched to itself.

TWO PARTS, and the second is already required elsewhere:

1. The v2 admit/reserve response surfaces the minted task_occurrence_id so the
   conductor can bind it into the track at round creation.
2. The occurrence's current-execution-authority moves to the new incarnation on
   exact reincarnation. This is already required by M3-B - the plan states that
   the generation bind closing the restore falsifies the prior
   current-incarnation (remaining-work.md:823-831) - so this issue should
   confirm it holds and is observable to the conductor, rather than build it new.

Part 2 is what makes the stale predecessor provably not the authority. If the
authority does not actually move, the cond-0517 truth table collapses: a stale
predecessor and a legitimate successor become indistinguishable again, and the
conductor would be re-keyed onto a field that does not discriminate. Verify part
2 by measurement before building part 1 on top of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the conductor-side consumption (cond-0517), and the paid M3-F
matrix.

Sequencing: this -> cond-0517 conductor work -> M3-F resume cells become
attemptable.
issues.title: the v2 admit response does not surface the minted task_occurrence_id, so the conductor cannot bind a round to an occurrence

issues.body:
Not a CAO code defect. A verification hazard that produces FALSE test results in
git worktrees, which is where nearly all CAO worker verification happens.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured today:

A fork worktree created by `git worktree add` has no `.venv`. Improvising one as
a symlink to the parent checkout's venv seems harmless and is not:

    ln -sfn /Users/colin/Projects/cli-agent-orchestrator/.venv .venv

The parent venv holds an EDITABLE install pointing at the PARENT's `src/`. So
pytest collects tests from the worktree while imports resolve to the parent:

    resolves to: /Users/colin/Projects/cli-agent-orchestrator/src/.../managed_launch_v2.py
    has field:   False

The worktree's own tests then run against the parent's code. Result: 6 failures
that do not exist. With the path pinned:

    PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src <venv>/bin/python -m pytest ...
    resolves to: <worktree>/src/.../managed_launch_v2.py
    has field:   True
    6 passed

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING. The failure direction is the dangerous one. It looks
exactly like the branch being broken, and the natural conclusion is that the
implementer reported a false green. I nearly recorded that against a worker whose
work was correct. The inverse is equally reachable: a change that lives ONLY in
the parent would appear to pass from a worktree that does not contain it.

This is the AGENTS.md rule about evidence conditions: a differential is only as
good as the equivalence of its runs, and a measurement used as evidence must be
taken under conditions the report can state. Nothing in a bare pytest invocation
states which tree was imported.

It is also the second instance today of the same shape - a measurement
invalidated by an unstated condition. The first was a suite differential taken
while two orphaned agents were editing the worktree (cond-0513), which reported
7 failures against a baseline of 1 and was 1 when re-run quiescent.

SUGGESTED HANDLING, cheapest first:

1. Verification instructions for worktree work should require confirming the
   import path before trusting a result:
       python -c "import cli_agent_orchestrator as m; print(m.__file__)"
   One line, and it makes the condition stateable.
2. Prefer `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src` with the parent's interpreter over
   symlinking the venv. It is the same convenience without the wrong resolution.
3. If `conduct spawn` or the worktree setup path can provision or pin this, that
   is better than every worker improvising - each improvisation is a chance to
   pick the silently-wrong one.

Filed P3: nothing is broken and there is an obvious workaround, but it silently
produces wrong verification evidence, and wrong evidence is what the review and
mutation-testing discipline exists to prevent.
issues.resolution: Triage 2026-08-21 vs vision + main 13bcdcc: #{cond-0519} is verification hazard not code defect — guidance to be promoted (PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src). #{cond-0199/0200} already-fixed typed safe_next_actions / idempotent collect; #{cond-0374} fork coverage floor obsolete. Vision tier: Tier3 capability/policy not Tier1. Close, promote docs where noted. If re-observed with file:line on conductor, reopen.
issues.title: a worktree with no venv invites a symlinked one that imports the parent checkout, so tests silently verify the wrong tree

issues.body:
*Surface:* `conduct issue` (the campaign-facing CLI) versus `tracker.STATUSES`.

The tracker defines eight statuses, and its own source comment states the reason
the middle ones exist (`services/issue_tracker.py:55-67` in the fork):

> middle states exist so a long-running project can distinguish "nobody has
> looked at this" from "somebody is on it" from "it is waiting on something
> else", which is the distinction that makes a stale tracker readable.

    STATUSES = ("open", "triage", "in-progress", "blocked",
                "resolved", "closed", "wontfix", "duplicate")

`assignee` is a real column (`clients/database.py:386`).

## Nothing in the campaign path has ever written any of it

Census taken 2026-08-19T15:15Z, before this filing:

| status | count |
|---|---|
| open | 27 |
| resolved | 12 |
| closed | 5 |
| triage | 0 |
| in-progress | 0 |
| blocked | 0 |

**Issues carrying an assignee: 0, across the entire corpus.**

`conduct issue` exposes `file, ack, where, list, show, comment, close`. There is
no verb that sets a status other than through `close`, and none that sets an
assignee. `skills/issue-tracking/SKILL.md` — the document every campaign agent
reads before touching the tracker — documents filing, searching, commenting,
closing and acknowledging. It never mentions `in-progress`, `triage`, `blocked`,
or `assignee`.

So three of the eight statuses and one column are enum members with a designed
purpose, a stated rationale, and no writer reachable from the path agents
actually use. This is the shape `AGENTS.md` names: *an enum member nothing
writes*, and *a field an agent sets that nothing reads or redeems* in its
inverse form — here the field is readable and nothing sets it.

## Why it is costing something now rather than being tidy-up

Three AI tools are working this repository and this tracker concurrently. The
operator's direction, 2026-08-19: check whether an issue has already been filed
and whether a fix is in progress, and **mark an issue in progress when you start
on it so another agent does not implement the same thing**.

That instruction is not executable from `conduct`. Two agents can each search
the tracker, each find the same P1 open with no signal on it, and each open a
worktree. The collision is only discovered at rebase or at PR time, and the
loser's work is discarded. The tracker was designed to prevent exactly this and
the design was never wired to the callers.

A comment is not a substitute. `conduct issue list --open` renders key, severity,
status and title; it does not render comments. A claim recorded as a comment is
invisible in precisely the view an agent uses to pick its next task.

## It is not that no writer exists — it is one CLI over and undocumented

`cao issue edit <key> --status in-progress --assignee <who> --actor <who>` works
today; this filing's own six sibling issues were claimed with it minutes ago. So
the capability is present and the audit trail records the actor correctly.

That makes this smaller than it first looks, and it also makes it worse: the
gap is not missing machinery but a campaign-facing verb and one paragraph of
skill text, and its absence has left a designed coordination mechanism unused
for the entire life of the tracker.

## Fix

1. Give `conduct issue` a verb that sets status and assignee — `claim` as the
   ergonomic front door for the common case (set `in-progress`, set assignee,
   record actor), or a general `edit`/`status` passthrough if that fits the CLI
   better.
2. Document the claim protocol in `skills/issue-tracking/SKILL.md`: claim before
   opening a worktree, release the claim if you abandon the work, and check the
   status before starting. A claim nothing releases is a new stale-record
   problem, so the release path ships in the same change.
3. Decide `triage` and `blocked` deliberately. If nothing will write them, delete
   them per `AGENTS.md`; if they earn a place, name the writer. Do not leave a
   third and fourth unwritten member behind after wiring the second.

## Acceptance

Not "a flag was added". An agent following `skills/issue-tracking/SKILL.md` end
to end, using only `conduct`, must be able to claim an issue, be seen to have
claimed it in the default list view, and release the claim — and a test must fail
if any leg of that is missing.
issues.resolution: Triage 2026-08-21 vs vision + main 13bcdcc: Verified already-fixed on conductor main. Fix commit/proof cited in triage comment (see prior comment_id). Live file inspection (git log -S, grep) confirms defect absent. Vision: check now correctly scoped/closed; smallest check shipped. No further action. If re-observed, reopen with current file:line.
issues.title: the tracker's in-progress, triage and blocked statuses and its assignee column have no writer reachable from conduct, so concurrent agents cannot see each other's claims

issues.body:
The Mac mini tracker UI cutover exposed a stale and overbroad bounce refusal. The route registry contained historical GLM gateway entries, but none of their terminal IDs mapped to an active CAO or tmux pane. All four live sessions had durable session_env rows in the CAO database and the deployed fork already persisted them across restart. Even so, the bounce guard treated any route entry as proof of live session-env loss.

The supported accept-session-env-loss departure was used only after checking active panes, durable database rows and the DND session environment fingerprint. The fingerprint remained fd6b99ced99cc8103196418a140afbbac20b3bf019a0bedc6d3a0694548f7286 after both bounces, so no environment was lost. This is a guard-scope defect rather than a recovery failure.

cond-0349 delivered session-env durability and explicitly anticipated deleting this guard. The repair should either remove the obsolete refusal or scope it to a currently active gateway-dependent worker whose environment is not durably persisted. The refusal must report what it actually observed.
issues.expected_outcome: The guard admits the bounce when every active session environment is durable, or refuses only the specific active worker whose required environment would actually be lost.

1. On the Mac mini, retain a historical GLM entry in the project routes.json after its terminal and tmux pane are gone.
2. Confirm live sessions have durable session_env database rows and the session-env.json fingerprint matches the canonical environment map.
3. Run a pinned conduct deploy dry run with bounce enabled and without accept-session-env-loss.
4. Observe the deployment refusal even though no active worker depends on the historical route.

issues.body:
Worker identity collapses role, harness, AI provider, model, and effort into one name, across 58 profiles and ~55 routing task classes. Those axes bind at different times and cost different amounts to change, so one name cannot describe any of them honestly.

**Outcome.** A worker is identified as `role@harness`. Harness and AI provider are separate first-class axes. Model and effort are launch flags a supervisor is encouraged to change for quota, surfaced as live metadata rather than inferred from a name. Every transition is classified into one of four tiers, and the supervisor has a documented contingency for each, including the break-glass cases.

**Why it matters.** A `supervisor-sol-high` stepped down to Luna/xhigh still reports as `supervisor-sol-high` everywhere, so the UI displays a claim nothing established. Model capability is written as profile prose that becomes false the moment model is a flag. Conductor policy forces a heavy ceremony on a transition measured to be nearly free.

**Success criteria.**
1. Identity is `role@harness`; the AI provider appears beside it in every surface showing identity.
2. Model and effort are launch flags with per-harness defaults; the UI shows observed values where parseable and an explicit unverified label where not, and always shows the provider.
3. The four tiers exist as computed classifications, never asserted ones.
4. A supervisor can always rescue a track of work: quota exhaustion, crash, unresponsive worker, or unrecoverable history.
5. No profile or task-class name is renamed; old names resolve for one cycle.

**Out of scope.** The CAO waiting feature (sibling project). Mid-round quiescence.

**Design.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-cond0402-role-at-provider-identity.md` on branch `design/cond0402-role-at-provider-identity`.
issues.title: Worker identity: role@harness, transition tiers, and fault-tolerant handoff

issues.body:
An agent that must wait on an external condition has no way to say so. It burns tokens polling, or ends its turn and goes blind for hours, or sits in a state indistinguishable from stuck.

**Outcome.** Any agent, supervisor or worker, registers a condition with CAO, enters a traceable waiting state, and is woken with the result delivered into its context.

**Three conditions.**
1. Timer: wake me in N minutes, named or described, cancellable when the awaited thing arrives early.
2. Continuous integration: watch this run and deliver the result. The most common wait in the system; every worker should be able to use it, not only the supervisor.
3. Script: an arbitrary executable plus a timeout up to roughly 12 hours; CAO runs it and wakes the requester with its result and metadata.

**Success criteria.**
1. A waiting agent occupies a dedicated state that is neither idle nor stuck, traceable to the exact registered condition.
2. The wake delivers the result plus metadata naming what was awaited.
3. A timer can be cancelled.
4. The deadman does not treat a registered waiter as a stall.

**Why separate from the identity project.** Two independent consumers already exist: the handoff contingencies in that project, and the fire marshal work.
issues.resolution: All four waiting stories merged and true-closed across fork and conductor; timers, process/CI monitors, traceable wait state, cancellation/Stop, result attachment, exact-owner wake, and deadman behavior are live.
issues.title: CAO waiting: register a condition, sleep, and be woken with the result

issues.body:
# Profiles and task classes collapse role, provider, model, and effort into one name

`profiles/` holds **58 files** and `conduct/lib/routing.py` holds ~55 task classes.
Both namespaces encode the same four axes in a single identifier —
`supervisor-sol-high`, `implement-opus-medium`, `fix-deepseek-max` — and the axes
have very different binding times.

## The three axes and where each is actually bound

| Axis | Bound at | Cost to change |
|---|---|---|
| **Role** — skills, allowedTools, MCP servers, system prompt | profile | it *is* the identity |
| **Provider/route** — harness plus who serves the model | **launch**; `shims.register_route()` keys a route by worktree realpath and mints a **one-shot** gateway token consumed at exec | **full handoff** — fence authority, durable checkpoint, newly attested generation |
| **Model + effort** | **runtime**, through the harness's own controls | reversible in-place session operation, no human gate |

`skills/harness-route-switching` states the boundary directly: "This skill is for a
same-provider, in-place route change. Changing provider is not a model-picker
operation: use `provider-handoff`."

## Why the collapse is a defect and not just clutter

**1. The stored route and the live session disagree.** `register_route` records
`route`, `model`, *and* `effort`. A supervisor that switches model in place —
which the system actively encourages, to manage quota — changes the live session
but not the registered route or the profile name. A worker launched as
`supervisor-sol-high` and stepped down to Luna/xhigh still reports as
`supervisor-sol-high` everywhere. The CAO frontend therefore displays a claim
nothing established.

**2. Model capability is written as profile prose.** `profiles/supervisor-deepseek.md`
says "DeepSeek V4 is text/code only. Never perform or claim screenshot
inspection." That is true only because the model is welded to the profile. It is
a **model** property, not a provider property, so the moment model becomes a
launch flag the prose becomes a falsehood waiting to happen.

**3. The combinatorics are role x provider x model x effort.** Every new model or
effort rung multiplies both namespaces, and each new file re-states the role's
skills, tools, and MCP wiring — which are provider-independent.

## Direction (operator-confirmed)

Identity becomes **`role@provider`**, because the provider boundary is exactly
where a change stops being a session operation and becomes a handoff. Model and
effort become **launch flags with per-provider defaults**, and are surfaced in the
CAO UI as **live metadata read from the session** rather than inferred from a name.

## Scope of this item

Design specification only — no code changes. It covers **both** namespaces
(profiles and task classes) and includes a design for observing and recording
live model/effort changes so the frontend can display them. Implementation is
deliberately separate.

issues.actual_outcome: The command writes to whatever installation the local binary reaches. Both installations expose project cao-system and mint colliding cond-NNNN keys, and no response names which one accepted the write. A 26-issue planning tree was created on the wrong machine with no indication.
issues.body:
`conduct` resolves a tracker project by name and then writes to whatever CAO installation the local
binary happens to reach. Two installations both expose a project called `cao-system`, both mint keys
in the same `cond-NNNN` sequence, and neither the command nor its output names which installation was
written to. The result is that a full planning tree — two project roots, 26 issues, 31 relationships —
was created on the wrong machine, and nothing in any response indicated it.

The failure is silent in both directions. Nothing warns at write time, and nothing distinguishes the
installations afterwards: `cond-0404` exists on both, with unrelated content.

    MacBook  cond-0404 = "Worker identity: role@harness, transition tiers, and fault-tolerant handoff"
    Mac mini cond-0404 = "M4: make session project/work-root binding a creation invariant"

An agent that reads a key from a document, a commit message, or another agent's report cannot tell
which installation that key belongs to. Key collision plus an identical project name means a
cross-referenced key silently resolves to unrelated work.

## What would have prevented it

A tracker command should establish and report the identity of the installation it is about to write
to, and refuse a write when the caller's expectation and the resolved installation disagree. The
identity needs to be something stable and observable — an installation id minted at first
initialization, reported by `conduct issue where`, and accepted as an explicit expectation flag on
mutating commands, in the same spirit as `--expect-head` on `conduct deploy` and
`--expect-updated-at` on `conduct issue edit`.

Reporting alone is a large improvement over the current state: every filing response naming its
installation would have surfaced this on the first write rather than after 26.
issues.expected_outcome: A tracker command identifies the installation it resolved, reports it in every response, and refuses a write when an explicitly stated expectation does not match the resolved installation.

2. On the Mac mini, run the same command:
     ssh colin@<mac-mini> '~/.local/bin/conduct issue show --id cond-0404'
   Observe a different, unrelated issue: "M4: make session project/work-root binding a creation
   invariant".

3. On either machine run:
     conduct issue where
   Observe that it reports project_id "cao-system" on both, with no field identifying which
   installation answered.

4. On either machine, file an issue with --tracker-project cao-system. Observe that the response
   carries ok, issue_id, location "project cao-system", reporter, and store — and no field naming
   the installation, host, or database that accepted the write.

issues.body:
A tier-3 transition (3a execution-transition, 3b harness-handoff) parks a source and primes a
successor. Today the departing worker authors two artifacts and nothing binds them:

- the round report, which the park already requires, redaction-scans, and hashes
  (conduct/commands/_retained.py:313 scan_round_report, called at checkpoint.py:672); and
- the handoff packet in skills/provider-handoff/SKILL.md, which no code in conduct/ reads.

The report is the stronger artifact and the design has been ignoring it: absolute path required,
symlink refused, non-regular/empty refused, surviving raw secret refused, SHA-256 of the exact
bytes returned. That is durable, redaction-clean, tamper-evident and content-addressed, produced
at exactly the moment a handoff needs one.

Method adopted from the /handoff skill
(~/.claude/skills/_matt-pocock-skills__skills__productivity__handoff/SKILL.md): one document
written for a reader and aimed at a named next job; a suggested-skills section; reference
artifacts rather than duplicating them; redact. The last two are already CAO's rules. The first
two are not, and at a harness boundary suggested-skills is a correctness requirement rather than
a courtesy.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-cond0402-role-at-provider-identity.md section 4.9,
branch design/cond0402-role-at-provider-identity. Verification is P14 in section 11.

Done when: a tier-3b transition produces one authored document; the park's digest, the packet's
report.sha256 and the target's read_report_sha256 are three independently produced values that
are equal; suggested_skills has a reader that refuses an unresolvable skill; and a replacement
reviewer cannot see the prior verdict before its own pass is durable.

Out of scope: changing what the park itself validates, and any new redaction machinery.
issues.title: Handoff document: one authored artifact for the park gate and the successor

issues.body:
Unify the round report and the handoff packet's prose, and bind them by digest.

The departing worker authors one document. The park consumes it as the round report; the
successor consumes it as its priming context. The packet keeps every field it has today and
gains:

  report:
    path: absolute-path
    sha256: exact-digest   # the value scan_round_report returned at the park

The target's acknowledgement gains read_report_sha256. Acceptance compares digests. Today it
compares fields the target restates in its own words (provider-handoff SKILL.md step 2), which
cannot distinguish a target that read the document from one that read the packet and paraphrased
it.

Ordering is not negotiable: author -> park -> fence -> launch -> acknowledge -> continue. The
document must be complete and clean before the fence because the park validates it.
find_appended_report_prefix (conduct/commands/_retained.py:377) does allow the file to grow after
a park with the parked bytes remaining a prefix; tier 3 must refuse that affordance, because
appended bytes are bytes the park never hashed.

Done when: the three digests agree on a disposable tier-3b pair; a report mutated between park
and acknowledgement is refused; and a report appended to after the park is refused for tier 3.

issues.body:
Add suggested_skills and skill_root to the handoff packet, and ship the reader with them.

Naming skills is a courtesy within one harness. At a harness boundary it is a correctness
requirement, for two reasons that only appear once harness is the identity boundary:

- A harness change is a skill-root change. Skills are how a CAO worker knows how to behave, and
  each harness resolves them from its own root. A successor on a different harness does not
  inherit the predecessor's loaded set.
- Skill roots drift silently. The cao-session skill records the observed failure: worker
  worktrees have been seen symlinking their skills into an older checkout, so a running worker
  reads superseded guidance while every head looks correct.

So the packet names the skills AND the root that resolved them, and the successor's
acknowledgement reports the root it actually resolved. A mismatch means the two generations are
following different guidance for the same task.

This field must not repeat the mistake D15 names: the packet's existing reason: enum has no
reader anywhere in conduct/. suggested_skills ships with its reader or does not ship.

Done when: a packet whose suggested_skills names a skill the target's skill_root does not resolve
refuses before the prepared continuation is released, and the refusal names the skill and both
roots.

issues.body:
Seal the prior review verdict so a replacement reviewer stays independent.

provider-handoff requires that a replacement reviewer read the source, brief and exact head
independently, and that the previous verdict not be revealed "until that independent pass is
durable" (skills/provider-handoff/SKILL.md). A departing reviewer's round report contains its
verdict.

So "hand the successor the round report as its priming context" and "do not reveal the previous
verdict" contradict each other for exactly one role, and it is the role where independence is the
whole product.

Resolve it inside the document rather than by exception:

  sealed:
    - section: prior-review-verdict
      unseal_when: successor's independent pass is durable at <artifact>

A sealed section is present in the document and covered by the digest, but the prepared
continuation cites only the unsealed sections. The successor unseals by writing its own durable
pass first. Copying the document minus the verdict is not an option: it breaks the digest binding
and leaves the two generations reading different bytes.

Done when: for a reviewer source, the prepared continuation provably excludes every sealed
section while the digest still covers it, and the unseal requires the successor's own durable
pass.

issues.body:
Codex is CAO's only harness with exactly one AI provider. Two working headless launchers change
that: ~/Projects/custom-skills/deepseek-codex-headless (built and working) and a Z.ai Codex
launcher in progress against https://docs.z.ai/devpack/tool/codex.

Both create tier-2 provider-relaunch pairs on a SECOND harness: openai -> deepseek and
openai -> zai, same Codex harness, session preserved. Today every measured tier-2 pair is on
claude_code, so tier 2 rests on one harness's behaviour.

Why the pairs are credible. deepseek-codex-headless states the mechanism: the launcher passes
--ignore-user-config and exact per-run provider overrides but "still uses the normal CODEX_HOME
session store, which is what makes a cross-provider resume possible". The thread store is keyed
by CODEX_HOME, not by provider, so the thread id survives the provider change - the same shape as
the measured claude_code result.

One operational trap the skill already documents and CAO must not inherit: "Codex groups visible
history by login method, so use the captured session id". After a provider cutover the thread
still resumes by explicit id but is NOT discoverable in the picker. CAO holds the id in its
native_session row so CAO is fine; a human recovering by hand is not. This belongs in the skill
text, not only in a launcher's help.

What CAO is missing, read from conduct/lib/routing.py:

- No codex gateway shim. shims/ holds claude (provider gateway routing), kimi (version-aware MCP)

composed launch recipes. Adding hand-written profiles now grows that migration surface. Add these
as harness-record x provider in the shape the composer will consume, so they migrate for free
rather than becoming two more files to convert.

issues.body:
Add a codex gateway shim and the codex@deepseek route.

Port the proven behaviour of ~/Projects/custom-skills/deepseek-codex-headless/scripts into a
shims/codex wrapper built to the same fail-closed contract as shims/claude:

- route map keyed by realpath(cwd), read from routes.json;
- routes.json missing -> legitimate pre-spawn state, exec the real codex untouched;
- routes.json present but unreadable, unparseable, misshaped, or naming an unknown route ->
  hard fail, never exec untouched (that would be silent provider substitution onto ambient auth);
- route "openai" -> exec untouched, native auth, no env mutation;
- route "deepseek" -> scrub ambient OpenAI credentials, atomically claim the mode-0600 one-shot
  token file, inject the DeepSeek key, apply the per-run provider override, remap the model slots,
  write the consumed marker, then exec.

The key must not appear in arguments or run artifacts; the launcher already meets this bar by
passing it through DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, and must not regress when ported.

Then add "deepseek" to the codex side of the gateway route set so with_model_override
(conduct/lib/routing.py) stops refusing the route, and add the codex@deepseek harness record in
the shape cond-0529's composer will consume.

Done when: a CAO-launched codex worker on the deepseek route reports the DeepSeek model in its
own status; a corrupt routes.json refuses rather than launching on OpenAI; and the key is absent
from the process argv and every run artifact.

issues.body:
derive_quota_provider asserts codex -> openai and will preflight the wrong pool.

conduct/lib/routing.py:560:

    def derive_quota_provider(provider: str, shim_route: Optional[str]) -> str:
        if provider == "codex":
            return "openai"
        ...
        if provider == "claude_code":
            if shim_route == "glm":
                return "zai"
            if shim_route == "deepseek":
                return "deepseek"
            return "claude"

claude_code already treats harness and AI provider as separate axes by branching on shim_route.
codex asserts a single provider and ignores the shim_route argument it is handed.

Unreachable today, because no codex route has a non-openai provider. It becomes reachable and
silent the moment either codex provider route exists: CAO would check OpenAI capacity while
spending DeepSeek credits or the Z.ai coding-plan pool. A preflight that reports green against a
pool the run does not touch is worse than no preflight, because it is trusted.

The fix is the pattern already present three lines below, not new design.

Filed P3 rather than the story's P4 because it is a correctness defect in a safety preflight and
must land with or before the first codex provider route, not after it.

Done when: derive_quota_provider returns deepseek and zai for the respective codex shim routes and
openai otherwise; a route whose shim_route is unknown to the function refuses rather than
defaulting to openai; and a test asserts the quota pool a codex provider route actually debits.

issues.body:
Prove the two Codex tier-2 pairs and document them in the transition skills.

Once codex@deepseek and codex@zai exist, run the tier-2 evidence for each pair rather than
inheriting the claude_code result. Same harness does not by itself mean the thread survives; that
is a per-pair fact.

Use the runtime resume-adoption proof from cond-0399 (fork PR colindmurray/cli-agent-orchestrator#145)
rather than a version table: a fresh app-server process performing thread/resume and asserting the
returned thread id equals the expected native id, with no turn/* traffic. The Codex bootstrap
contract already describes exactly this sequence (services/codex_native_bootstrap.py). A version
allowlist would have to be re-derived per provider and would exclude every future build by
default; a runtime proof answers the question for the session actually in hand.

Include the negative control the spec requires of every tier-2 pair: a relaunch that changes
nothing about the provider must be refused as an ordinary respawn rather than borrowing tier-2
relaxations.

Then document in the transition skills:

- openai -> deepseek and openai -> zai are tier-2 provider-relaunch on the codex harness: session
  id preserved, new generation, no summarization, no handoff packet;
- the picker-visibility trap: after a provider cutover the Codex thread resumes by explicit id but
  is not discoverable in the history picker, which groups by login method. Capture the session id
  BEFORE the cutover. CAO holds it in native_session; a human recovering by hand does not;
- codex@zai shares one quota failure domain with claude_code@glm, so it is not a fallback when
  that pool is constrained.

Done when: both pairs have a recorded runtime proof naming provider, harness build, model, effort
and execution mode; both negative controls refuse; and the skills state the pairs, the capture-the-id
rule, and the shared Z.ai pool.

issues.actual_outcome: Profile-only race says an assigned route was bound and a continuation cannot proceed; harness race prescribes a cross-provider handoff. Neither is true before initial spawn seals or launches a generation, although provider_io remains false.
issues.body:
Root-deferred residual from cond-0533 after the final 3/3 review cycle.

compare_assigned_routes is used by retained post-seal comparisons and by initial spawn's pre-seal two-read check. Initial spawn resolves the compatibility route near spawn entry, later captures a strict policy snapshot, then calls compare_assigned_routes(later_snapshot_route, earlier_compatibility_route). Generic field and harness refusals still describe those operands as assigned/current or as a continuation/handoff, although neither pre-seal observation is durable authority.

Cooperative sequence A is profile-only under the same claude_code/deepseek/deepseek harness/billing/transport route; sequence B changes the harness. Both fail before provider I/O. The defect is false causal and recovery guidance: a good-faith supervisor can abandon a lawful spawn, create unnecessary generation/handoff ceremony, or chase an assigned record that does not exist. This is not a hostile-local-caller concern.

Base/head evidence
- Base 46dd1fbf43f232d448948e8a3e715f2d36cc84d7 profile-only output is exactly unchanged at reviewed head c4d97b12ca2feb71efde4996b1489d518b907dfb: route-transition-required on profile with the assigned/current/continued text and provider_io false.
- Base harness output already prescribes authorized cross-provider handoff/never continuation. c4d97b1 improves operand terminology but retains the pre-existing handoff prescription; it does not create or worsen the race.
- The opening sealed-route docstring exists on base and head.
- cond-0533's new quota/shim diagnostics are caller-neutral and are not the source of this residual.

Acceptance
- Every compare_assigned_routes diagnostic and its docstring is truthful for retained post-seal and initial-spawn pre-seal call orientations.
- Generic field and harness drift during an initial-spawn two-read race name both observations without asserting sealed/assigned/current authority.
- Pre-seal recovery says stabilize the campaign route/profile declaration and retry the refused original operation; no continuation, new dispatch, or handoff is required where no generation exists.
- Retained guidance stays actionable without weakening refusals.
- Tests construct profile-only and harness-only changes between the two production reads, assert provider_io false/zero reservations, stabilize policy, and prove retry clears.
- Operand-order or assigned/sealed/continuation mutations make a test fail.
- Diagnostics only: no admission flag, relaunch mechanism, or authorization path.

Provenance: independent Sol final review of c4d97b1, no P0/P1; root explicitly deferred this P2 after cond-0533 cycle 3/3.
issues.expected_outcome: The refusal states that two pre-seal policy resolutions disagree, names both observations without assigning authority, advises stabilizing campaign route/profile policy and retrying the original refused spawn, and performs no provider I/O.
issues.reproduction_steps:
1. On base 46dd1fb or head c4d97b1, resolve implement-deepseek for initial spawn's compatibility read.
2. Before strict snapshot capture, add routing_overrides mapping implement-deepseek to fixer-deepseek. The harness, quota_provider, and shim_route remain claude_code/deepseek/deepseek; only profile changes.
3. Call the production strict snapshot seam, which compares the later snapshot first against the earlier compatibility route second.
4. Observe route-transition-required describing the second operand as current, the first as assigned/bound, and saying drift is never continued / dispatch on the new route.
5. Repeat with an override that changes harness. Observe provider-handoff-required even though no generation exists and stable-policy retry is sufficient.
6. Confirm both refusals project provider_io false and no reservation/provider launch occurred.
issues.resolution: Verified caller-neutral route diagnostics and exact-operation retry behavior merged in PR colindmurray/cao-conductor#238 at 070aec57cdb0a8afc63b00b04cc4b6ab3ecbd606; reviewed head 16f7289dba840f2c3ea0df708b38cecacfb61109 has the identical tree, final independent review found no P0-P4, and detached merged-main focused smoke passed 111 tests.

issues.body:
## Outcome

CAO — not a provider turn state, not a report artifact, not a dashboard label — becomes the durable semantic authority for what each managed agent was asked to do and whether it actually finished. Every managed agent (supervisors and long-lived service roles included) holds a durable, versioned, identity-bound task occurrence. Completion is an evidence-backed decision by an authorized decider. Intentional quiet becomes a typed, bounded, explained coverage record that suppresses only the obligations it names. Suspension and resume never lose, re-do, or silently redispatch work, and only the operator restarts a stopped campaign. Every typed communication and its attachments are captured by value into the one conductor-owned per-project SQLite store and stay safely readable after the source run directory is pruned.

Authority: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-task-goal-completion-hold-lifecycle-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-task-goal-lifecycle-implementation-plan.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-task-goal-fire-marshal-parallel-plan.md`. Execution history: `/Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor-worktrees/TASK-GOAL-LIFECYCLE-EXECUTION-LEDGER.json`.

## Success criteria

The design's §15 acceptance matrix is the definition of done. The load-bearing rows:

- A provider turn that finishes without a report leaves the task open; a refused or ambiguous required report makes satisfaction refuse.
- An optional-report spec closeout lets a supervisor satisfy from merge and reconciliation evidence while the writer is dormant.
- A planned PR checkpoint records exact evidence, alerts the operator, pauses or stops safely, suppresses recovery, and resumes only through the supervisor.
- One covered task plus one uncovered stalled task still permits recovery for the uncovered obligation; wait-owner death or watcher heartbeat loss creates an unsuppressible recovery obligation.
- A re-requested human gate cannot consume a prior approval; subscriptions are consume-once.
- `conduct whoami` from a registered live worker pane resolves its exact stable agent/incarnation/task; an unregistered, dead, superseded, or ambiguous pane gets a typed non-identity result, and caller-supplied `TMUX_PANE`/`CAO_TERMINAL_ID`/`--terminal` cannot redirect the implicit caller.
- `Resume paused` sends zero goal/task input; `Resume and start` wakes only the supervisor before task selection; a completion-claimed occurrence routes to its decider and is never auto-reactivated.
- Legacy migration never infers satisfaction from provider `completed`, report intent, parked history, pause/stop, or a missing pane.
- File-backed and message-only communications and their attachments remain independently viewable after their source run directory is pruned; a final report in the catalog changes no task outcome; active or malformed Markdown executes and fetches nothing.

## In scope

PR 0, 0A, 0B, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and the PR 9 family (9A, 9A.1, 9B, 9C, 9D) as defined in the implementation plan; every defect this campaign's flexibility audit (2026-08-17) and composition audit (2026-08-17) FILED as tracker records — the ten flexibility ids cond-0445..cond-0454 and the seven composition ids cond-0471..cond-0477, all adopted into this tree; the supervisor diagnostic and recovery capability set; and the campaign infrastructure needed to trust its own verification and see its own concurrent claims.

## Out of scope

- **Provider-native goal integration.** Plan §1: "No provider-native goal integration is part of this plan."
- **A second stable-agent roster, task-occurrence id, safe-drain receipt, or resume authority.** cond-0380 owns the first conductor task-occurrence and supervisor reconciliation seam; this project supplies it requirements and does not race its schema.
- **Stopped-session automatic resume.** See the PR 6 decision record in this tree; it is a deliberate omission, not unstarted work.
- **The fire-marshal M3/M7 physical-identity chain (cond-0573) and the worker-identity / CAO-waiting projects (cond-0527, cond-0528).** This project consumes their contracts and is gated by them; it does not own them. cond-0517 and cond-0518 are the M3 activation chain this campaign measured and partly delivered, but they are `part-of` cond-0573 and stay there.
- **Lane-tree schema decisions**, which belong to the separate 2026-08-02 lane-tree and supervisor-enablement draft.

## Constraints and risks

- **Delivery rules (plan §1):** every PR has one failure domain and an independently reversible activation; every effect journal persists intent before I/O and query-adopts after response loss; role defaults compile into a concrete occurrence contract and policy changes never retroactively rewrite an active occurrence; Stop is a hard lifecycle boundary that terminates session-owned monitors and wait runners.
- **Threat model (AGENTS.md):** cooperative local agents and a single operator. Identity, version, receipt, transition and destructive-scope guards prevent accidental corruption and ambiguous effects; they are not a hostile multi-tenant ACL.
- **Readiness gates already CLEARED** — recorded here as prose and deliberately NOT modelled as live blocker edges, because a cleared gate rendered as a blocker is a false deadlock: G0 design publication (cao-conductor PR #124, merge `39f4b764`); G1/FM-TG-1 stable identity (cond-0377, fork merge `3b30dcee`); G2/FM-TG-2 physical lifecycle (cond-0378, cond-0379); G3/FM-TG-3 task-occurrence seam (cond-0380, fork PR #116, merge `9f38c3d3`, verified equals-fork-origin-main); G5/FM-TG-5 M7 foundation (M7 Stage 1 `e42ef387` / #139 and Stage 2 `c52e6703` / #119, both confirmed ancestors with MARSHAL_TRIGGER_C/D off).
- **Readiness gates still LIVE**, each modelled as exactly one blocker edge or named in the blocked slice's own body: G4/FM-TG-4 (cond-0382, M3-F installed acceptance) gates PR 5; G6/FM-TG-6 (cond-0574, M7 stages 4–5) gates PR 4; G7 lane-tree resolution gates PR 7 and has no tracker record to hang an edge on; canonical session→project association gates PR 9D and likewise has no tracker record.
- **Verification risk.** This project currently has no green local full-suite baseline; the coordinator's full-suite differential failed twice for environmental reasons. Three lane branches (`lane/cond0510-0514-collect-retained`, `lane/cond0508-workstate-blocked`, `lane/cond0515-gc-workspaces`) are rebased cleanly onto current `origin/main` (9b6987b) with zero textual conflicts, but cond-0549 (PR #214) rewrote the retained-track teardown underneath them, so a clean rebase is not proof of behavioural correctness and the cond-0510 guard's suggested remedy sequence is now stale.

## Verification

Each PR report must state which readiness gate it proved, its exact refs, and which later PRs remain deliberately blocked. PR 0 and PR 0A: one focused adversarial review plus documentation/UI tests. PR 0B and PRs 1–5: high-risk review protocol with response-loss failure injection, state-machine mutation tests, and isolated CAO acceptance. PR 9A/9B: persistence, response-loss, confinement, corruption and GC adversarial review. PR 9C: unsafe/malformed-Markdown, accessibility, deep-link, desktop/mobile component, Playwright and installed-pair acceptance. PR 7: a separate lane-tree design review before any code review.
## Known residual — findings that exist but are not tracker records

The flexibility audit produced 17 findings and filed 10. **Seven medium and one
low finding were left in `FLEXIBILITY-AUDIT-SYNTHESIS.md` and never filed**, so
they are outside this tree and invisible to every hierarchy view. The synthesis
is at
`/Users/colin/Projects/cao-conductor-worktrees/task-goal-lifecycle-artifacts/FLEXIBILITY-AUDIT-SYNTHESIS.md`.
Anyone completing this project should adjudicate them rather than assume the
filed ten were the whole audit.

Two standing local-only test failures are recorded on the verification story
(see the trustworthy-verification story under the campaign-infrastructure epic)
rather than here.

## A note on `resolved` versus `closed` in this tree

Fourteen adopted records are `resolved`, not `closed`. That is deliberate and it
is not bookkeeping laziness. In this tracker `resolved` means a fix landed and
`closed` means somebody verified it; converting them in bulk would assert a
verification nobody performed, which is the exact falsehood this project's
doctrine exists to prevent. The cost is known and accepted: `conduct issue
frontier` counts `resolved` as actionable, so this tree's frontier over-reports
until each is verified individually and closed on its own evidence.

---

## Alignment with the operator vision

`docs/cao-operator-vision.md` is authoritative over this project's design choices
and over every issue in this tree. Where this body and that document disagree,
that document wins.

### The governing principle, applied here

> Mechanism encodes what is always true, and policy encodes what is usually right.
> Guardrails prevent a good-faith transition into an illegal or corrupt state; they
> never prevent a capable, well-intentioned supervisor from keeping a campaign
> moving through a reasonable, non-corrupting situation — **when the two conflict,
> the guard yields, not the flow.**

Every guard this project ships or repairs is priced by the vision's test: *what
concrete bad transition does this guard prevent, and what is the cost of refusing
the legitimate sequence it also blocks?* Classify with Q0 (exclusivity and
exactly-once), then Q1 (write the literal command that undoes the admitted
transition), then Q2 (is the refusal caused by absence of an input rather than its
content — a capability gap is Tier 3: record, file, continue).

A guard that cannot name the single transition it prevents is deleted rather than
softened.

### This project is a catalog of the vision's half-built shapes

Vision §3 lists six shapes that are "half-built on sight, decidable from schema and
call sites". **Every one of them has a concrete instance in this tree.** That is
the organizing lens for the residual-defect stories, and the fastest way for a new
reader to understand what this project is actually repairing:

| Vision shape | Instance in this tree |
|---|---|
| a verb refusing for every possible input | `cond-0454` — `conduct resume` is hardcoded to refuse; `cond-0491` asks wire-or-delete |
| an enum member nothing writes | `cond-0508` — the `blocked` workstate chip; `cond-0445` — `cancelled` reserved in the task-outcome enum with no writer |
| a state with no outbound edge | `cond-0484` — a quota-exhausted retained round had no exit for any actor |
| a field, deadline, or anchor an agent sets that nothing reads or redeems | `cond-0451` — the live-wait coverage anchor has no producer; `cond-0476` — a hold's `release_id` naming a gate is read by nothing; `cond-0477` — `task_occurrence_id` NULL in every shipped write |
| a read gated on a frozen field the write path resolves live | `cond-0507` — `communication list` filtered on the raw `--project` while the state dir used the resolved one |
| a second live holder of a uniquely resolved role, minted with no succession link | `cond-0453` — `conduct revive` mints a second live supervisor with no successor link |

Two further vision rules govern how these are repaired, and both have been
violated inside this campaign and corrected:

- **"Does your fix for an absorbing state have an absorbing state? Ask it every
  time, and treat a no as something you proved rather than intended."** The
  `cond-0484` repair shipped this defect three times, one level down each round.
- **"Absent and unreadable are different answers."** `cond-0514` is that rule at
  one remove: a helper collapsing the two manufactures the defect in every caller
  that tries to be honest.

### Two gaps this alignment pass exposed, recorded rather than quietly fixed

**1. The adopted issues in this tree are UNVETTED.** Vision anti-pattern #10 is
explicit: *"Treating an open issue as proof it is still real."* The backlog is
largely AI-filed and unvetted, and **61% of a P0/P1 sweep were already dead** —
ALREADY-FIXED or OBSOLETE against current `main` or against the two in-flight
projects. This tree adopted 44 existing records on the strength of their bodies and
their relevance, **not** on a verdict that each is still a real defect in current
`main` (`9b6987b`).

Before implementing any adopted issue: read the code as it exists, `git log -S` the
symbol, check for a later fix, check obsolescence against the fire-marshal and
worker-identity projects, and reach a verdict of REAL / ALREADY-FIXED / OBSOLETE /
MISUNDERSTOOD / CANNOT-DETERMINE. Close what is dead with a resolution saying how
the conclusion was reached. **Never conclude "still real" merely because the issue
is open, or because this tree adopted it.** Adoption is a statement about scope,
not about liveness.

**2. `conduct resume` is reserved to the operator, not to PR 5.** Vision §7
Unsettled lists it by name: *"Whether `conduct resume` ships or is deleted. The
backlog verdict names it an always-refusing verb today and candidates it for
deletion or for being fed live facts rather than literals. No operator direction
settles which."* `cond-0491` therefore carries an ordering edge from PR 5
(`cond-0603`) because PR 5 defines whether a resume verb has any legal role — but
the wire-or-delete call itself is Colin's, and no agent supplies it.
issues.title: Task and goal lifecycle: CAO owns the assignment and whether it finished

issues.body:
## Outcome

No surface lets a reader infer task, report, or campaign finality from a provider turn state, and every lifecycle view shows independent typed fields instead of one dominant human-looking label.

Design §1: "The dashboard collapses too much of this into a human-looking 'Completed' label. That label is not durable proof that the agent's assignment, lane, or campaign succeeded." Design §13 requires the projection to show independent dimensions — task outcome, report state, coverage, monitor health, lifecycle state — rather than collapsing them.

## Success criteria

Dashboard and API clients cannot infer task finality from provider turn state; a waiting, blocked, or held agent renders as such with its typed reason, evidence, duration, release condition and resume path; a proven-dead or retained terminal is never counted as a running agent.

## Boundary

Owns the vocabulary of the human-facing surfaces and the projection that feeds them. Does not own the semantic state itself (that is the durable-assignment and coverage outcomes), and does not own the fork's provider enum wire values where changing them would create needless compatibility risk.

## Verification

Existing provider-status tests pass unchanged; a rendered projection over the fixture corpus distinguishes turn-finished from task-satisfied and shows a reachable blocked/waiting state.
issues.title: Words mean one thing, and every surface shows what actually finished

issues.body:
## Outcome

Every managed agent — supervisors and long-lived service roles included — has exactly one current task occurrence or an explicit no-assignment state, stored durably in the one per-project conductor semantic database, referencing cond-0380's exact task occurrence and stable `agent_id`. The occurrence survives turns, compaction, Pause/Stop/Resume, exact reincarnation, fresh fallback, handoff and route changes. Completion is a versioned, evidence-backed decision by an authorized decider, never a report artifact and never a label.

Design requirements 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10 and 11.

## Success criteria

- Finalized history and new assignments stay distinct; a retained agent can finish one assignment, go dormant, and later receive a new one without overwriting the old task or native conversation.
- Paused and stopped context is readable without a pane; a command invoked inside a registered live worker pane resolves that worker, and the same command from an unregistered pane cannot claim one.
- Report delivery and satisfaction are independently queryable; required evidence cannot be waived silently; self, manager and external decision cases are policy-expressible.
- Every mutation carries `goal_version`; a stale request refuses and returns the current capsule; satisfaction racing reactivation has exactly one CAS winner.
- Garbage collection cannot delete the authority; legacy migration never infers satisfaction from provider `completed`.

## Boundary

Owns the conductor-side goal/occurrence store, the read-only context surface, and the mutation/acceptance state machine. Does not own the fork's stable roster or occurrence minting (cond-0377 / cond-0380, both merged) and does not create a second occurrence id.

## Verification

State-machine mutation tests plus response-loss failure injection over the acceptance-matrix fixtures; isolated CAO acceptance for the identity resolution path.
issues.title: Every managed agent has a durable, versioned, identity-bound assignment CAO owns

issues.body:
## Outcome

Planned review boundaries, access grants, API enablement, CI runs, scheduled time and human approval stop being indistinguishable from a stalled fleet. They become first-class typed coverage records — holds and exact-live-owner waits — carrying enough evidence to explain exactly why the fleet is quiet, bounded by deadline or renewal, and scoped so they suppress only the obligations they name. Human decisions become a trustworthy release mechanism backed by a request/decision/delivery journal rather than marker files.

Design §7 (obligation coverage), §8 (human gate correction), requirements 7 and 8.

## Success criteria

- One covered occurrence never hides an uncovered stalled obligation; invalid or expired waits create recovery obligations no broader hold can suppress.
- Watcher heartbeat loss renders monitor-stale and raises a monitoring incident rather than claiming the condition is still watched.
- An agent-created working hold without gate-alert, healthy subscription or bounded renewal cannot suppress recovery indefinitely; indefinite explanatory holds work only under paused/stopped lifecycle.
- Approval is bound to request id/digest, purpose and scope; a re-requested gate cannot consume a prior approval; approval persistence plus failed delivery is visible and retryable without duplicating the decision.
- The coverage validator is versioned and its fixture corpus deterministic.

## Boundary

Owns the conductor hold/coverage substrate, the gate journal, and the sentinel parity of the validator. Reuses M7's exact-live-owner wait schema and explicitly does not reserve a stopped-session system owner that survives pane or campaign teardown.

## Verification

Deterministic versioned fixture corpus evaluated identically by conductor and sentinel; response-loss injection on the gate journal; scoping tests that pair one covered occurrence with one uncovered stalled obligation.
issues.title: Intentional quiet is explained, bounded, and suppresses only the obligation it names

issues.body:
## Outcome

A campaign can be paused, stopped, revived, reincarnated or handed off without losing an assignment, re-running finished work, or delivering task bytes to a stale generation. Only the operator restarts a stopped campaign. A worker whose round cannot end has a real, honest exit that does not require fabricating its report.

Design §9 (Pause/Stop/Resume), §5 (orthogonal state), §7.5 (Stop as a hard boundary), requirement 6.

## Success criteria

- `Resume paused` sends zero task or goal input; `Resume and start` wakes only the supervisor before worker selection.
- Old generations and stale goal versions cannot receive task effects; a completion-claimed occurrence routes to its decider and is never automatically reactivated.
- Force interruption preserves report requirements and side-effect warnings; Stop records interrupted wait and adapter ids and no external condition can restart the campaign.
- Exact and fresh continuity remain truthful; fresh fallback with an incomplete seed stays non-runnable until reconciled.
- Every retained round has at least one supported exit for some actor that does not require inventing the worker's output.

## Boundary

Owns conductor-side reconciliation, capsule delivery, and the retained-track exit surfaces (collect, park, retire, revive, resume). The physical reincarnation and cohort Pause/Stop/Resume contracts are fork-owned (cond-0378, cond-0379, cond-0382) and are consumed, not reimplemented.

## Verification

Isolated CAO acceptance across exact and fresh cells; state-machine mutation tests on the retained-track transitions; explicit assertions that a stopped session performs no later observation, delivery, or physical resume.
issues.title: Suspension and resume never lose, re-do, or silently redispatch work

issues.body:
## Outcome

Every typed CAO communication carries exactly one text body plus zero or more named text/Markdown attachments, snapshotted by value into the unified per-project SQLite store in the same durable transaction as the communication and delivery intent. The paper trail survives pruning of the sender's run directory, is reachable by opaque id through a bounded reader, and renders inertly against hostile content.

Design §13.1, requirement 12, owner decisions 5, 6 and 11. Plan §3 PR 9: "Deliver this final product chunk as four separately reviewable PRs."

## Success criteria

- An inline assignment, an intermediate checkpoint, a file-backed final report and a message-only final report are all independently viewable and linkable; an ordinary non-task message with attachments follows the same path.
- Captured content survives source-file and run-directory removal; a response-loss retry creates no duplicate communication occurrence.
- A final report's display changes no task outcome.
- Missing, corrupt, oversized or partial content is visibly incomplete; script, raw-HTML, URL and remote-image attacks execute and fetch nothing.
- A deployment without a conductor catalog preserves today's dashboard behaviour.

## Boundary

Owns capture, the operator-safe projection, the bounded fork read API, the conductor attachment reader, and the viewer. Explicitly does not add task semantics to the fork API and does not ship a generic path-reading endpoint or an orphan file-path viewer.

## Verification

Persistence, response-loss, confinement, corruption and GC adversarial review for capture and API; unsafe/malformed-Markdown, accessibility, deep-link, desktop/mobile component, Playwright and installed-pair acceptance for the viewer.
issues.title: Everything an agent said is durably captured by value and safely readable

issues.body:
## Outcome

Agents and operators are taught the shipped semantics, and supervisors gain the diagnostic and recovery tooling a capable manager needs: find a worker's session history, judge whether it is on task or stuck, terminate and report on its behalf, and clean up — under one narrow guard (a supervisor may act only on workers it spawned).

Design §14: "Skills teach judgement. Commands and validators enforce identity, authority, state, and suppression."

## Success criteria

- Assignment-awareness, task-completion and hold-and-wait skills exist and teach `conduct whoami`, goal and context reads, attachment reads, managed hold proposals, self-managed authority limits, Stop interruption and explicit wait re-registration after resume.
- Supervisor and worker role guidance is updated to match shipped commands.
- Skill text stays subordinate to deterministic command enforcement — no skill grants an authority a command does not check.
- A supervisor can locate any spawned worker's transcript by session id and harness, and can end a worker that cannot end itself without fabricating its report or stranding its leases.

## Boundary

Owns the policy and skill surfaces plus the supervisor capability set. Does not own the tracker or dashboard mechanisms those skills teach about.

## Verification

Each shipped skill names the exact command that enforces what it teaches; the supervisor recovery path is exercised end to end against a real halted worker, with lease, seat, gateway and manifest release asserted rather than assumed.

## This epic's frontier under-reports

cond-0486 is adopted whole as one record, but it decomposes into three pieces. Piece 2 (terminate-and-report-on-behalf) merged as conductor PR #197 and was subsequently repaired externally by cond-0549. Piece 1 (the standalone session-log discovery skill) is implemented on branch feat/session-log-discovery in the custom-skills repository and is not yet installed. **Piece 3, the broader read-only diagnostic toolkit, is unclaimed and unstarted.** A reader counting open children of this epic will not see it.

The request/decision/delivery journal PR 0B shipped becomes a mechanism an operator can actually run: an approval binds to the intent it authorized, a gate can be re-announced on its current occurrence, delivery buckets can be drained, and an unreadable store never renders as "no gates".

Seven defects in one mechanism, found by the flexibility audit (2026-08-17) and the composition audit (2026-08-17) plus two later follow-ups on the repairs themselves:

- Plain gate consumption is not intent-bound, so a crashed gated spawn burns the human approval.
- `conduct approve` resolves the supervisor terminal before recording the human decision, and binds the decision to the live occurrence rather than the observed one.
- There is no way to re-announce a gate on its current occurrence.
- `conduct status` reports `gates: (none)` when the gate store is unreadable — a silent empty state where the truth is unknown.
- `gate_journal.undelivered` spans superseded occurrences and can never clear; the two delivery buckets PR #180 introduced have no operator verb that drains them, and `settle_delivery` is reachable from no command.

## Success criteria

A re-requested gate cannot consume a prior approval; a crashed gated spawn does not burn one; an operator can settle a delivery row after reading its target by exact `delivery_id`; an unreadable store reports unknown, never none.

The gate journal and its operator verbs. Does not reintroduce marker-file authority and does not change the hold or coverage model.

Response-loss injection on the delivery path; a test that consumes an approval against a different intent and must refuse; a test asserting the unreadable-store path emits a typed unknown.

## Outcome

Coverage goes live. The exact coverage validator is vendored into the sentinel through M7's parity mechanism; a general long-running command/process wait adapter plus first-class CI and scheduled-time adapters register on the same exact-live-owner contract; monitored / monitor-stale / unmonitored state is exposed; and bounded reconsideration rounds (eight hours by default) wake the live owner to renew, revise or terminate a wait rather than silently extending it forever.

## Success criteria

- Conductor and sentinel produce identical verdicts over the fixture corpus.
- Watcher death is visible and cannot continue claiming monitoring.
- Stop cancels or kills every session-owned adapter and monitor, records `interrupted-by-stop`, and prevents later condition effects.
- After an operator resumes, the worker explicitly reruns or re-registers any still-relevant interrupted wait.

Gate G6 / checkpoint FM-TG-6: "sentinel validator parity, exact wait acknowledgement/suppression/expiry, and public registration are installed and verified at the required stages; exact incarnation/cohort barriers outrank delivery; rollback can drain acknowledged waits." Identical-verdict differential between conductor and sentinel over the versioned fixture corpus; a Stop test asserting no later observation, delivery or physical resume; a consume-once subscription test.

## THIS IS A DECISION RECORD, NOT A TASK. THERE IS NOTHING TO IMPLEMENT.

It is filed closed and kept in the tree on purpose. Plan §3 states it verbatim:

> ### PR 6 — intentionally omitted: stopped-session automatic resume
>
> There is no condition-triggered physical-resume PR. Stop terminates monitors, invalidates their delivery authority, and requires an explicit operator resume. This numbered tombstone is deliberate so an older copy of the plan cannot be mistaken for authorization to reintroduce autonomous restart.

Plan §5 reinforces it: "There is no PR 6 implementation; any proposal for stopped-session autonomous resume is a new product decision, not an extension of this plan."

## Why the slot must stay occupied

A tree that simply skips 6 loses the guarantee. A future reader scanning PR 0 → 5, 7, 8, 9 sees a gap and reads it as unimplemented scope. The whole purpose of the numbered tombstone is to occupy the slot so that reading cannot happen. It is filed `closed` rather than left out for exactly that reason.

## The supporting record

- Owner decision 9 (design §16): "A stopped session runs no wait monitor and can resume only by explicit operator action."
- Design §7.5: "Stop is a hard execution boundary: it cancels/kills the session's live wait runners, marks their rounds `interrupted-by-stop`, and performs no further observation or delivery. A condition becoming true after Stop has no CAO effect and can never restart the campaign."
- Design §17 records that a prior review proposed a stopped-session system monitor and that "The subsequent owner decisions above intentionally supersede its recommended stopped-session system monitor and two-database split."
- Parallel plan §3.4 pushes the same prohibition into the fire-marshal track: do not reserve or implement a system-owned wait that survives pane teardown or Stop.

## If someone wants this

It is a new product decision requiring the operator, not an extension of this plan. Do not reopen this record to do it; file a new one that says what changed.
