## Outcome

No retained round can reach a state where no actor has a supported exit, and no ordinary command can silently strand one. Collect, park, retire and report-on-behalf each refuse honestly rather than exiting zero on the wrong state, and a park never admits an unproven native session identity.

## What is in here and why it is one story

Five defects on one state machine — the retained track — found by this campaign:

- A quota-exhausted retained round had no exit for any actor, and the only one that existed required fabricating the worker's report. This is the canonical absorbing state and AGENTS.md's own worked example.
- Ordinary `conduct collect` on an active retained track exits 0, tears down the worker, and strands the record permanently — while `collect --retained` refuses on `active`, making collect unusable in both forms.
- `accepted_callback_report_for_round` returns None for both "there is nothing" and "I could not look", so a corrupt reconciliation file reads as no-report and can trip a forced contingency against a worker that did report. The most generalizable finding of the campaign.
- The ACP park relaxation let a native retained round with no session binding park instead of refusing, turning main red during PR 3's CI gate; the corrective lane scoped it to a declared bridged mode and proved by test that it did not regress the earlier ACP park fix.
- `checkpoint --park` stopped refusing a run whose native session identity is unproven, returning exit 0 and parking the track where it previously refused with zero mutation.

## Success criteria

Every retained round has at least one supported exit for some actor; no exit requires inventing the worker's output; a command that cannot proceed refuses with a typed reason and a correct safe next action, mutating nothing.

## Live risk the coordinator must handle before merging

cond-0549 (PR #214, merge `3aa8961`) rewrote `report_on_behalf.py` so the command now CAS-transitions a retained track active → collecting → collected and releases the lease itself. The cond-0510 guard's `safe_next_action` still suggests report-on-behalf, then `checkpoint --park`, then `collect --retained` — a sequence that is now wrong: after report-on-behalf the track is already collected, the suggested park hits the new `_refresh_park_journal` refusal, and the following collect has nothing to finalize. The remedy text must name report-on-behalf as a terminal clearing verb in its own right. The three lane branches rebased cleanly onto `9b6987b` but a clean rebase is textual only.

## Verification

A test per exit verb asserting the refusal path mutates nothing and names a next action that actually works against current main; a differential run of `tests/test_report_on_behalf.py` after any change to `_retained.py`.

- Every skill names the deterministic command that enforces what it teaches; no skill grants an authority a command does not check. Design §14: "Skills teach judgement. Commands and validators enforce identity, authority, state, and suppression."
- Role defaults compile into a concrete occurrence contract, and a later policy change does not retroactively rewrite an active occurrence.

## Boundary

Split deliberately from PR 8's dashboard half (see the PR 8b story under the legibility outcome): one plan slice spanning two outcomes gets two independently reversible activations, which plan §1 requires. Gated per-surface — "the semantic surfaces each view teaches" — so it is actionable now for what PRs 0B/1/2/3/9A already shipped, and the lane-lifecycle skill waits on PR 7.

## Verification

A documentation test asserting each skill's claimed enforcement point exists as a real command check.

## Outcome

A green or red local result means something. Test fixtures perform the effects they certify, standing exemptions have tracker records rather than folklore, and any production defect hiding behind an environmental failure is separated out and fixed.

## What is in here and why it is one story

Two defects in the campaign's own verification trust:

- The standing `test_gc_workspaces` exemption had no tracker record and was misattributed twice — first to a fork baseline-stability issue, then to a load-flaky fire-marshal cleanup test. Filing it properly then exposed a real production defect in `gc.py`'s lsof handling behind the environmental part, which is why its severity was raised.
- `FakeCao` answered `DELETE` with 200 without removing the terminal, so every teardown assertion written against it certified nothing.

## Why misattribution is the theme, not an accident

Both items are cases of a signal being trusted without being measured. The campaign's own correction record is the evidence: baseline classification must run before attribution, and a guard needs a test asserting it FAILS on each case it claims to catch.

## Known adjacent record NOT adopted here

The fork's local full-suite baseline instability is tracked separately under the `cli-agent-orchestrator test stability` component. It is genuinely relevant — it is why this project has no green local full-suite baseline — but it belongs to the fork's test surface, not to this project's scope, so it is attached as a `relates` edge rather than adopted.

## Verification

Each exemption names the exact test id, the SHAs it was reproduced at, and the CI run that passed the same SHA; each fixture repair is proved by an assertion that fails against the old fixture.

## Outcome

Every one of the 44 pre-existing records adopted into the task/goal lifecycle tree (cond-0588) carries a recorded liveness verdict against current `main`, so an implementer can pull from the frontier without first re-deriving whether the defect still exists.

## Why this is real work and not bookkeeping

`docs/cao-operator-vision.md` anti-pattern 10 is explicit:

> **Treating an open issue as proof it is still real.** Opened an implementation PR against a tracker issue because the issue was open and the quoted file still existed. The tracker holds ~145 AI-filed, largely unvetted issues. **61% of a P0/P1 sweep were already dead** - ALREADY-FIXED or OBSOLETE against current `main` or against the fire-marshal / goal-lifecycle projects.

The tree adopted those 44 records on the strength of their bodies and their relevance to this project's scope. That is a statement about SCOPE, not about LIVENESS. No adoption verdict established that any of them is still a real defect at `9b6987b`.

The risk is concrete and asymmetric. An implementer who trusts adoption as liveness spends a full lane on a defect that another project already fixed, and the wasted lane is only discovered at rebase or review. At the sweep's observed rate that is a majority of the adopted set.

## What to do

For each adopted record, in the order the frontier surfaces them rather than all at once:

1. Read the code as it exists now at the cited path, not as the issue describes it.
2. `git log -S <symbol>` for the symbol the issue names, to find a later fix.
3. Check obsolescence against the two in-flight sibling projects - fire-marshal (cond-0573) and worker identity / CAO waiting (cond-0527, cond-0528) - since both touch adjacent records and either may have resolved it in passing.
4. Reach one verdict: REAL / ALREADY-FIXED / OBSOLETE / MISUNDERSTOOD / CANNOT-DETERMINE.
5. Record it as a comment on the issue. Close what is dead with a resolution stating how the conclusion was reached.

Never conclude "still real" merely because the issue is open, or because this tree adopted it.

## Scope boundary

This covers the 44 adopted records only. The 27 planning nodes created with the tree (cond-0588..cond-0614) describe intended work rather than observed defects and need no liveness verdict.

## Success criteria

Every adopted record carries a dated verdict comment naming the evidence that produced it, and every record whose verdict is ALREADY-FIXED or OBSOLETE is closed with that resolution. The count of adopted records with no verdict reaches zero.

## Verification

`conduct issue list --tracker-project cao-system --kind all --label task-goal-lifecycle` cross-referenced against the tree's adopt list; each adopted id has a verdict comment. A spot check of three ALREADY-FIXED closures reproduces the cited fix at the named sha.

issues.body:
`main` is red and every open PR inherits the failure, so no lane in any of the three concurrently-executing projects can merge on a green check.

## Measured

| ref | CI | |
|---|---|---|
| `9b6987b` (main, PR #218 merge) | **failure** | run 32423838504 |
| `6d0b9e0` (main, PR #217 merge) | **failure** | |
| `55d16d9` (main) | success | last green |

Four failures, identical on `main` and on every branch cut from it:

```
FAIL: test_installed_wheel_admits_a_complete_nonlegacy_extension
      (tests.test_profile_identity.ProfileWheelTest)
FAIL: test_installed_wheel_composes_without_checkout_imports
      (tests.test_profile_identity.ProfileWheelTest)
FAIL: test_wheel_contains_one_complete_registry_and_role_catalogue
      (tests.test_profile_identity.ProfileWheelTest)
FAIL: test_listing_no_sources_is_an_empty_answer_not_a_refusal
      (tests.test_wait_command.ListTest)
FAILED: tests.test_profile_identity, tests.test_wait_command
```

Candidate commits, all between the last green and now:

```
d45a342 fix: pin profile identity composition contracts        (#218)
cbf059a fix: enforce canonical profile registry boundaries     (#217)
46e19ac feat(wait): add managed timer lifecycle                (#217)
38d4abf feat: compose profiles from role and harness registries
```

## The part that makes this worse than an ordinary red main

**Both modules PASS locally on a clean checkout of the same sha.**

```
$ git worktree add --detach <dir> 9b6987b && cd <dir>
$ python3 -m unittest tests.test_wait_command       ->  Ran 25 tests   OK
$ python3 -m unittest tests.test_profile_identity   ->  Ran 27 tests   OK
```

So local verification cannot catch this. Three of the failing tests are named
`test_installed_wheel_*` and `test_wheel_contains_*`, which suggests they assert
against a **built and installed wheel** that CI produces and a checkout run does
not — in which case the local pass is vacuous rather than contradictory, and the
tests are silently not exercising their subject locally.

This is the same class as `cond-0515`, where a test failed locally and passed in
CI because the environments differ in a way nobody had named. The direction is
reversed here, and the consequence is worse: a divergence that fails CI and passes
locally means every contributor's pre-push check reports green on broken code.

## Impact

Blocks `cao-conductor` PRs #219, #220 and #221 (task/goal lifecycle), and any other
open lane, from merging on a green check. It does not block the *work* — those
three branches are verified against this base by full-suite differential — only the
merge gate.

## Expected

`main` is green, and a full-suite run on a checkout exercises the same subjects CI
does, or says explicitly that it is skipping them.

## Actual

`main` is red on four tests that a local full-suite run reports as passing.

## Ownership

The candidate commits are all worker-identity project work (`cond-0527` subtree,
PRs #217 and #218). Filed by the task/goal lifecycle coordinator because it blocks
that project's merges; the fix belongs with whoever owns the profile registry and
managed timer work.

## Note on the two questions this raises separately

1. Which of the four commits broke it, and what the fix is.
2. Why a checkout run reports OK. If the wheel tests silently no-op without a built
   wheel, that is its own defect and worth its own record — a test that passes by
   not running is the fixture-versus-expectation failure in a different costume.

The accepted role@provider design S1/D12 requires removing `derive_shim_route` profile-name inference. cond-0569 migrated the route projection, `apply_override`, and `_run_attest` to declared provider-registry identity, but exact reviewed head `f67251c9f488ba0b453d3784e84ed08d4782670c` proves two pre-existing live callers remain in `conduct/commands/up.py` (around lines 387 and 401).

Plausible cooperative failure sequence: an operator selects a `claude_code` supervisor profile whose name does not contain `deepseek` or `glm`, but whose declared binding/provider requires a gateway. `up.py` calls `derive_shim_route`, falls back to `anthropic`, and therefore does not register the required gateway route. The worker can launch on ambient Anthropic credentials and preflight/bill the wrong pool. This is silent route-evidence corruption; a green receipt describes a pool the process does not debit.

Lawful flow to preserve: `conduct up` must still admit registered ambient-Anthropic supervisors and must register the declared gateway transport for registered DeepSeek/Z.ai supervisors without relying on filename tokens. Missing provider declaration and unreadable/invalid registry data are distinct; an unreadable registry must not be treated as an ambient provider. An unregistered external supervisor profile must have a documented current clearing path or a proportionate typed refusal rather than a hard-coded provider default.

Done when:

1. `up.py` resolves supervisor AI provider and `shim_route` from the accepted registries, or refuses before launching when it cannot establish them; no call path reaches substring profile-name derivation.
2. `derive_shim_route` is deleted when its last caller is migrated.
3. Tests prove a misleading profile name cannot select ambient Anthropic, a lawful ambient profile remains green, gateway profiles register the declared transport, and absent versus unreadable/invalid registry observations remain distinct.
4. Reverting/bypassing the declared lookup makes the production `up.py` wiring test red.

Scope is the conductor S1/D12 supervisor startup surface. It is related to Lane A parent cond-0529 but is not part of cond-0540's model/effort launch-flag acceptance, and it does not add Lane G provider rows/shims/credentials or touch Lane B/C/D/F ownership.

issues.body:
*Surface:* `conduct/commands/report_on_behalf.py:1189`.

The spawn-ownership guard compares terminal ids by raw equality and never walks the succession chain:

```python
if caller_id != supervisor_id:
    raise ConductorError(
        "result-handoff-validation",
        f"worker terminal {worker_id!r} was not spawned by this supervisor: "
        f"caller_id={caller_id!r} != supervisor_id={supervisor_id!r}; refused",
```

## Why this fails closed on a case this campaign made ordinary

`conduct revive` mints a **linked successor supervisor with a new terminal id** — that is what `cond-0453` (resolved, this project) shipped, and `cond-0501` extended it so a gate answer routes to the successor rather than the retired predecessor.

After a legitimate revive, every worker the predecessor spawned carries `caller_id = <predecessor terminal>`, which is no longer the live supervisor's id. So `report-on-behalf` refuses for **every** worker the succeeded supervisor inherited — precisely the recovery case the capability exists to serve.

**The succession link is readable and is already read elsewhere.** `conduct/commands/_common.py:587` resolves `successor_terminal_id` from the retirement record, and `_retired_with_live_successor` uses it to route a gate answer correctly. `report_on_behalf.py` does not import it: `grep -n "successor" conduct/commands/report_on_behalf.py` returns nothing.

## The exit it names is a human

The module's own guard table names **"conduct retire by OPERATOR"** as the exit for R1, R2 and R3, and records R2 as *"Reachable even for legitimately spawned workers (known projection identity-loss defect)"*.

So the refusal's releasing verb is the operator. `docs/cao-operator-vision.md` §5: *"No agent adds a new human approval gate on its own initiative"* and *"Escalate last. Reduce effort, switch lanes, quarantine, attest, park. Waking Colin comes after all of those."* §3 lists as half-built on sight: *a second live holder of a uniquely resolved role, minted with no succession link, after which every resolving command fails closed.* Here the succession link exists — the guard just does not consult it, which is the same defect one step further along.

## The acceptance criterion would pin the defect into the suite

`cond-0486` states the rule as an absolute — *"A supervisor cannot collect, or report on behalf of, a worker it did not spawn"* — and `cond-0594` repeats it verbatim. An implementer writing the test that criterion demands locks in both refusals, after which the correct behaviour becomes a test failure.

That is why this is filed separately rather than as a comment: the criterion needs amending before anyone implements against it.

## Fix

Resolve spawn ownership through the succession chain rather than by identity equality: the caller is authorized when it **is** the spawning terminal, or is a live successor of it via the recorded `successor_terminal_id` links. Reuse the existing resolution in `_common.py` rather than writing a second one.

Amend `cond-0486`'s and `cond-0594`'s acceptance criterion to state the rule as *spawn ownership, resolved through succession* — the guard's purpose is that a supervisor does not tear down a worker it has no relationship to, and a succeeded supervisor plainly has one.

Keep the refusal for a genuinely unrelated caller. This narrows the guard to the transition it actually prevents rather than deleting it.

## Note on the absent-caller_id branch

`:1179` refuses separately when `caller_id` is absent. That is a refusal on the *absence of an input*, which vision §2 Q2 classifies as a capability gap — Tier 3, *record it, file it, continue* — rather than a safety property. Worth deciding deliberately in the same change: if the projection cannot supply `caller_id`, refusing every on-behalf report is a heavy price for a missing observation.

## Outcome

CAO provides fast, explained, project-scoped lexical and local semantic issue retrieval; agents can check related/duplicate candidates before filing; cao-system can ground triage in both repositories and committed documentation; and reusable guidance makes the issue/code/document workflows adoptable by other projects.

## Success criteria

- Existing issue list substring behavior remains compatible.
- Ranked FTS5 search, structured tracker-project/subtree filters, exact technical matching, local semantic retrieval, and dashboard navigation are usable.
- Similar-issue checking is available before filing but never gates writes or assigns relationships automatically.
- observed_revision and reversible important comments ship on all normal surfaces.
- The optional cao-system QMD/codebase-memory overlay works across cao-conductor and cli-agent-orchestrator with exact revision provenance and rg/Git fallbacks.
- Independent generic QMD, codebase-memory, repository-evidence, and CAO code-grounded triage skills ship with tested degradation.
- Every shipped skill/AGENTS workflow traces to a lightweight real-repository journey spike and an explicit generic, composed, project-specific, or reject/defer disposition.
- cao-conductor and cli-agent-orchestrator AGENTS guidance plus a logical project manifest state tracker scope, two-repository routing, worktree freshness, trust classes, and fallback.
- The 128-bug high-scrutiny audit completes with cited important comments and independently judged native tracker changes.
- Retrieval and code-grounding evaluation gates, recovery paths, and mutation tests pass.

## In scope

M0 evaluation baselines; M1 generic lexical search; M2 local semantic search and filing support; M3 optional cao-system code/document intelligence; M4 the bug audit; M5 workflow discovery, reusable skills, CAO repository guidance, and the project-onboarding template.

## Out of scope

Automatic relationship or duplicate verdicts; hosted embeddings; ANN/search services at current scale; permanent audit-only schema; indexing every CAO worktree; mandatory bundling of QMD/codebase-memory with CAO; shipping raw research inside skills; downstream Aegix or Quest Scheduler rollout; and multi-repository worker ownership, which receives a separate design/project.

## Constraints and risks

Local trusted single-operator deployment; SQLite remains tracker authority; derived indexes are disposable; model work never runs in authoritative write transactions; optional tools never block work; generic tool skills remain independent from CAO; project AGENTS files contain tested local routing rather than copied tool manuals; cross-repository implementation uses companion lanes until separately redesigned.

## Verification

Use the relevance fixture and historical bug fixture, migration/concurrency/mutation tests, workflow-evidence matrices, representative real-repository experiments, skill trigger and degradation forward tests, manifest/local-binding validation, exact revision receipts, and the final 128-bug audit coverage report.

## Outcome

One CAO run can own one primary workspace and one companion workspace per additional Git repository, with complete assignment, publication, handoff, continuation, collection, retirement, recovery, and GC semantics.

## Success criteria

- The terminal keeps one primary cwd while conductor records the complete workspace bundle.
- Every writable repository has its own repository-qualified branch lease, artifact seat, branch, PR, validation, and disposition.
- Scalar one-repository runs remain compatible.
- Checkpoint, continuation, whole-bundle successor transfer and cancellation, collect, retire, status, and GC cover every member.

- The scalar-surface inventory, transition prototype, and two-repository agent journey revise or validate the design before implementation issues are filed.

## Current frontier

cond-0674 inventories every scalar custody and repository-keyed migration surface. cond-0675 prototypes the proposed deep module and injects failure after every partial member effect. They are independent parallel frontier spikes.

Both block cond-0676, which pilots the real two-repository worker journey with each repository as primary. cond-0676 blocks cond-0660 design acceptance. No implementation slice should be filed or claimed until the spike evidence has been applied to the design and cond-0660 is accepted.

## Relationships

cond-0674 relates directly to the stale-lease and shared-git-dir defects because the migration must compose with their fixes. cond-0675 relates to worker identity and task or goal lifecycle because whole-bundle succession and terminal-state recovery share those contracts. cond-0676 relates to the CAO-specific developer-guidance and code-intelligence work but does not depend on optional QMD or codebase-memory availability.

The project remains separate from hybrid issue search. It enables a single audit or implementation worker to reason over both CAO repositories, while issue search and derived code indexes remain independent projections.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Produce the exact call-site and persisted-key matrix needed to migrate CAO from one scalar worker workspace to a repository-qualified workspace bundle without leaving a scalar reader, writer, cleanup path, or compatibility lookup behind.

## Questions

- Which current fields and call sites are custody authority, which are compatibility inputs, and which are observability only?
- Which paths assume one worktree, branch, lease, artifact seat, checkpoint, successor record, publication result, or GC root?
- Which branch-keyed files or lookups collide when two repositories use the same branch name?
- Does any current read-only workflow need a read member in bundle custody, or are explicit pinned evidence roots sufficient?
- What must schema-1 normalization and one-cycle compatibility reads preserve?

## Method

Keep this a lightweight source spike. Trace spawn, manifest, state and leases, artifact authority, task delivery, checkpoints and continuation, successor, collect and retire, status and workstate, publication caches, callbacks, operator commands, issue projections, and GC. Use rg, focused Git history, and narrow tests or probes. Do not change production behavior.

Exercise two repositories with the same branch basename so repository qualification is tested rather than inferred. Classify every discovered surface as authoritative custody, derived projection, compatibility adapter, or unrelated scalar state.

## Deliverable

A revision-stamped matrix of field or key, writer, readers, current identity, required bundle identity, migration behavior, negative test, and owning implementation slice. Include a recommendation to retain or remove read members from V1 based on observed workflows.

## Verification

A reviewer can start from each manifest, lease, branch-keyed, checkpoint, successor, collection, and GC field in the draft and find every live call site in the matrix. A same-branch-name two-repository fixture identifies every collision. Deliberately omitting the second repository from each load-bearing path makes the proposed test fail.

## Non-goals

No production schema, migration, lease, or lifecycle changes. No heavyweight research flow.
issues.title: S0 — Inventory scalar workspace custody and repository-keyed migration surface

issues.body:
## Outcome

Prove or revise the proposed workspace-bundle interface and durable phase model before production commands depend on it.

## Questions

- Can plan, acquire, bind, transfer, discharge, and project remain one deep conductor-owned seam?
- Does every phase reachable with one, two, or three members have a writer, a legal next verb, and an actor that can take it?
- Can deterministic acquisition, reverse rollback, whole-bundle successor transfer, cancellation, and release resume after every partial effect?
- Does schema 1 normalize to a one-member bundle without changing custody meaning?
- Which state or verb in the draft is unnecessary or incomplete?

## Method

Build a throwaway pure or in-memory prototype with fake lease, authority, reservation, publication, and journal adapters. Inject failure after every member claim, generation bind, transfer, restore, checkpoint, discharge, and release boundary for bundle sizes one through three. Explore the reachable transition graph and assert recovery to a truthful stable or terminal state. Do not wire production commands or persistence.

## Deliverable

The executable prototype and a compact transition report: stable phases, partial-effect records, legal next verbs, responsible actor, idempotency key, rollback order, and any required design changes. Reject the proposed interface if the prototype needs command-specific custody logic outside the module.

## Verification

Mutation checks fail when the second member is skipped, order is nondeterministic, rollback is forward instead of reverse, a partial transfer can finalize, an inconclusive record is treated as absent, or a phase has no exit. The report accounts for every reachable injected-failure state.

## Non-goals

No production feature, schema migration, provider launch change, or external Git or tracker effect. No claim that a mock proves real Git publication behavior.
